findings.title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached or held by the keyboard
findings.impact: With 6 or more switch targets (7+ projects, or 6+ other storages — `SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6` at line 129, counting only labelled "Switch to" groups, e.g. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2427-2438), the crumb switcher renders a filter box that no keyboard user can use. Focus enters the menu only through `focusMenuOption`, which selects `[role="menuitem"]` nodes (menuKeyboard.ts:13); the input is not one. Arrow/Home/End never leave that set. The only tabbable node inside the open menu is that input, but the container's Tab handler closes the menu on Tab in either direction, so Shift+Tab from the first list row focuses the input and the very next commit sets `hidden` on its ancestor, dropping focus to `<body>`. A keyboard or screen-reader user with many projects therefore cannot filter the list at all and can lose focus to the top of the document just by pressing Shift+Tab; the Enter-takes-first-match branch at lines 267-272 is unreachable dead code as a result.
findings.fix: In src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx, focus the search input first when `searchable` (extend `focusMenuOption`/`focusMenuEdge` to prefer `.sync-path-menu-search` when present), and stop treating Tab inside a searchable switcher as "close": let Tab move between the input and the option list, closing only when focus actually leaves the menu root (a `focusout` check), so the field is reachable and keeps focus while typing.

findings.title: Escape discards the prepared Push review from anywhere, including inside the Logs drawer
findings.impact: `onClose` runs `setPendingPush(null)` plus three selection resets (ProjectSync.tsx:3396-3402), throwing away a backend-prepared push and every conversation/file the user ticked. The Logs drawer renders in the same workspace above the review (ProjectSync.tsx:3876) and has no Escape handler of its own, so a user who opens Logs mid-review and presses Escape expecting the drawer to close instead silently loses the whole prepared push while the drawer stays open. LogPanel only stops Escape for two cases — a non-empty search field (LogPanel.tsx:305-312) and an open type filter (LogPanel.tsx:180-192) — so Escape from the Level select, Manage logs, Close, Load older, or the drawer region itself reaches the review. The comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:873 shows the hazard is known but only partially mitigated.
findings.fix: Give the Logs drawer its own Escape handler in src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx that closes the drawer and calls `stopPropagation()` while it is open, and scope the review's listener to the review subtree (attach it to the review root element rather than `window`) so Escape only discards a review the user is actually focused in.

findings.title: Focus indicators on the thread-status badge and metric readouts fall below 3:1
findings.impact: Both classes drop the global 2px `--accent` outline (App.css:5215, 5367) and replace it with a translucent shadow. Composited against `--surface-row` with the current retheme tokens (`--accent: #2a211d` light / `#efe7d4` dark; `--surface-row: #fdf9f3` / `#14120f`) the ring measures 2.11:1 light and 2.83:1 dark for the status badge, and 2.72:1 light for the metric — all below the 3:1 WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor. These are not decorative: every session row makes 5-6 of them a tab stop (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:602, 670, 701-706) purely so their `data-tooltip` content is reachable, so a keyboard user walking a session list cannot see where they are. `tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx` measures text contrast only and does not check focus rings, so nothing catches this.
findings.fix: In src/App.css, delete the `outline: none` at lines 5215 and 5367 and drop the two `box-shadow` replacements, letting the global `--focus-ring` outline apply; or replace them with an opaque ring (e.g. `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--focus-ring)`) and re-measure both themes.

findings.title: Logs drawer resize separator is mouse-only
findings.evidence:
<div
          className="log-resizer"
          role="separator"
          aria-label="Resize log"
          aria-orientation="horizontal"
          onMouseDown={onStartResize}
          onDoubleClick={onResetHeight}
        />
findings.impact: The separator has no `tabIndex`, no `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow`, and no key handler, so a keyboard user cannot change or reset the log drawer height at all — the drawer is stuck at whatever pixel height was last set with a mouse, and on a short window that can leave only a couple of log lines visible with no way to enlarge it. The same file's sibling control in ProjectSync.tsx:3695-3709 already ships the correct contract (`tabIndex={0}`, all three value attributes, `onKeyDown={resizeSidebarWithKeyboard}`), and ProjectSidebar.tsx:664-681 ships a third, so the pattern exists and this one diverges.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx, add `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow` for the drawer height, and an `onKeyDown` that steps the height on ArrowUp/ArrowDown and resets on Home/End, mirroring `resizeSidebarWithKeyboard` in ProjectSync.tsx; switch the pointer handlers to the pointer-event set the sidebar uses.

findings.title: Every custom radiogroup ignores arrow keys and makes each radio a separate tab stop
findings.evidence:
<div className="sync-bundle-choice-list" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Available remote repos">
            {matches.map((match) => {
              …
                <button
                  key={match.bundle_id}
                  type="button"
                  role="radio"
                  aria-checked={active}
                  className={`sync-bundle-choice${active ? " active" : ""}`}
                  onClick={() => setSelectedId(match.bundle_id)}
                  disabled={busy}
                >
findings.impact: Five production radiogroups declare the role but implement none of its keyboard contract — no roving `tabIndex`, no ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right: this one, SettingsPage.tsx:391 (Theme), StorageSettings.tsx:230 (Storage type), ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905 (Repo identity), and AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228 (Resource kind). A screen reader announces "radio group, 1 of N" and switches to arrow-key mode; the arrows then do nothing, so the user is told the group works one way and it works another. Sighted keyboard users must Tab through every option — in the Bundle dialog that is one stop per remote repo found in the storage, sitting between the dialog's other controls, on a screen whose choice decides which remote repo a project binds to.
findings.fix: Replace the button groups with native `<input type="radio">` inside a `<fieldset>` (the visual treatment can stay via the existing `.sync-bundle-radio` span), or keep the buttons and add a shared roving-tabindex helper — `tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` plus an `onKeyDown` handling all four arrows, Home and End — applied to all five sites listed above.

findings.title: Three menus that close by `hidden` drop focus to <body> on Escape
findings.impact: The Catalog local-action menu focuses its first option on open (`ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}`, line 585), so focus is inside the menu when Escape arrives; closing unmounts it and focus falls to `<body>`, so the user's next Tab restarts at the top of the page instead of on the chevron they opened. The same omission exists in the app-actions menu (ProjectSync.tsx:1318-1322, whose single `role="menuitem"` at line 2784 is tabbable and reachable) and the storage agent-setup menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278-1281). SyncPathBar.tsx:410-412 and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:878-884 already do this correctly with a stored opener ref, so the pattern is established and these three diverge.
findings.fix: Hold a ref to each trigger button and call `trigger.focus()` after the close in all three Escape handlers — StorageCatalogPage.tsx:955-961, ProjectSync.tsx:1318-1322, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278-1281 — matching `closeMenu(true)` in ProjectActivityPage.tsx:163-166.

findings.impact: The split button at line 2032 advertises `aria-haspopup="menu"`, but the popup it opens has no `aria-label` (a screen reader announces an unnamed menu), no ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End handling, and no focus move on open — pressing Enter on the chevron leaves focus on the trigger with nothing announced. `menuKeyboard.ts` exists in the codebase precisely for this and is imported by only two files (SyncPathBar.tsx and StorageCatalogPage.tsx); this menu, on the R2 storage-setup path where the alternative agent launchers live, reimplements nothing at all.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx, give the menu an `aria-label` ("Agent setup routes"), import `focusMenuEdge`/`moveMenuFocus` from ../sync-review/menuKeyboard, focus the first item on open, add the arrow/Home/End `onKeyDown`, set `tabIndex={-1}` on the items, and restore focus to the chevron on Escape.

findings.title: Branch picker reimplements the shared menu keyboard helper and leaves every option a tab stop
findings.impact: This is a hand copy of `moveMenuFocus` (menuKeyboard.ts:22-35) that has already drifted from it: it handles no Tab case and its options (line 268) carry no `tabIndex={-1}`, so unlike every other menu in the app the branch menu stays open under Tab and puts one tab stop on every branch. On a repository with a few dozen branches, a keyboard user who Tabs off the branch trigger must walk the entire branch list before reaching the next control in the path bar, with the menu still open behind them.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx, replace the inline handler with `moveMenuFocus` from ../sync-review/menuKeyboard, add `tabIndex={-1}` to the `role="menuitemradio"` buttons at line 268, and close the menu on Tab the way SyncPathBar.tsx:258-261 does.

findings.title: Pull review has no Escape handler, but its own status copy tells the user Escape closes it
findings.evidence: /* Same contract as Push: no safe mid-write abort exists, so the sealed exits are named instead of leaving a cancel to hunt for. And as on Push it announces, because it appears only once `busy` flips — the one explanation for the button going dead under the reader's focus and Escape no longer closing the review. */ A running pull finishes or fails whole — it can’t be cancelled midway.
findings.impact: RestorePlanView registers no `keydown` listener anywhere (the file's only `onClose` is the selection bar's close button at line 547), and no ancestor closes the Pull review on Escape — the only Escape-closes-a-review listener in the tree is PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-423. So Escape never closed the Pull review, and the reasoning the code states for this announcement is false. The user-visible consequence is an inconsistency between the two mirrored reviews: Escape throws Push away instantly but does nothing on Pull, so a user who has learned the Push behaviour will hit Escape on Pull and get no response with no explanation.
findings.fix: Pick one contract and make both reviews keep it: either add the same scoped Escape-to-close to src/components/project-sync/RestorePlanView.tsx, or drop the window listener from PushResourceWorkspace.tsx and rely on the explicit close control in both — then correct the comment at RestorePlanView.tsx:666-671.

findings.title: Path-bar crumb menus open on Enter/Space without moving focus into the menu
findings.impact: Enter and Space on a crumb toggle fire `onClick`, which only flips `openMenu`; focus stays on the trigger while `aria-expanded` flips to true. A screen-reader user is told the menu is expanded and then hears nothing further, because no menu item has focus — they have to guess that a second key (ArrowDown) is needed. The same gap is in the non-split crumb button (line 541-548) and the overflow ⋯ button (line 616). Only the Arrow-key open path (lines 520-524) calls `focusMenuOption`.
findings.fix: In src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx, have each toggle's `onClick` call `focusMenuOption(key, "first")` whenever it transitions the menu to open, so Enter, Space, ArrowDown and a mouse click all land focus on the first item.

findings.title: The switcher's search field can never receive keyboard focus — every route to it closes the menu
findings.impact: The new filter box (rendered whenever a switcher has >=6 targets, SyncPathBar.tsx:328-337) is mouse-only. Every keyboard path to it is closed: the menu's own Tab branch (line 258) closes the menu on Tab from any menuitem, and each trigger's onKeyDown does the same before the browser can move focus into the panel (line 516 for the split crumb's chevron, line 551 for the plain crumb). Opening with ArrowDown routes through menuOptions(), whose selector is '[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]' (menuKeyboard.ts:11), so the input is skipped. A keyboard-only user with 6+ projects or storages therefore cannot filter at all — they can only arrow through the unfiltered list, which is exactly the list the feature exists to shorten. The comment at lines 265-266 documents behaviour that is unreachable without a mouse. Compounding it, the <input> is a direct child of role="menu", which admits only the menuitem/group/separator family, so screen readers reading the panel in menu mode will not surface it either.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx, when `searchable` is true focus the `.sync-path-menu-search` input as the menu's opening focus target (instead of options[0] in focusMenuOption) and let Tab move between the input and the list rather than calling onClose(false); alternatively give the input role="searchbox" inside a role="group" wrapper and add it to the roving set in menuKeyboard.ts so ArrowUp from the first target returns to it.

findings.title: Switch targets drop their path line, so same-named projects and storages render as identical rows
findings.impact: Every switch target whose detail is a path (`detailIsPath: true`) now renders with the path suppressed — it survives only in the native `title` (line 202). The project switcher feeds `label: projectLabel(candidate)` with `detail: compactProjectPath(candidate.project_root), detailIsPath: true` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2431-2433), and projectLabel is the alias or display name (model.ts:32-34), i.e. usually the folder basename. Two checkouts of the same repo — ~/work/app and ~/archive/app — therefore render as two visually identical 'app' rows with nothing to tell them apart. The same holds for local storages, whose only subtitle is the folder path (storageSubtitleIsPath returns true for kind === "local", ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:215-217), and for catalog rows keyed on configured_home (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1320-1327). Before this change the path was a visible second line on every row. A mouse user must hover each row in turn; a keyboard user arrowing the list gets nothing at all, because `title` does not surface on focus and the button's accessible name is the bare label. In a mixed local/S3 storage list the suppression is also inconsistent — S3 rows keep their 'Bucket · …' line because detailIsPath is false — so rows in one list are alternately one and two lines high.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx:191 stop suppressing the path for targets: render it as the row's second line as before (the existing `.sync-path-menu-copy > small` already ellipsises it and App.css:9095 gives it the mono face), or truncate the path from the left and keep it on the row, reserving the tooltip for the untruncated value.

findings.title: With one storage configured, 'Add storage…' collapses to an unlabeled '+' glyph and the switcher body is empty
findings.impact: Roles are assigned by group position, so the same menu item changes shape with the data. The storage editor's crumb builds its 'Switch to' group conditionally (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1708-1721) and then always appends the unlabelled `add-storage` group. With two or more storages, populated[0] is the labelled list, so `add-storage` lands in `tails` and renders as a text pill reading 'Add storage…'. With exactly one storage — the first-run state — the 'Switch to' group is absent, `populated[0]` is the `add-storage` group, and it is classified as a verb instead: renderPill(item, false) emits only `{item.icon && <Icon …/>}` with no text (line 241-242), so the menu shows the current-storage row and then a footer strip containing a single bare 32px '+' button whose words exist only in `title`/`aria-label`. The list area between them is empty. Verified by replaying the partition over the real caller shapes: one storage yields verbs:["add-storage"], lists:[], tails:[]; three storages yield verbs:[], lists:["Switch to"], tails:["add-storage"].
findings.fix: Classify roles explicitly rather than by position — e.g. add a `role?: "verbs" | "targets" | "more"` field to PathBarMenuGroup and have ProjectLinksWorkspace tag the `add-storage` group as "more" — or, in SyncPathBar.tsx:168, only treat populated[0] as verbs when a labelled group exists later in `populated`.

findings.title: A disabled footer pill's reason is no longer rendered, defeating the caller's stated intent
findings.impact: `renderPill` puts `disabledReason` in the native `title` only; `renderItem` still draws it as a visible second line (lines 190-192). Items that moved into the footer therefore lost their explanation. The workspace storage menu's 'Link storage…' is exactly that case, and its own comment says so: 'Stays put at zero candidates and says why, instead of vanishing from the DOM for a reason the user cannot see' with `disabledReason: "Everything you've added is already linked"` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2314-2322). A user who has linked every storage now sees a 50%-opacity 'Link storage…' pill (App.css:3276-3279) with no visible reason, and a keyboard user who arrows onto it gets none at all, because `title` does not fire on focus. The same applies to the catalog crumb's 'Unlink from …' verb, which carries `disabledReason: "This row is not linked to it yet"` (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239) and is rendered as a bare icon.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx, render a disabled pill's reason where the user can see it — either keep such items in the list body as `.sync-path-menu-item` rows, or add a reason line to `.sync-path-menu-foot` (the `.sync-path-menu-cap` slot at App.css:3225 already spans the footer's full width) and reference it with aria-describedby.

findings.title: The switcher panel has no max-height or scroll and is clipped by #root's overflow:hidden
findings.impact: No rule in App.css gives `.sync-path-menu` a max-height or `overflow`, and the panel's only clipping ancestor is `html, body, #root { height: 100%; width: 100%; overflow: hidden; }` (App.css:7-11) — nothing between them scrolls. The bar is 3.25rem tall (App.css:2539) and each target row is min-height 34px (App.css:3102), so on the configured minimum window height of 560px (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:25) about 11 target rows fit; on the 720px default about 16. Past that the list is cut off by the window bottom and the `.sync-path-menu-foot` strip goes with it — meaning 'Storage settings…', 'Unlink…', 'Rename project…', 'Reset local sync state…' and 'Add project…' become entirely unreachable, since they now live only in that footer. Arrow-key focus does not rescue it: focus() finds no scrollable ancestor, so the focused row stays off-screen. The change makes this reachable by design rather than by accident — SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 (SyncPathBar.tsx:129) exists precisely because lists of this size are expected.
findings.fix: Give `.sync-path-menu` a viewport-relative ceiling and let the target list scroll: `max-height: min(60vh, …)` on the panel with `overflow-y: auto` on the `.sync-path-menu-group` region, keeping `.sync-path-menu-current`, `.sync-path-menu-search` and `.sync-path-menu-foot` pinned outside the scrollport so the verbs stay reachable.

findings.title: The 'Switch to' group heading disappears in switcher mode and its replacement aria-label is inert
findings.evidence:

No match.

}
findings.impact: The switcher branch never renders `.sync-path-menu-label` (only the headerless branch does, line 363), so the visible 'Switch to' heading and the separator that used to precede it are gone. What replaces it is `aria-label` on a plain `<div>` with no role — a div maps to `generic`, which prohibits naming, so browsers drop the label and no assistive technology ever reports it. Below the search floor of 6 targets there is no search placeholder either, which is the common case, so the panel becomes: a lifted current-object row with a tick, then an unheaded run of rows, then a strip of icons — with no word anywhere saying the middle rows are alternatives to switch to. The div also has no CSS rule of its own (`.sync-path-menu-group` appears nowhere in App.css), so nothing else distinguishes the region.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx:343 give the wrapper `role="group"` so the aria-label is honoured, and render the group's label visibly (reuse `.sync-path-menu-label`, App.css:3084) at least when `searchable` is false so the list is introduced.

findings.title: Type-ahead cannot reach the footer's text pills — their computed label is the empty string
findings.impact: Tail pills render their words as a bare `<span>` outside `.sync-path-menu-copy` (line 242) and deliberately carry no aria-label (`aria-label={tail ? undefined : item.label}`, line 232), so both lookups miss and the label resolves to "". `"".startsWith(buffer)` is false for any non-empty buffer, so type-ahead skips them permanently. Before this change 'Add storage…', 'Add project…', 'Link storage…' and 'Add Catalog resource…' were ordinary `.sync-path-menu-item` rows and typing 'a' jumped straight to them; now typing 'a' in an open switcher silently passes over every one.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx:242 wrap the tail's text in `{item.label}`, or set `aria-label={item.label}` on tails as well as verbs so the second lookup in the labels map succeeds.

findings.title: The file's architecture comment now describes the opposite of what the component renders
findings.evidence:
* Each crumb's menu speaks for exactly one scope: a header block naming the
 * object the menu acts on, that object's verbs beneath it, a Switch-to list,
 * and the ways to get more. The current object is the header, not a checked
 * row — position says "this is the one you're on" — so no radio state exists
 * anywhere in the bar.
findings.impact: Both claims are now false in the same file. The verbs are no longer 'beneath' the header — they render last, inside `.sync-path-menu-foot` (lines 349-357) — and the header does carry a tick: `<Icon name="check" size={13} className="sync-path-menu-check" />` at line 325, added by this change. App.css:3161-3162 repeats the stale reading ('The object the menu acts on: context at the top, not a command'). The next maintainer reading the module docblock before the code will build against a layout that no longer exists, and the 'no radio state' invariant is the kind of claim that gets relied on when adding a new crumb menu.
findings.fix: Rewrite the docblock at SyncPathBar.tsx:16-20 to describe the shipped switcher — header row with tick, optional filter at 6+ targets, target list, footer strip of icon verbs and text tails — and update the matching comment at App.css:3161-3162.

Read every production caller that supplies a `menuHeader` (i.e. every switcher): ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx storage-editor crumb (1679-1736), workspace storage crumb (2272-2356), project crumb (2361-2450), non-Git section "Switch view" crumb (2497-2534); StorageCatalogPage.tsx storage crumb (1205-1270) and catalog-row crumb (1271-1338). Two emitted hooks have no rule: `.sync-path-menu-group` (also absent at HEAD, harmless as a block div) and `.sync-path-menu-item.target` (a behavioural hook read by the Enter handler, not a style hook). Checked all 18 custom properties used in the new CSS block — every one is defined. Confirmed via `git show HEAD:src/App.css` that the panel had no max-height before this change either, so that finding is a live defect rather than a regression.

Simulated the group-role partition (lines 166-174) in node against the five real caller shapes to confirm the single-storage misclassification and the >=6 search boundary rather than reasoning about it. Also checked and did NOT find problems in: duplicate React keys (every caller has at most one labelled group), event-listener cleanup (the document mousedown/keydown effect at 398-420 cleans up; the rAF in focusMenuOption is safe because menuRefs entries are deleted on unmount), measurement during render (none), click-outside and Escape dismissal (both work, and Escape from the search box reaches the document handler), focus return to the trigger, `query` reset on close (162-164), and label overflow (`.sync-path-menu-copy` has min-width:0 with ellipsis on both lines).

Not checked: I did not run the app or the test suite, so nothing here is confirmed against rendered pixels — in particular the vertical-clipping arithmetic in the max-height finding is computed from the CSS row heights and tauri.conf.json's minHeight, not measured in the running window. I also did not measure horizontal overflow of the fixed 380px switcher at the 800px minimum window width (`.sync-path-menu` has `left: 0` with no flip or viewport clamp, but I could not confirm the crumb offsets that would make it clip, so I left it out). Findings outside this lens — the rest of the App.css retheme, SessionDetailEvent, PushResourceWorkspace, ProjectSidebar, Icons — were not audited.

findings.title: The new capture-budget banner counts conversations the Push review filters out of every list
findings.impact: The comment's premise is false: a capture-budget row is never rendered. hold_over_budget_candidates (service.rs:6501) replaces the decision with blocked_conversation_decision, which sets `selectable: false` and action `blocked`; every list in the review filters on isPushReviewDecision (`selectable && (publish|create_cloud)`) — ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 for the session rows, :1600 for the older-entries group, and PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:437 for the fallback ResourceInventory. sessionSyncPresentation also downgrades those rows to status "unavailable", which isPushReviewStatus rejects. So the user is told "3 conversations wait for the next round" and can find no such row anywhere in the review. When every candidate is over budget the screen is worse: sessions and olderEntries are both empty, so ProjectActivityPage renders the success-toned empty state "Nothing to push — No local session changes are ready to push." (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1852) directly under a warning banner saying N conversations are waiting. Two contradictory statements, and the advice ("Push the selected conversations first") is unfollowable because nothing is selected or selectable.
findings.fix: Make the held rows visible instead of counted: admit `action === "blocked" && blocker === "capture_budget"` through the push-review filters (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 and :1600, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:437) so they render unselectable with the syncHoldDetail sentence already written for them, and suppress the "Nothing to push" empty state while capturePendingCount > 0. If they are meant to stay hidden, drop the banner's row-pointing language and say the round was truncated instead.

findings.title: The comparison-failure banner offers the destructive local-state reset for transient errors, including an offline storage
findings.evidence:
action: onResetMetadata
      ? (
        <button type="button" className="btn btn-ghost" onClick={onResetMetadata} disabled={busy}>Reset local sync state</button>
      )
      : undefined,
findings.impact: threadComparisonError is set for ANY degraded push review, not only for corrupt metadata: service.rs:7563 assigns the storage-engine open error to it (`Err(error) => { if wants_thread_comparison { thread_comparison_error = Some(error.clone()); } }`), and ProjectSync.tsx:1836 deliberately lets an `unavailable` destination open the review ("Degraded sections such as offline storage or capture failures open without a comparison"). So a network blip or an unreachable R2 bucket produces a banner whose only offered action wipes reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, Pull results and saved plans (the confirm text at ProjectSync.tsx:2679). The repo already encodes the opposite rule twenty lines below, where the push error notice gates the same button behind `isIrrecoverableSyncError(error)` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:835), whose doc says "transient and ordinary stale-plan errors keep Retry". The banner also offers no retry, so the user's only exit from a transient failure is the destructive one.
findings.fix: Gate the banner's action the same way the error notice does — `isIrrecoverableSyncError(threadComparisonError) && onResetMetadata` — and offer a plain retry (re-open the review) otherwise.

findings.title: A failed comparison is passed as `undefined`, so the review re-runs the whole comparison and can render rows that contradict the banner
findings.impact: thread_comparison and thread_comparison_error are mutually exclusive in the backend, so whenever the new banner fires the comparison prop is `undefined`, not `null`. PushResourceWorkspace forwards it as `comparisonOverride={threadComparison}` (line 765), and ProjectActivityPage treats undefined as "no override": loadWorkspace (line 2224) falls through to `load()` + `loadComparison()`, firing a second full `get_project_thread_sync_comparison` invoke — the expensive half of the page, the one the perf work measured in seconds — every time a push review opens after the comparison already failed. If that second fetch succeeds (the review path builds a push plan and captures; the standalone path runs ReviewPurpose::Observe and can succeed where the review failed), the list renders real per-row statuses reading "Not selected" with no checkboxes — because selectableConversationIds is empty — directly beneath a danger banner saying the conversations "couldn't be compared". The banner's own comment ("every session shows its fallback status and the counts read 0/0") describes a state the component never actually produces.
findings.fix: Pass `context.thread_comparison ?? null` so the override applies and the embedded activity page stops re-fetching, or explicitly pass `comparisonOverride={null}` from PushResourceWorkspace when threadComparisonError is set.

findings.title: project_files_error is never rendered: a failed inventory silently deletes the Project files step
findings.evidence:
projectContentInventory: lockedProjectContentInventory,
        projectContentScanned: lockedProjectContentInventory !== null,
        showProjectFiles: !isGitRepository || lockedProjectContentInventory !== null,
findings.impact: The same change surfaced thread_comparison_error to the UI and added a backend warning log for both errors (commands.rs:1481), but `project_files_error` — declared in the frontend contract at src/types.ts:786 — has zero readers in src/. When build_project_files_inventory fails for a Git-managed project, context.project_files is null, so lockedProjectContentInventory is null and showProjectFiles is false; syncReviewSteps then returns ["history"] alone (reviewSteps.ts:8). The Project files tab, its file rows and its Scan button all disappear with no message, and the state is indistinguishable from "this project has no stored file changes". The user pushes sessions believing there was nothing else to review; the only trace is a line in the activity log.
findings.fix: Carry project_files_error into PendingPush the way threadComparisonError now is, and either keep the Project files step visible with an error notice inside it or add a banner naming the failure — do not let a failure and an empty inventory collapse into the same silent UI.

findings.title: The new `search` icon is dead code — no production component renders it
findings.impact: `grep -rn '\"search\"' src/` returns only the IconName union member (line 59) and this render branch; every other hit is an `<input type="search">`. In particular the new SyncPathBar switcher menu — the change this glyph was presumably drawn for — renders a bare `<input type="search" className="sync-path-menu-search">` at SyncPathBar.tsx:329 with no Icon beside it. So the mark ships in every bundle and is never painted, and the menu's filter field has no glyph.
findings.fix: Either render it in the switcher menu's search field (SyncPathBar.tsx:328) or drop both the union member and the branch.

findings.title: The magnifier's handle is detached from its ring by one empty cell
findings.impact:
Rasterising the path on the 24-unit grid the file mandates gives a ring whose lowest-right cell is (13,13) and a handle whose first cell is (15,15); cell (14,14) is empty, so the two shapes do not even touch at a corner:
13 ....##......##..........
14 .....###..###...........
15 ........##.....##.......
16 ................##......
With shapeRendering="crispEdges" (Icons.tsx:85) the gap is rounded to a whole device pixel, so the first consumer of this glyph gets a circle with a floating diagonal dash next to it rather than a magnifier — most visible at the size=24 empty-state scale the file documents.
findings.fix: Add the missing cell at (14,14) (e.g. `M14 14h1v1h-1Z`, or start the handle at `M14 14h2v1`) so the handle meets the ring.

findings.title: The capture_budget hold sentence is unreachable, and is push-worded inside a mode-generic function
findings.evidence:
case "capture_budget":
        return "Not in this round — the review's 512 MB capture budget filled before this session's turn. Push the selected sessions first, then open Push review again.";
findings.impact: syncHoldDetail only runs when selectionMode is set (lines 1167 and 1384) and inside sessionSyncPresentation's label; every one of those call sites sits behind the isPushReviewDecision filter that drops capture_budget rows, and the standalone Activity comparison runs ReviewPurpose::Observe, which never mints the blocker. The copy therefore cannot appear on screen today. It is also written for one direction while the function branches on `mode: "push" | "pull"` for every neighbouring blocker — if a pull ever carried it, the row would read "Push the selected sessions first" in a Pull review.
findings.fix: Fix the visibility filter (see the capture-budget banner finding) so this sentence can render, and give the case the same `mode === "push" ? … : …` shape the codec_unsupported case above it uses.

findings.title: Singular capture-budget banner reads "1 conversation wait for the next round"
findings.evidence: title: `${capturePendingCount} conversation${capturePendingCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} wait for the next round`,
findings.impact: The noun is pluralised but the verb is not, so a one-row hold prints ungrammatical copy in a standing banner. The sibling banner twelve lines above gets this right (`${heldProjectFileCount === 1 ? "requires" : "require"}`), so the review can show a correct and an incorrect sentence side by side.
findings.fix: `${count} conversation${count === 1 ? " waits" : "s wait"} for the next round`, matching the project-file banner's verb agreement.

findings.title: The 512 MB capture budget is hardcoded in two user-facing strings and misstates the constant's unit
findings.evidence: message: "This review's 512 MB capture budget filled before their turn. Push the selected conversations first, then open Push review again.",
findings.impact: The authority is `pub const MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES: u64 = 512 * 1024 * 1024;` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/provider_capture.rs:25) — 536.9 MB, i.e. 512 MiB. The number is retyped here and again in ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1120 with no link to the constant, so any change to the ceiling leaves two screens quoting a figure the product no longer enforces, and the backend's own warning string prints the raw byte count instead (service.rs:6757).
findings.fix: Ship the ceiling on the comparison payload (or a formatted string) from Rust and render that, so the copy cannot drift; if it stays hardcoded, write 512 MiB and define it once in the frontend.

findings.title: Five sidebar-gutter assertions were rewritten to reference the constant they test, and nothing now pins the CSS side of the invariant
findings.impact: These assertions previously spelled the literal `3px`; they now import SECTION_DIVIDER_NET from the module under test and interpolate it into the expected string, so they pass for any value the constant takes — the same is true of the three `BOX - SECTION_DIVIDERS_HEIGHT` rewrites at lines 572/580/588 and 596. The number survives only because project-activity.integration.test.tsx:2636 still matches a literal `8px`. Nothing anywhere ties that 8 to the CSS it must equal: App.css:8869 gets the net gutter from `height: 20px; margin: -6px 0`, so a later edit to the handle box (say 20px/-4px) would silently reintroduce exactly the drag-math mismatch this change was made to fix, with the whole suite green.
findings.fix: Keep one literal expectation for the grid template, and add a css-hygiene assertion that `.sidebar-section-divider`'s height plus twice its margin equals SECTION_DIVIDER_NET, so the TS constant and the stylesheet are gated against each other.

findings.title: The new card's `overflow: hidden` clips the in-project file-path tooltip out of existence
findings.impact: Every prompt and reply body now lives inside a clipping box (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and :346 both render `session-detail-card`), and the project-link tooltip is an absolutely positioned `::after` whose containing block is inside that box. Hovering or keyboard-focusing a `[SessionDetailEvent.tsx](src/…)`-style link in a message no longer shows the resolved absolute path: the tooltip sits `100% + 8px` above the link, so for a link on the card's first line (~35px below the card's top border, or ~12px on a reply card with no timestamp band) most or all of the ~40px tooltip is above the card and is cut away, and a link in the right half of a wide card has its 520px tooltip shaved at the card's right edge. The `:focus-visible` arm is clipped identically, so the keyboard route to the path is dead too. At HEAD neither `.session-detail-prompt-card` nor `.session-detail-response-prose` established a clipping box, so this is a regression introduced by the punchcard cutover. The frontend gates assert App.css source text, so all 269 tests pass with the tooltip broken.
findings.fix: In src/App.css, drop `overflow: hidden` from `.session-detail-card` (7240) — the card no longer needs it for grid min-size, because `.session-detail-event-copy` already sets `min-width: 0` and `pre` already sets `overflow: auto`. If the rounded corner must clip the stamp band, clip only the head instead (`.session-detail-card-head { border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0 }`) and leave the card unclipped.

findings.title: Prompt and reply prose lost its 68ch reading measure; the cap was deleted with `.session-detail-prompt-card` and never re-homed
findings.impact: At HEAD `.session-detail-prompt-card` carried `max-width: 68ch` and responses rendered as bare `.session-detail-event-copy`, so both speakers were held to the stated measure. The cutover removed that declaration and put nothing in its place, while keeping the `max-width: none` escape on the inner copy — so conversation text is now uncapped. `.session-detail-page` caps at 1380px (App.css:6842) and the event grid spends 38px on the rail, so a maximized window renders message prose ~1310px wide, roughly 170 characters per line at `--type-lg` (14px); at the default 1100px window with the sidebar hidden it is already ~125. That is the exact failure the rule at 7226 exists to prevent, and it hits the page's primary content — every user prompt and every agent reply.
findings.fix: Restore the measure on the new box: add `max-width: 68ch` to `.session-detail-card` (src/App.css:7239), and re-add `.session-detail-card` to the `@container session-detail-layout (max-width: 720px)` block at App.css:7862 that currently relaxes only `.session-detail-event-copy`. If full-bleed boxes are genuinely wanted, instead cap the inner copy (replace `max-width: none` at 7248 with `max-width: 68ch`) so the box is wide but the text is not.

findings.title: The step box is the only box on the rail still capped at 68ch, so it does not line up with anything
findings.impact: `.session-detail-intermediate-prose` is applied to the same element as `.session-detail-event-copy` (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:487), so it inherits `max-width: 68ch` from App.css:7227, while `.session-detail-card` (7239), `.session-detail-checkpoint-card` (7459 — its `max-width: 68ch` was also deleted in this diff) and the tool rows are all uncapped. Above a 720px container the step boxes stop ~500px in while every other box on the rail runs the full column, producing a ragged right edge that contradicts both this rule's own comment ("the same ink box as everything else on the rail") and the card's ("Every box on the rail runs to the content's right edge"). Below 720px the container query hides it, so it only shows on the wide windows a desktop app spends most of its life in.
findings.fix: Pick one width rule and apply it to all four boxes in src/App.css: either add `max-width: 68ch` to `.session-detail-card` (7239) and `.session-detail-checkpoint-card` (7459), or add `max-width: none` to `.session-detail-intermediate-prose` (7274).

findings.title: `session-detail-card-prompt` and `session-detail-card-reply` are rendered into production markup but match no CSS rule
findings.evidence:
<div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-prompt">
…346:
    <div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-reply">
findings.impact: `grep -n "session-detail-card-prompt\|session-detail-card-reply" src/App.css` returns nothing — the only rules are `.session-detail-card` (7239) and its RetroTheme background override (10964). Prompt and reply cards therefore paint identically: same 2px ink border, same 8px radius, same fill, same shadow, same stamp band. The cutover removed the previous cue (the deleted comment states it outright: "You ask in a card, the agent answers in prose — shape is the speaker") and replaced it with nothing, so in a scrolled transcript the only thing separating your own words from the agent's is the 12px glyph in the 24px rail tile, 38px to the left of the text. The two class names are dead markup that tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:339 and :343 now pin in place.
findings.fix: Either give the two modifiers real rules in src/App.css next to `.session-detail-card` (e.g. `.session-detail-card-prompt { background: var(--surface-subtle) }` or a left ink edge in `--session-detail-you` mirroring the step box's purple edge), or delete both class names from SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303/346 and the assertions that pin them.

findings.title: Every markdown link in session prose renders an invalid `node="[object Object]"` attribute
findings.impact:
react-markdown 10 runs hast-util-to-jsx-runtime with `passNode: true`, so every custom component receives the hast `node` object as a prop. It is not destructured out, so `...props` spreads it onto the DOM element and React 19 stringifies it. Confirmed by rendering the same component shape against the installed packages: output is `

See the file now.

`. Every link in every prompt, reply and step body on the session page carries this bogus attribute — invalid HTML in the inspector, in any copied selection of the DOM, and in anything that scrapes the rendered page.
findings.fix: Destructure the extra prop away in SessionDetailEvent.tsx:158: `a: ({ href, children, node: _node, ...props }) => {`. (The `img` component at :120 already destructures only `src`/`alt` and spreads nothing, so it is unaffected.)

findings.title: A lower-bound tool count prints in the singular: "1+ call"
findings.impact: `formatSessionCount` appends `+` when `count.quality === "lower_bound"` (sessionDetailModel.ts:181), and the turn tool summary is built with a per-session quality that can be LowerBound (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/claude/history.rs:696 and codex/history.rs:1062 both pass `tool_quality` straight through). The plural, however, is chosen from `value`, not from the rendered string — so a truncated transcript whose turn has one known call prints "1+ call" on the prompt card's stamp band: a lower bound stated in the singular, which reads as an exact count of one.
findings.fix: Pluralise on the fact rather than the value in SessionDetailEvent.tsx:309: `callCount.value === 1 && callCount.quality === "exact" ? "call" : "calls"`.

findings.title: Tool calls now default off, so a turn whose last event is a tool call loses its duration stamp
findings.impact: The prompt card's duration is measured over the *loaded* array only — SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:58 computes `sessionTurnSpans(events)` from the filtered page, and `sessionTurnDurationLabel` returns null when `span.ended <= span.started` (sessionDetailModel.ts:317). With tool calls excluded from `included_event_kinds` by default (SessionDetailPage.tsx:229), a turn that has no `response` event — an interrupted turn, where the prompt is followed only by tool calls — now contributes a single-timestamp span and shows no duration at all, where the previous default loaded the calls and printed the real elapsed time. The stamp band silently degrades to a bare clock, indistinguishable from a reply card's, and the "N calls" figure beside it points at rows that are not on screen.
findings.fix: Either keep `toolCalls: sessionCountSupported(counts.tool_calls)` for the span computation and hide the rows in the view layer, or compute turn spans from the session's own turn index server-side so the duration does not depend on which kinds happen to be filtered in.

findings.title: Event anchors, `tabIndex={-1}` and the event focus ring are plumbing nothing reaches
findings.impact: `grep -rn "eventAnchorId" src` shows the id is only ever written, never read: nothing in src/components/project-sync calls `scrollIntoView`, sets `location.hash`, or `getElementById`s an event. The checkpoint `tabIndex={-1}` is never focused programmatically, and `:focus-visible` does not match a mouse click, so `.session-detail-event:focus-visible` (App.css:7161) and `scroll-margin: 80px 0` (App.css:7157) can never fire. A maintainer reading this reasonably assumes deep-linking to an event works and will keep it alive through refactors.
findings.fix: Either wire the anchor up — have SessionDetailPage scroll to and focus `eventAnchorId(...)` when the page is opened for a specific event — or delete `eventAnchorId` from sessionDetailModel.ts:231, the `id`/`tabIndex` at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:440/444, and the `scroll-margin` and `:focus-visible` rules at App.css:7157/7161.

findings.title: Portalled role="dialog" popovers never take focus and close on focus-out, so their controls are keyboard-unreachable
findings.impact: The three info popovers (File details, Session debug info, Catalog "Paths and digests") render through TopLayer at the end of document.body. Opening one moves no focus (the click handler only calls setOpen(true)), so the next Tab from the trigger goes to the next control in the row — which is outside the panel — and the focusin listener immediately closes the popover. Every Copy / Copy all button inside is therefore reachable by mouse only. The role="dialog" announcement also promises a dialog that a screen-reader user is never placed inside.
findings.fix: On open, move focus to the panel (give the panel tabIndex={-1} and focus it, or focus its first Copy button) and only arm the focusin dismissal once focus is inside the panel; keep the existing closeMenu(true) focus restore on Escape. Apply the same change to the two clones at src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:934 and src/components/storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx:315.

findings.title: New path-bar switcher puts a textbox inside role="menu", and no keyboard path can reach it
findings.impact:
role="menu" admits only the menuitem family, so the filter field is not exposed as a form control once assistive tech switches to menu navigation. A keyboard user with six or more storages/projects gets a search box they can only use with a mouse. The zero-result state on line 345 (`

No match.

Wrote three throwaway AST-ish scanners (in the scratchpad) over all 43 production .tsx files to enumerate: buttons/links/summaries whose only content is an icon and that carry no accessible name (one hit, named by title); all 49 form controls and their labelling route (all named); every aria-label/aria-labelledby on a role-less generic element (39 hits); and nested interactive content (no true hits). Prior audit docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md was read and each ARIA-lens item re-verified against today's tree rather than copied: H01 (closed Logs controls tabbable) is FIXED — ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:200 now unmounts LogPanel when closed and the trigger has aria-controls; H07's label-stripping is FIXED — the container queries at App.css:3009 and 3054 now preserve the Push/Pull words and collapse crumb names instead. Not checked: no Tauri run, no browser, no VoiceOver/NVDA pass, no forced-colors or 200%-text pass, so every claim here is source-derived — in particular the accessible-name pollution in StorageSettings.tsx:331 is derived from the accname name-from-label rules rather than observed in a screen reader, and the exact announcement of the `generic`-role aria-labels varies by AT even though the attribute is name-prohibited in all of them. findings.title: Path-bar switcher's filter box cannot be reached by keyboard — Tab closes the menu instead of entering it
findings.impact: The Switch-storage / Switch-project filter box appears only once a switcher has ≥6 targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR, line 129) — exactly when filtering is needed. No keyboard path reaches it: opening with click leaves focus on the toggle and Tab there closes the menu (line 516); opening with ArrowDown calls focusMenuOption, which focuses `menuOptions(root)[0]` — a `[role=menuitem]` button, never the input (menuKeyboard.ts:11); Tab from inside the menu closes it (line 258); and moveMenuFocus only cycles menuitems, so arrows never return to the input. A keyboard-only user with 12 projects must arrow past all of them one row at a time and can never filter. WCAG 2.1.1 failure on a newly added control.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx give the input `tabIndex={0}` in an explicit focus cycle: when `searchable`, have focusMenuOption target the input first on open, and in the menu's onKeyDown special-case Tab/Shift+Tab to move between the input and the first menu option (preventDefault) instead of calling onClose(false); keep Tab-closes only for menus with no search field. ArrowUp from the first option should return focus to the input.

findings.title: Switcher menu has no max-height or scroll, so its verb footer falls off the clipped window on long switch lists
findings.impact: This change moved the crumb's verbs from the top of the menu (they were the first group, always visible) into a footer strip rendered after the whole switch list. `.sync-path-menu` has no max-height and the app root is `overflow: hidden`, so a tall menu is hard-clipped with no scrollbar and no page scroll. Chrome measures ~166px (header 52 + search 42 + footer 60 + padding/border 12) and each target row is 34px min-height; the menu opens 66px below the window top. At the app's configured minWidth/minHeight of 800×560 (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) that leaves room for about 9 targets. A user with 10+ projects opens the project crumb and Reveal in Finder, Agent profile…, Rename project…, Reset local sync state… and Add project… are all painted below the window edge and unreachable — those verbs exist nowhere else in the UI.
findings.fix: In src/App.css give `.sync-path-menu` a `max-height: calc(100vh - 80px)` with `display: flex; flex-direction: column`, make only the switch-list region (`.sync-path-menu-group`) `overflow-y: auto; min-height: 0`, and leave `.sync-path-menu-current`, `.sync-path-menu-search` and `.sync-path-menu-foot` as non-shrinking flex children so the verbs stay pinned inside the viewport.

findings.title: Role-by-position turns a lone "Add storage…" group into an unlabelled icon pill
findings.impact: The switcher decides "verb" vs "way to get more" purely by group position, so when the labelled "Switch to" group is empty the trailing group is misread as the first group. In ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707-1731 the storage-page crumb menu is exactly `[...(otherStorages ? [{label:"Switch to",…}] : []), {items:[add-storage]}]`. With one storage configured — the state right after adding the first one — `storages.some(c => c.id !== editedStorageConfig.id)` is false, so `populated[0]` is the unlabelled Add group and "Add storage…" renders as a bare `+` glyph in the footer with no visible text (label survives only in aria-label and title). The user opens the storage switcher and sees the current storage plus one unexplained icon.
findings.fix: Stop inferring the verbs group from position alone. Either only treat `populated[0]` as verbs when a labelled group exists later in the array (`populated.some(g => g.label)`), falling back to rendering it as tails, or add an explicit `role: "verbs" | "tail"` field to PathBarMenuGroup and have ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1722 mark its Add group as a tail.

findings.title: Prompt cards lose their turn duration entirely for tool-only turns after the SHOW default flip
findings.impact: `sessionTurnSpans` derives each turn's extent from whatever events are currently loaded, and this diff flipped tool calls off by default (they used to be `sessionCountSupported(counts.tool_calls)`, i.e. on). Measured against the real index in ~/.mallard/session_timeline_cache.json (36 sessions, 229 turns): 8 turns collapse to a zero-length span under the new defaults and their duration chip disappears completely — including one codex turn that actually ran 730s and one claude turn that ran 467s. Those are turns that ended in tool calls with no separate response event (interrupted or still-running turns), so the punchcard stamp band now reads "14:02 · 24 calls" and silently implies the agent's twelve minutes of work took no time at all. Turning SHOW › Tool calls on makes the duration reappear, so the same card shows two different truths.
findings.fix: Compute turn spans from the session's full index rather than the filtered page: have SessionDetailPage pass an unfiltered span map (or have the backend include turn start/end in `turn_tool_summary`) into SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:58, so `turnDuration` no longer depends on which SHOW toggles are on. Update the PromptCard comment at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:279-283, which still says "duration measured from the turn's loaded extent".

findings.title: No error boundary anywhere: one render-time RangeError blanks the whole Tauri window with no way back
findings.impact: `grep -rn "componentDidCatch|ErrorBoundary|getDerivedStateFromError" src/` returns nothing, so any throw during render unmounts the entire tree. There are seven unguarded `Date.prototype.toISOString()` calls in render paths (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:404, 671, 1445, 1923, 1966; SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:161; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:719; sessionDetailModel.ts:245) plus `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format` in clock.ts:56 and LogPanel.tsx:114 — all of which throw RangeError on an invalid or out-of-range Date rather than returning "Invalid Date". `toEpochMilliseconds` (clock.ts:27) passes any value above 1e10 through unscaled, so a nanosecond-precision timestamp from a malformed transcript lands at ~1.7e18 ms, well outside Date's ±8.64e15 range. In a Tauri webview the result is a permanently white window: there is no browser chrome, no reload button, and no visible error.
findings.fix: Add an ErrorBoundary component wrapping <ProjectSync/> in src/App.tsx that renders a recovery panel (the error text plus a button calling window.location.reload()), and harden the date helpers: make `sessionDetailDateTime` and the inline `new Date(x*1000).toISOString()` call sites return undefined when `Number.isFinite(date.getTime())` is false.
