findings.title: Push review's capture-budget banner counts conversations the review filters out of every list
findings.impact: The comment's premise is false. `blocked_conversation_decision` (crates/mallard-domain/src/conversation_reconciliation.rs:246-253) returns `selectable: false, action: Blocked`, and the Push review's session list drops exactly those rows: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 keeps a session only when `isPushReviewStatus(status) && isPushReviewDecision(entry.push_decision)`, and `isPushReviewDecision` (sync-review/pullReviewStatus.ts:17) requires `decision.selectable`. The ResourceInventory fallback at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:768 filters the same way via `visibleConversationResourceIds` (line 437). So the banner says "3 conversations wait for the next round" while none of the three appear anywhere in the review — the user cannot tell which sessions were deferred, cannot check their size, and has no way to verify the situation cleared after the next push.
findings.fix: Either render the held rows: relax the Push-review filter at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 to keep entries whose blocker is `capture_budget` (rendered inert, with syncHoldDetail's new case at line 1119 as the reason line), or reword the banner at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:571-576 to say the deferred conversations are not listed in this review and correct the comment at line 564.

findings.title: session-detail-card-prompt and session-detail-card-reply are emitted with no CSS rule anywhere
findings.evidence:
<div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-prompt">
…
    <div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-reply">
findings.impact: `grep -n "session-detail-card" src/App.css` matches only `.session-detail-card` (7239), `.session-detail-card > .session-detail-event-copy` (7247), `.session-detail-card-head` (7255) and two RetroTheme references (10919, 10964). Neither `-prompt` nor `-reply` has a single declaration, so the two modifiers are inert: prompt and reply cards paint identically and the classes read as a styling hook that does not exist, which is a trap for the next person trying to differentiate the two speakers.
findings.fix: Either drop the two modifier classes in SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and 346 and keep only `session-detail-card`, or add the intended `.session-detail-card-prompt` / `.session-detail-card-reply` rules to src/App.css near the `.session-detail-card` block at line 7239.

r.coverage:
Read in full or in the relevant regions: SyncPathBar.tsx (all 645 lines, plus its git diff), menuKeyboard.ts, SessionDetailEvent.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx (hooks 100-380), SessionDetailTimeline.tsx, sessionDetailModel.ts, SessionDetailToolbar.tsx, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx (hooks + banner block 400-780), ProjectSync.tsx (all hooks: 320-680, 760-860, 1121-1440, push call site 3390-3480), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx (hooks 700-1400, crumb/menu construction 1660-1760 and 2265-2560), ProjectActivityPage.tsx (BranchPicker 136-200, debug menu 835-905, memo/effect tail 1495-1560 and 2230-2350), ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx, ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx (auto-scan effect), StorageCatalogPage.tsx (820-1030, crumbs 1180-1400), RestorePlanView.tsx (315-400), ActivityLogDrawer.tsx, LogPanel.tsx, SettingsPage.tsx (tuning selects), ProjectSidebar.tsx (geometry + persistence effects), App.tsx, main.tsx, clock.ts, and the relevant App.css blocks (.sync-path-menu family 3055-3320, sidebar sections 3389-3560 / 8757-8915, .session-detail-card 7239-7260, root layout 1-60).

Method: enumerated every useEffect/useLayoutEffect/useMemo/useCallback with its dependency array across the whole non-mockup src tree via a Node script; grepped every `key=` in the production tree for index/duplicate keys; grepped every timer/rAF for cleanup; scripted a scan for hooks after early returns (all four hits verified as false positives — no conditional hooks exist); grepped every controlled `value={}` for undefined flips. Ran `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Verified the turn-duration regression numerically against real data in ~/.mallard/session_timeline_cache.json (36 sessions, 229 turns) with a Python script comparing all-event spans to prompt/response/checkpoint-only spans. Confirmed the capture_budget selectability claim by reading blocked_conversation_decision in crates/mallard-domain/src/conversation_reconciliation.rs and isPushReviewDecision in sync-review/pullReviewStatus.ts. Confirmed CSS class existence by grepping App.css for every new class name emitted by the changed components.

Not checked: no runtime execution — the app was never launched, so nothing was verified in a live webview (menu clipping and the keyboard trap are argued from source, CSS and the tauri.conf.json window bounds, not observed on screen). Did not run the node:test frontend suite. Rust/backend correctness was consulted only for the two decisions above. Mockup files (src/*mockup*.tsx, root *.html) were excluded per the brief and I found no import of them from the production tree and no class collision with production selectors. Deliberately did not report: ref writes during render (reconcileExternalChangesRef in ProjectSync.tsx:1290, selectionRef/onApplyRef in RestorePlanView.tsx:386-389, bannersAtOpen in PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:598) — all idempotent latest-value patterns, safe under StrictMode; requestToolDetail's `toolDetails` dependency (SessionDetailPage.tsx:268) and `selectedResourceIds = new Set()` default (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1521) — identity churn with no observable consequence; the openMenuRequest effect's missing `crumbs` dependency (SyncPathBar.tsx:440) — its only caller's menu is always populated, so the stale-closure path is unreachable today; a ~10px optimism in the sidebar drag clamp (ProjectSidebar.tsx:69) caused by measuring `getBoundingClientRect().height` against a grid that also carries 8px/2px padding — the pane just scrolls, no visible break.

findings.title: Pull is permanently disabled and mislabelled "Loading storage changes…" when the in-review comparison fails
findings.impact: If the thread comparison (or the activity page load) fails while a Pull review is open — R2 offline, a provider scan error — `comparison` stays null and `reviewListReady` never becomes true. Both Pull controls (the review footer button at line 692 and the path-bar Pull at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2619, which shares `continueDisabled`/`continueTitle`) stay disabled forever, and the only explanation offered is the tooltip "Loading storage changes…" — which claims work is still in flight when it has already failed. Nothing inside the review can re-run the comparison: `refreshEpoch={0}` is hardcoded (RestorePlanView.tsx:585), `comparisonOverride` is not passed so the mount effect's deps never change, the comparison notice carries no retry (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1751-1759), and the path bar's refresh button is not rendered during an inline review (the standalone activity page is unmounted at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3302, which nulls `activityHeader`). The user must abandon and reopen the whole review, with no on-screen hint that this is what is needed.
findings.fix: In RestorePlanView.tsx, have ProjectActivityPage report failure as well as readiness (e.g. widen `onReviewListReadyChange` to a tri-state or add `onReviewListFailed`), and when it reports failure set `primaryDisabledReason` to a truthful sentence plus a visible Retry that bumps a `refreshEpoch` prop passed down to ProjectActivityPage. At minimum, add an `action` with a retry button to the `comparison-failed` notice in ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1751 that calls `loadComparison`, and stop gating the primary on `reviewListReady` once the load has settled in failure.

findings.title: A failed project-file scan leaves the Push review showing an endless "Scanning project files" skeleton
findings.impact: `scanPendingProjectFiles` (ProjectSync.tsx:2015) leaves `projectContentScanned` false on failure, so this branch stays true forever: the page renders LoadingScaffold with the caption "Scanning project files…" and a spinning `status-loader` indefinitely, while the toolbar's Rescan button beside it reads "Rescan" (not "Scanning…") and the parent shows a red error notice. The comment two lines above ("A failed scan leaves `scanned` false with the parent's error notice on screen") assumes the body shows nothing; it actually shows a permanent, contradictory progress state. A user who does not notice the error banner will wait for a scan that is not running.
findings.fix: Pass the scan failure into ProjectFilesReviewPage (a `scanError?: string | null` prop fed from `pushError`) and branch on it: render an error state with a Retry that calls `onScan` instead of the LoadingScaffold. Gate the skeleton on `loading`, not on `!scanned`.

findings.title: `project_files_error` is never read, so a failed project-file inventory silently removes the Files step from the Push review
findings.impact: For a Git-managed project the backend builds the stored project-files inventory during `prepare_push_review`; when that build fails it returns `project_files: null` plus `project_files_error`. The frontend never reads the error field, so `showProjectFiles` is false and the entire "Project files" tab, step navigator and footer step disappear from the Push review — rendered identically to "this project has no project-file changes". The user pushes believing there is nothing to publish outside conversations, when in fact the check never completed. The backend already logs a warning for exactly this ("the reason must reach the log, not only the context the frontend may or may not render"), but no UI consumes it. Note `thread_comparison_error` was just wired up in this same working tree; its sibling was left behind.
findings.fix: Thread `context.project_files_error` into `PendingPush` the same way `threadComparisonError` was (ProjectSync.tsx:1912) and render it as a danger banner in PushResourceWorkspace beside the existing `comparison-failed` banner, keeping the Files step visible with a Rescan action rather than hiding it.

findings.title: Path-bar switcher menus have no max-height and are hard-clipped by the app's `overflow: hidden` root
findings.impact: The uncommitted switcher rework makes the project and storage crumb menus list every other project/storage (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2427, 2298) and appends a footer strip carrying the verbs plus "Link storage…"/"Add storage…"/"Add project…". With `.sync-path-menu-item { min-height: 34px }`, a header (~52px), the search field (~42px) and the footer (~52px), the menu exceeds the viewport at roughly 14 other projects in the 720px default window and roughly 9 at the 560px `minHeight` from tauri.conf.json. Because the menu has no `max-height`/`overflow-y` and the document root is `overflow: hidden`, the overflowing rows and the whole footer strip are clipped with no scrollbar — "Add project…" and "Link storage…" become unreachable by mouse, and arrow-key focus lands on invisible rows. The search field exists precisely because ≥6 targets is expected (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR), so this is a state the design anticipates.
findings.fix: Give `.sync-path-menu` a `max-height: min(70vh, calc(100vh - 96px))` and make only the target list scroll: wrap the `lists` groups in a scroll container with `overflow-y: auto` so the header, the search field and `.sync-path-menu-foot` stay pinned and reachable.

findings.title: Capture-budget conversations are filtered out of the Push review that the new banner points at
findings.impact: `blocked_conversation_decision` sets `selectable: false` (conversation_reconciliation.rs:250), so `isPushReviewDecision` returns false and every capture-budget row is removed from `sessions` in the Push review's list — the opposite of what the comment promises. The banner tells the user "N conversations wait for the next round" while none of those N are anywhere on screen, so they cannot see which sessions were held. When every candidate is over budget the review renders the green check-circle empty state "Nothing to push · No local session changes are ready to push" (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1848-1858) directly beneath a warning banner saying N are waiting — two mutually contradictory statements in one view.
findings.fix: In ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1543-1546, admit push-review rows whose `push_decision.blocker === "capture_budget"` into `sessions` (unselectable, wearing the `syncHoldDetail` sentence already added at line 1119), and exclude them from `selectionReviewEmpty` so the "Nothing to push" state cannot co-render with the banner.

findings.title: Switcher footer reduces menu verbs to unlabelled icons, dropping the visible disabled reason a comment explicitly requires
findings.impact: Every item in a switcher's first unlabelled group is now drawn as an icon-only pill and every trailing item as a text pill; in both cases `disabledReason` and `detail` reach the screen only through `title`. Concretely: the storage crumb's "Unlink from <project>…" — a destructive action — becomes a bare red chain-break glyph with no words (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2284), and "Link storage…" loses its visible reason "Everything you've added is already linked" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2321), whose own source comment says it "stays put at zero candidates and says why, instead of vanishing from the DOM for a reason the user cannot see". A sighted user now sees a greyed pill with no explanation unless they hover, and `.sync-path-menu-item[aria-disabled]`'s documented "reason line is reachable by keyboard" contract no longer holds for these rows.
findings.fix: Render the pill's `disabledReason` as visible text — either as a second line in `.sync-path-menu-cap` (the footer caption already reserves a full-width row) or by keeping items that carry a `disabledReason` in the list body rather than the footer. Give verb pills a visible label, or at minimum keep destructive verbs (`danger: true`) as full rows.

findings.title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard and is an invalid child of `role="menu"`
findings.impact:
Opening a switcher by click leaves focus on the trigger, and opening it with Arrow keys focuses the first `role="menuitem"`; `focusMenuEdge`/`focusMenuOption` only ever look at menuitem roles, so the input is never focused. Tab — the only remaining way to reach it — is intercepted at line 256 and closes the menu. The field is therefore pointer-only: a keyboard user with 6+ projects or storages must arrow through the whole unbounded list (which, per the previous finding, may be clipped off-screen). Separately, `role="menu"` admits only menuitem/group/separator children, so the textbox and the `

No match.

` fallback at line 355 are not reliably exposed by screen readers in menu navigation mode.
findings.fix: Focus the search input on open when `searchable` (and let ArrowDown step from it into the list, which the keydown handler already supports), or add an explicit key (e.g. `/`) that moves focus there. For semantics, either drop `role="menu"` for switchers in favour of a listbox/combobox pattern, or move the input outside the menu element and reference it with `aria-controls`.

findings.title: A failed autosave wedges project setup: Finish goes dead with no reason and no retry
findings.impact: The debounced autosave clears `dirtyRef.current` before it awaits (line 300) and does not restore it in the catch (line 324-327), so after a failed `updateSetupDraft` the effect's own guard (`!dirtyRef.current` at line 297) prevents any retry. `saveState` is stuck at "error", which disables Finish permanently. The footer shows only the two words "Not saved", the Finish button carries no `title` explaining why it is dead, and there is no Retry button anywhere — the danger Notice at line 986 has no action. The only ways out are to make an unrelated edit (which sets `dirtyRef` and reschedules a save) or to Discard the draft; neither is signposted.
findings.fix: Set `dirtyRef.current = true` in the autosave catch so the next scheduled pass retries, add an explicit "Try saving again" action to the error Notice, and give the Finish button a `title` derived from why `canFinalize` is false ("Save the draft before finishing").

findings.title: A failed tool-detail fetch hides the preview payload the row already has, and offers no retry
findings.impact: Expanding a tool row fires `getProjectSessionEventDetail`; if it fails, the row shows only a red box. The `tool.argument_preview` and `tool.result_preview` that arrived with the timeline page are already in memory and would render fine, but the `!detailState?.error` guard suppresses `ToolPayload` entirely — the user loses content they could otherwise read. There is also no retry button: the only way to re-request is to collapse the `<details>` and reopen it, which is not discoverable from the error box.
findings.fix: Render `ToolPayload` whenever `argumentsValue`/`resultValue`/`affectedPaths` are non-empty, regardless of `detailState.error`, and downgrade the notice to a warning ("Full detail unavailable — showing the bounded preview") with a Retry `action` that calls back into `requestToolDetail` for this event id.

findings.title: Catalog and setup-draft list failures are swallowed, so the sidebar shows "Add your first…" for content that exists
findings.impact: `refreshCatalogScopes` (1542), `refreshSetupDrafts` (1390) and `refreshStorageSetupDrafts` (1410) all catch and discard. Because they never reject, `Promise.allSettled` always reports them fulfilled and they contribute nothing to `backendError`, so no notice appears anywhere. On a cold start where any of these listings fails, the sidebar's Catalog section renders the first-run call to action "Add your first resource" (ProjectSidebar.tsx:950-957) and the Storages section "Add your first storage" (1031) even though the user has rows and in-progress drafts — an empty state presented as fact when the request that would have listed them failed. An interrupted project or storage setup draft simply disappears, inviting the user to start over and create a duplicate.
findings.fix: Let these helpers reject (or record a failure flag) and fold them into `loadShell`'s `failures` array so the shell's backend-unavailable notice with its Retry appears. At minimum, track a per-section load-failed flag and render "Couldn't load Catalog rows" with a retry in place of the first-run empty state.

findings.title: The non-Git Files page replaces the whole view with an error box that carries no retry
findings.impact: This early return pre-empts the toolbar (line 331-356) that holds the Rescan button, so a failed folder scan leaves a bare red message with no control next to it. The only retry is the small refresh glyph in the path bar (wired through `onHeaderModelChange` at line 461-467) — a different region of the screen, with a generic refresh icon and no visual connection to the failure. The message also does not say the view is recoverable, so a user reasonably concludes the folder cannot be scanned.
findings.fix: Give the Notice an `action` with a "Try again" button that calls `onRescan` (already available as `setScanEpoch`), matching the pattern ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1834-1844 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1949-1956 already use.

findings.title: No React error boundary: an uncaught render error blanks the window with no way back
findings.impact: React 19 unmounts the whole tree on an uncaught render error. With `hiddenTitle: true` and `titleBarStyle: "Overlay"` in tauri.conf.json there is no app chrome left to act on, and `html, body, #root { overflow: hidden }` means the user is left with a blank coloured window and must force-quit. Render-time throws are reachable from data: `sessionDetailDateTime` (sessionDetailModel.ts:244) does `new Date(toEpochMilliseconds(value)).toISOString()`, and `toEpochMilliseconds` (clock.ts:27) passes any value above 1e10 through unscaled — a nanosecond-precision timestamp from a provider log yields an Invalid Date and `toISOString()` throws RangeError. Similar unguarded `toISOString()` calls exist at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:404, 671, 1445, 1923, 1966.
findings.fix: Wrap `<App />` in an error boundary that renders a recovery screen (message plus a "Reload" button calling `window.location.reload()`), reusing the shape of the existing `sync-host-recovery` screen in ProjectSync.tsx:3516. Separately, make `sessionDetailDateTime` return `undefined` when `Number.isNaN(new Date(ms).getTime())`.

findings.title: Add Catalog resource: a failed capability load leaves an empty provider dropdown with no retry
findings.impact: `listProfiles`/`listCapabilities` run once on mount with no loading state and no retry. On failure `capabilities` stays `[]`, so `supportedProviders` is empty and the Provider select offers only the placeholder "Choose provider"; the Kind radios still respond, and Add stays disabled with no title. The page shows a red error box (line 345-354) with no action, so the only recovery is to close the workspace and re-enter it — which is not stated. On success there is also no skeleton, so the provider list pops in after the radios render.
findings.fix: Track a `catalogLoading` flag, render a loading line in place of the provider row while it is set, and give the error Notice an `action` that re-runs the two `storageCatalogApi` reads.

findings.title: The session-detail loading skeleton draws a two-column layout the loaded page never has
findings.evidence:
<div className="loading-scaffold-panes">
        {[0, 1].map((pane) => (
          <div key={pane} className="loading-scaffold-pane">

// App.css:287
.loading-scaffold-panes {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));

// App.css:6935 / 7081 — what actually lands
.session-detail-layout { display: grid; gap: 14px; }
.session-detail-event-list { position: relative; min-width: 0; display: grid; gap: 0; list-style: none; }
findings.impact: The `detail` shape is used only by SessionDetailPage (line 85). Its third block is a 2-column grid of two bordered panes, but the loaded page is a single-column toolbar over a single-column rail of full-width `.session-detail-card` boxes — there is no two-column region anywhere in the session detail markup. Every session opened therefore shows two half-width bone panes that snap into one full-width column on arrival, which is exactly the layout jump the scaffold's own docstring says it exists to prevent ("arrival changes pixels, never geometry").
findings.fix: Replace `loading-scaffold-panes` in `DetailBones` with a single-column stack of two or three full-width card bones matching `.session-detail-card` (ink border, 8px radius, stamp band strip on top), and drop `grid-template-columns: repeat(2, …)` from `.loading-scaffold-panes`.

findings.title: The main empty pane offers no primary action and names only Codex
findings.evidence:
Project history

Select a completed project to view its Codex history.
findings.impact: This is what a first-run user sees in the whole workspace area. It contains no button — unlike StorageIndexPage.tsx:63-69 and CatalogIndexPage.tsx:44-50, which both pair their empty state with an "Add …" primary — so the only route forward is the sidebar's "Add your first project". The copy also tells the user to select a "completed" project (a word the product never defines) and promises "Codex history", although the same page lists Claude sessions: `list_agent_providers` drives a multi-provider binding and ProjectActivityPage renders per-provider marks and per-provider error notices. A Claude-only user is told this view is for another agent.
findings.fix: Add an "Add project" primary button to this state (the `onAddProject` handler already reaches ProjectLinksWorkspace), and change the subtitle to name the product concept rather than one provider — e.g. "Choose a project in the sidebar to see its agent sessions."

findings.title: Two concurrent session row actions clobber each other's busy state
findings.impact: Busy state is a single resource id, and each row disables its own buttons only while it is the busy one (`busy={actionBusyResourceId === session.resource_id}` at line 1655, `disabled={!action.enabled || busy}` at line 1304). Starting an action on row B while row A is still in flight clears A's spinner and re-enables A's buttons, so A can be launched a second time; whichever request settles first then clears the busy state for both, leaving the other row's spinner off while its launch is still running. Also, `setActionError(null)` at the top of the second call wipes an error the first call may have just reported.
findings.fix: Track in-flight actions as a `Set<string>` of `${resource_id}:${action_id}` (or at least guard with `if (actionBusyResourceId) return;`), and clear only this call's own entry in the `finally`.

findings.title: The retheme's hard cast shadow is invisible in the dark theme (1.00–1.04:1) while the light theme carries it at 4.03–5.83:1
findings.impact: The cast shadow is the retheme's box grammar — `box-shadow: var(--shadow-card)` was added to buttons, cards, tiles, path-bar pills, sidebar panes, the active nav row, the switcher's current-object row and the sidebar section actions in this very diff, and `.btn:active` drops it to signal a press ("Pressing sinks the button into its own shadow", App.css:8506). Composited over the surfaces it actually falls on, the dark value measures: #0b0705 on --retro-frame-gutter #040303 = 1.03:1, #191312 on --surface-card #171412 = 1.01:1, #141210 on --bg-0 #12100d = 1.00:1. It is not visible at all. Light measures #6f6057 on those same grounds at 4.03:1, 5.65:1 and 5.83:1. So in dark mode every lifted box is flat, the active sidebar destination loses the "lifted box" cue the comment at App.css:8733 promises, and the press animation is a bare 1px jump with nothing behind it. The light theme was deliberately converted to a solid ink in this diff; the dark block was left on the old translucent wash.
findings.fix: In the dark palette block (src/App.css:8074-8076) replace the translucent shadow inks with a solid value that separates from the dark surfaces the same way #6f6057 separates from cream — e.g. a warm near-black lifted off the paper, or the same #6f6057-equivalent step measured against --bg-0/--surface-card. Then re-measure --shadow-card against --retro-frame-gutter, --bg-0, --surface-card and --surface-row in both themes and pin the pair with a gate alongside tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx.

findings.title: Keyboard focus on a session-detail tool row draws nothing: a 2px --accent outline is inset exactly onto the row's 2px --accent border
findings.impact: With `outline-offset: -2px` the outline edge is inset 2px and the 2px outline is painted outward from it, so it lands exactly on the 2px border band — and both are the same colour (`--box-border` is `2px solid var(--accent)` and `--focus-ring` is `var(--accent)`). I rendered the exact three-case comparison in a browser: a 2px #efe7d4 border with a 2px #efe7d4 outline at -2px is pixel-identical to the unfocused row, while the same geometry with a red outline turns the whole border red — proving the outline is fully covered. Before this diff the summary had no border (`margin: 0 -8px; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 3px`, HEAD App.css:7331) so the inset ring was the only ink there and was visible. A keyboard user tabbing/arrowing through a session transcript now has no indication of which tool row is focused (WCAG 2.4.7).
findings.fix: In src/App.css:7583-7586 change the offset so the ring is not the border: use `outline-offset: -4px` (a ring inside the border, verified visible in the same test) or `outline-offset: 2px` with the row's overflow allowing it. Same audit applies to any other selector that pairs `outline-offset: -2px` with `border: var(--box-border)`.

findings.title: The Settings theme segmented control clips its buttons' focus ring — overflow:hidden with a +2px outline offset
findings.impact: The segment has no padding, so each button's border box touches the segment's padding box; `overflow: hidden` clips to that padding box, and an outline offset 2px outward falls entirely outside it. I rendered the control both ways: with overflow:hidden the focused "Light" button shows only two vertical slivers that look exactly like the existing dividers between segments, while overflow:visible shows a full ring. The user cannot tell which of System / Light / Dark is focused when tabbing (SettingsPage.tsx:391-404 is the Theme radiogroup, the app's only appearance control).
findings.fix: Give `.sync-settings-segment` 2px of padding (and shrink the inner button geometry to match) so the outline lands inside the clip, or add a scoped `.sync-settings-segment > button:focus-visible { outline-offset: -2px }` so the ring is drawn inside the button.

findings.title: Warning glyphs painted in raw --yellow measure 2.19–2.49:1 in the light theme against 8.0–11.1:1 in dark
findings.impact: Measured across every opaque surface in the app the best light-theme ratio --yellow (#d99609) reaches is 2.49:1 (on --bg-4 #fffdf9); on the sidebar pane it is 2.41:1, on --surface-card 2.37:1 and on the warning tint behind the path-menu banner 2.19:1. The dark value (#f4b94f) reaches 10.11–11.13:1 on the same grounds. The sidebar one is the sharpest case: the triangle is `aria-hidden="true"` (ProjectSidebar.tsx:892-897), so for a sighted user it is the only indication in the project list that a project has no agent profile assigned, and in light mode it is barely there. The comment quoted above records the 2.4:1 measurement and calls it "fine for glyphs", but WCAG 1.4.11 sets 3:1 for graphical objects required to understand content, and green (3.38) and blue (3.72) clear it while amber does not.
findings.fix: Darken the light palette's --yellow (src/App.css:8163) until it clears 3:1 on --bg-4 and --surface-card, or repoint these five glyph rules at --warning-text (light #885e06, 5.40:1 on --surface-card; dark #f4b94f, 10.39:1) which already resolves per theme. Extend tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx with a 3:1 gate over the raw signal hues on every opaque surface.

findings.title: The settings switch's off-state thumb is nearly invisible in the light theme (2.50:1) but clear in dark (7.06:1)
findings.impact: `.sync-settings-switch` is `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` (SettingsPage.tsx:86-93) and its off state is conveyed only by the thumb sitting at the left of the track — the track itself is --switch-off in both states-off. Light: thumb #fffaf4 on track #ad9e92 = 2.50:1. Dark: #f6f2df on #575048 = 7.06:1. Same construction, a 2.8x difference. In light mode the three Settings toggles read as plain tan pills with a faint pale smudge at one end, so "off" is hard to distinguish at a glance; in dark it is unambiguous. The track itself is also only 2.44:1 against --surface-card in light (2.31:1 in dark), so the 1px --border-strong rim (6.48:1 light) is doing all the work of finding the control.
findings.fix: Darken the light --switch-off (src/App.css:8143) until the #fffaf4 thumb clears 3:1 against it — around #8d7d70 gives ~3.6:1 — and re-check the thumb/track pair for both themes; the checked state already inverts to --accent/--accent-contrast and is fine.

findings.title: Two focusable readouts replace the global focus ring with a translucent shadow that never reaches 3:1
findings.impact: Both elements are `tabIndex={0}` (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:596-605 and 670-707) — every session row in Activity puts five or six of them in the tab order — and both cancel the app's opaque outline. Composited over --surface-row the replacement measures: indicator 35% mix #b3ada8 on #fdf9f3 = 2.11:1 light, #615d54 on #14120f = 2.83:1 dark; metric 45% mix #9e9893 on #fdf9f3 = 2.72:1 light, #777268 on #14120f = 3.90:1 dark. Only the dark metric clears the 3:1 floor for a focus indicator. A keyboard user stepping across a session row's sync badge and its message/tool/token readouts cannot see where focus is, in either theme for the badge.
findings.fix: Drop the `outline: none` at src/App.css:5215 and 5367 and let the shared `.sync-app *:focus-visible` ring apply, or raise the mixes to an opaque ink that clears 3:1 on --surface-row and --surface-row-hover in both themes (the current 45% mix is 3.90:1 dark / 2.72:1 light, so light needs a materially stronger step).

findings.title: The new switcher menu's search field cannot be reached with the keyboard
findings.impact: The field renders once a switcher has SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 or more switch targets — reachable in practice with seven projects (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2427-2438 builds the "Switch to" group from every other project) or seven linked storages. It is not a menuitem, so `moveMenuFocus` skips it; opening with ArrowDown lands on `options[0]`; Tab from inside the menu calls `onClose(false)` and from the crumb button (SyncPathBar.tsx:516, 551) closes the menu too; and printable characters are consumed by the menu's own typeahead (L280-297). Only a mouse click reaches it. A keyboard user with many projects is left scrolling a list the mouse user can filter, and the handler at L264-274 that carefully implements Enter/ArrowDown behaviour "while typing" is unreachable code.
findings.fix: Focus the search input instead of `options[0]` when the menu is searchable (SyncPathBar.tsx:420-430), and let ArrowUp from the first menuitem return to it; keep Tab closing the menu only when focus is not in the field, or move the field into the roving order explicitly.

findings.title: Read-category tool names fall to 3.93:1 on an expanded tool row in the light theme
findings.impact: `--session-detail-link` resolves to #2c779c in light. On the closed row's --surface-row (#fdf9f3) it is 4.72:1, but the moment the row is expanded the background becomes --surface-row-active (#f0e3d5) and it drops to 3.93:1 — under the 4.5 floor for text that is 9px (`font-size: var(--type-3xs)`), uppercase and letter-spaced (App.css:7597-7606). The same row's `--session-detail-you` red would be 4.00:1 and `--danger-text` on the failure pill 4.41:1 there. Dark is unaffected (8.8–10.6:1). The mixes at App.css:6850-6852 were tuned against the page paper, not against the darkest row state the page actually paints.
findings.fix: Re-tune the three `--session-detail-*` mixes at src/App.css:6850-6852 against --surface-row-active (#f0e3d5 light) rather than the page paper — raising the --text-0 share for the link mix clears it — or stop darkening the open row and use the ink border alone to mark it open.

findings.title: The SHOW filter's drawn checkbox is below the 3:1 non-text floor in both themes, and the retheme made its low-contrast state the default
findings.impact: The unchecked box is a 9px square whose only ink is a 1px --border-mid rim on the toggle's --bg-4 fill: 2.70:1 light (#aa998d on #fffdf9), 1.75:1 dark (#443d36 on #14120f). Its own fill --bg-1 against --bg-4 is 1.03:1/1.05:1, so there is no shape to fall back on. The toggle's own boundary is no better — --border on --surface-footer is 1.41:1 light / 1.35:1 dark, and --bg-4 vs --surface-footer is 1.08:1/1.04:1 — so the whole control reads as bare text. This diff also flipped `toolCalls` and `intermediateSteps` to false by default (sessionDetailModel.ts:91-94), so two of the five SHOW filters now open in exactly this near-invisible unchecked state, which is what the user has to find to reveal tool calls at all.
findings.fix: Draw `.session-detail-filter-box` with `--control-border` (--border-strong: 6.48:1 light / 3.78:1 dark on card) instead of --border-mid, and give `.session-detail-filter-toggle` a boundary that clears 3:1 against --surface-footer — the app already has `--box-border` for exactly this.

findings.title: The Theme radiogroup is three plain buttons: no roving tabindex, no arrow-key selection
findings.evidence:
<div className="sync-settings-segment" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Theme">
  {THEME_CHOICES.map((choice) => (
    <button
      key={choice.value}
      type="button"
      role="radio"
      aria-checked={themeChoice === choice.value}
      className={themeChoice === choice.value ? "active" : undefined}
      onClick={() => setThemeChoice(choice.value)}
    >
findings.impact: A `role="radio"` set inside `role="radiogroup"` promises one tab stop with Arrow keys moving and selecting; here all three buttons carry the default tabIndex so Tab visits each one, and there is no onKeyDown, so Arrow keys do nothing. A screen-reader user told "radio, 1 of 3" presses Right and nothing happens, then has to Tab past all three to leave the control. The review tabs elsewhere in the app (SyncReviewTabs.tsx) already implement the roving pattern correctly, so this one control diverges.
findings.fix: Give each button `tabIndex={themeChoice === choice.value ? 0 : -1}` and an onKeyDown that maps ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End to move focus and select, reusing the roving helper the review tabs already use; or drop role=radio and expose the three as toggle buttons with aria-pressed.

findings.title: Dead `border-radius: 50%` on the settings switch thumb, immediately overridden in the same block
findings.impact: The retheme rounded the switch track to a pill (`border-radius: var(--r-pill)` at App.css:4306, changed from 4px in this diff) and added `border-radius: 50%` to the thumb to match, but left the pre-existing `border-radius: 2px` on the next line, which wins. The shipped control is a pill track with a square thumb — the one shape mismatch in a retheme whose whole premise is pill-and-box consistency. This is also the only duplicate-property declaration in the entire 10,989-line stylesheet, so it is clearly an editing slip rather than an intended override.
findings.fix: Delete one of the two lines in src/App.css:4321-4322 — keep `50%` to finish the pill treatment, or delete it if the square thumb was the intent.

findings.title: The pill radius the retheme added to the session-detail filter toggle never applies
findings.impact: `.session-detail-filter-toggle` at L6973 and the RetroTheme rule at L10975 have identical specificity, so source order decides and the later `border-radius: 0` wins. The SHOW filter chips stay square while every other chip and control on the page went to `--r-pill` in this diff, and the declaration added at L6980 is dead. Anyone reading the first rule will believe the chips are pills. This is the class of bug the existing CSS gates cannot catch, because they assert App.css source text rather than computed style.
findings.fix: Decide the shape once: either delete `border-radius: var(--r-pill)` at src/App.css:6980, or drop `.session-detail-filter-toggle` from the RetroTheme rule at src/App.css:10975-10977 and leave only `.session-detail-filter-box` square.

findings.title: Scrollbar thumbs sit below the 3:1 floor in both themes, and unevenly between them
findings.impact: The 35% mix composites to #b4afaa on --bg-0 in light (2.11:1) and #5f5b53 in dark (2.82:1) — the same formula lands 33% further apart than it reads, because light's --accent is near-black on near-white and dark's is near-white on near-black. On a 6px-wide track that is a faint smudge; the hover state (3.32:1 light / 4.82:1 dark) is the only one that clears 3:1, and it is only reachable once the pointer is already on the bar. The prior tokens this replaced were worse in light (#d3d4d7 ≈ 1.4:1), so this is an improvement, not a regression — but it still leaves the only scroll-position affordance under the floor.
findings.fix: Raise the resting mix until it clears 3:1 on --bg-0 and --surface-card in both themes (roughly 50% light / 40% dark), or use two per-theme mix percentages rather than one shared value, since --accent's relationship to the paper is inverted between themes.

findings.title: The app paints the dark palette before the theme attribute is stamped, so light-theme users get a dark flash on every launch
findings.impact: index.html carries no theme attribute and no inline style; in a production build the stylesheet is a <link> in <head> that applies before the deferred module script executes, so the first painted frame uses the bare `:root` block — the dark palette — for every user whose choice or OS preference is light. main.tsx:7 then stamps `data-theme="light"` and `body`'s 180ms background-color transition (App.css:19-22) animates the whole window from near-black to cream. The comment at preferences.ts:74 ("Boot-time paint, before React mounts, so light mode does not flash dark") describes an outcome the current ordering cannot deliver.
findings.fix: Either add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` guard that redefines the palette on bare `:root`, or inline a tiny classic (non-module) script in index.html's <head> that reads localStorage `mallard.theme` and sets `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` before the stylesheet's first paint.

r.coverage:
WHAT I READ AND RAN

Source: the full `git diff HEAD -- src/App.css` (2,719 diff lines) hunk by hunk; the current src/App.css palette region (bare `:root` 7904-7981, dark `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` 7982-8193, light `:root[data-theme="light"]` 8094-8193) plus every rule I cite; the full component diffs for SyncPathBar.tsx (+217), SessionDetailEvent.tsx, sessionDetailModel.ts, ProjectSidebar.tsx, Icons.tsx, ProjectSync.tsx, ProjectActivityPage.tsx, types.ts; SyncPathBar.tsx in full for menu/focus behaviour; menuKeyboard.ts; SettingsPage.tsx (switch + theme segment); ProjectSidebar.tsx (profile warning glyph); ProjectActivityPage.tsx (indicator/metric tabIndex); ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx (crumb menu construction); preferences.ts, main.tsx, index.html; docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md; tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx and the three touched test files.

Measurement: I wrote a resolver/contrast/composite module in the scratchpad reusing the css-hygiene technique and extended it to handle `color-mix(in srgb|oklab, …)`, alpha compositing and `opacity` stacking, then ran (a) a token-parity diff of the three `:root` blocks, (b) contrast for every rule that declares `color` and `background` in the same block, (c) a sweep of every `color:` value in the file against all 15 opaque surface tokens in both themes, (d) targeted non-text pairs (borders, switch, focus rings, scrollbar, shadows, filter box), (e) an undeclared/unused `var()` audit, (f) a duplicate-declaration and same-selector-override scan. All ratios in the findings are computed, not estimated. I also ran `npx tsx --test tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx` (2/2 pass — the gated notice and badge sets are clean; my findings are all outside its coverage).

Two claims I verified in a real browser rather than by spec reasoning: the tool-row focus ring (rendered a 2px-border/2px-inset-outline/red-control comparison — case A is pixel-identical to unfocused) and the segmented-control clip (rendered overflow:hidden vs overflow:visible side by side).

WHAT I DID NOT CHECK

- Theme parity is clean at the token level: no token is defined for one theme and missing in the other except geometry (`--r`, `--r-pill`, `--retro-gutter*`, `--retro-panel-radius*`, `--button-radius`, `--retro-chevron-down`), which is correctly theme-invariant. No `var()` reference in the file is undeclared. Only four hardcoded colours exist outside the palette blocks (the modal backdrop scrim, App.css:10736-10739) and they are theme-neutral by construction.
- I did not run the app or drive the real UI — the running dev server at localhost:1420 was not exercised, so nothing here is a screenshot of the shipped screens; the two browser checks were isolated reductions of the exact CSS in question.
- Not covered: forced-colors / Windows high-contrast mode, macOS "Increase contrast", real Tauri focus behaviour, VoiceOver output, printed output, or the Baloo 2 webfont's actual rendering (I confirmed `font-display: block` at App.css:7885 and that public/fonts/Baloo2-Variable.woff2 exists and DepartureMono is fully unreferenced, but did not judge the FOIT window in a Tauri webview).
- Not covered: narrow-window layout, the log drawer, StorageCatalogPage / AddCatalogScopeWorkspace / RestorePlanView / ProjectFilesReviewPage internals beyond their colour tokens, and the Rust/tauri.conf changes in the same working tree.
- Deliberately excluded per the brief: src/*mockup*.tsx and the root *.html specimens. I confirmed none of them are imported by the production tree and that the classes the retheme touches are defined in App.css itself, so no mockup leaks in.
- One thing I checked and decided was not a finding: `.btn-primary { color: var(--text-0) }` at App.css:336 measures 3.10:1 (dark) / 3.30:1 (light) on its own fill, but every production call site uses `className="btn btn-primary"` so the higher-specificity `.btn.btn-primary { color: var(--button-primary-text) }` at App.css:8515 always wins (5.33:1 / 5.11:1). It is a latent trap, not a live defect.

findings.title: Pull review names every conversation "Conversation" instead of its session title, which the model already carries
findings.evidence: {item.title} {itemKindLabel(item)}{item.provider ? ` · ${providerLabel(item.provider)}` : ""}
findings.impact: Every conversation row in the Pull review reads "Conversation" in bold with "Conversation · Codex" directly beneath it. A user reviewing a pull of ten sessions sees ten identical rows and cannot tell which session each one is before applying. pullReviewModel.ts:273 already stores the real name (`item.threadTitle = row.display_title?.trim() ?? ""`), and syncOutcome.ts:174 uses it for the *after* receipt — so the same operation shows real names once it is too late to choose, and no names while choosing. The checkbox and disclosure accessible names at lines 210 and 222 inherit the same defect ("Select Conversation", "Show details for Conversation").
findings.fix: In RestorePlanView.tsx render `item.threadTitle || item.title` as the row's bold name (matching syncOutcome.ts's `nameFor`, which falls back through `displayThreadTitle` to "Untitled session"), and use the same value in the `aria-label`s at lines 210 and 222. Keep `itemKindLabel(item)` on the second line only.

findings.title: The Clear storage data confirmation names "Library", a product concept that no longer exists in the UI
findings.evidence: `Permanently clear all Mallard data from “${storageName}”?\n\nThis deletes every synced project repository and Library resource in this storage. It does not delete unrelated bucket/folder contents, local project files, provider sessions, or the storage connection. This cannot be undone.`,
findings.impact: This is the app's most destructive confirmation, and it is the only user-visible string anywhere in src/ that says "Library" (verified by grep: every other hit is a code comment or the HackerNoon icon credit). The feature is called Catalog on every screen — the sidebar section is "Catalog", the dialog is "Add Catalog resource", the other confirmation at line 1581 says "Remove the “X” row from the Catalog". A user about to irreversibly wipe a bucket is told it will delete "Library resources" and has no way to know that means their skills, plugins and pets.
findings.fix: Change "Library resource" to "Catalog resource" in ProjectSync.tsx:3242 so the sentence names the same thing the sidebar, the Add dialog and the Remove-row confirmation name.

findings.title: Push and Pull failures print raw Rust error strings containing Debug-formatted enum variants and action UUIDs
findings.evidence:
{error}
          </Notice>
findings.impact: `error` is the backend message verbatim. src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:9360 formats it as `"conversation Push action '{}' is stale at {:?}"`, so the review's danger banner reads e.g. "conversation Push action '0198f3a4-…' is stale at SemanticDigest" — a Rust enum variant Debug-printed and an internal action UUID. Sibling messages in the same file are just as raw: "…lost its descriptor" (service.rs:8402), "…has no publishable tail" (8835). syncError.ts:6 proves the frontend already recognises these exact strings (it greps for "stale at semanticdigest" and "recoveryblockedcorruption") yet passes them through unchanged. The user gets a code, no cause, and no next step beyond a bare "Reset local sync state" button whose relationship to the code is unexplained. RestorePlanView.tsx:484 (`message: error,`) has the identical problem on the Pull side.
findings.fix: Extend the storageError.ts pattern: add a `syncFailureMessage(error)` that maps the recognised shapes syncError.ts already matches to a cause-and-next-step sentence (e.g. "This session changed on disk while the review was open. Refresh the review and select it again." / "Mallard's local sync record for this project is inconsistent and cannot be repaired by retrying. Reset local sync state, then push again."), keep the raw text behind a "Details" disclosure, and route both PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:844 and RestorePlanView.tsx:484 through it.

findings.title: Path-bar switcher renders its action verbs as bare icons, including the destructive ones
findings.evidence: {item.icon && } {tail && {item.label}}
findings.impact: `renderPill(item, false)` is used for the first (unlabelled) menu group, so every crumb switcher's verbs lose their text. The project crumb footer becomes four unlabelled glyphs — folder, terminal, pencil, trash — where trash is "Reset local sync state…" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2418), which forgets sync bases, conversation mappings and saved plans. The Catalog row crumb becomes refresh/pencil/trash where trash is "Remove this Catalog row…" (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1311). The storage crumb becomes gear/link-off where link-off unlinks the storage. Worse, the folder glyph in the project footer means "Reveal in Finder" while the identical folder glyph on every switch-target row directly above it means "a project", so one open menu uses one glyph for two things. The `caption` at line 179 only prints verbs that have a `detail`, which in the project menu is exactly one of the four ("Agent profile · …"), so the single caption line appears to label the whole strip.
findings.fix: Render verbs with their label the way tails already do — drop the `tail &&` guard on the `<span>` in renderPill, or at minimum force it for `item.danger` items so destructive verbs are never icon-only. If the footer cannot fit four labels, move the danger verbs back into the list body as labelled rows.

findings.title: "Add storage…" degrades to an unlabelled + icon when the user has exactly one storage
findings.impact: The storage-editor crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707) builds its menu as `[ {label:"Switch to", …} (only if another storage exists), {items:[add-storage]} ]`. With one storage configured, the "Switch to" group is omitted, so `populated[0]` is the unlabelled add-storage group and it is classified as *verbs* rather than *tails* — rendering "Add storage…" as a bare `+` glyph with no visible text, and with `caption` empty because the item has no `detail`. A first-time user on their only storage page opens the switcher and sees a header row and one unexplained plus sign. With two or more storages the same item correctly renders as a labelled text pill, so the label appears and disappears depending on how many storages exist.
findings.fix: Classify by position among *groups*, not by whether group 0 happens to be unlabelled: treat the leading unlabelled group as verbs only when a labelled list group follows it (`populated.some(g => g.label)`), otherwise fall through to tails. Fixing the icon-only verb rendering (previous finding) also removes the visible symptom.

findings.title: The same pull action is called "session" on the chip and "task" in that chip's own tooltip
findings.impact: `pullOperationChip` (line 1036-1038) labels the very same decisions "Update session" and "Add session", and line 1257 renders that chip with `title={holdDetail ?? reviewStateLabel ?? undefined}` — i.e. the chip reads "Update session" and hovering it says "Update this task". "Publish new task" (line 1063) appears on Push rows in a list whose tab is titled "Sessions". "Task" is a fourth noun for an object the app already calls session, conversation and thread; nothing in the UI defines it, and a user cannot tell whether a "task" is the same object as the session on the row.
findings.fix: In `syncReviewStateLabel` replace "task" with "session": "Publish new session", "Update this session", "Create local session" — matching `pullOperationChip` above it and the "Sessions" tab label from reviewSteps.ts:18.

findings.title: One sentence in the repo-connection dialog uses "repository" and "repo" for two different objects
findings.evidence:
? "Connect to this repository's repo"
                : missing
                  ? "Choose the remote repo"
                  : "Choose a repo from this storage"}
findings.impact: The dialog heading asks the user to connect a Git repository to a Mallard repo, using the same word stem for both, with no cue which is which. The same object gets four spellings across the app: "Repositories" as the storage-page section crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1737), "Repository ID" as its detail label (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:411), "Repository" as the setup section heading (ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:887), and "Repo" in the binding editor (ProjectBindingEditor.tsx:295). terminology.ts exists precisely to normalise this (Bundle→Repo) but is only applied to backend error text and log lines (storageError.ts:13, LogPanel.tsx:125), never to authored UI copy. The prior audit filed this as M07; it is unchanged.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the Mallard-side object and use it everywhere authored copy appears — "sync repo" reads unambiguously next to Git. Rewrite line 99 as "Connect this Git repository to an existing sync repo", and align ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1737/411, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:887 and ProjectBindingEditor.tsx:295 to the same word.

findings.title: A Settings control labelled "Thread size limit" describes itself using two other nouns
findings.evidence: label="Thread size limit"
findings.impact: The row's own description immediately below (lines 476-477) reads "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read. Threads over the cap are skipped by compare, Push, and Pull." — so a two-sentence blurb uses "session transcript" and "Threads" for the thing the label calls a "Thread", while every list, tab and card in the app calls it a session. "Thread" is the internal wire noun (ThreadSyncEntry, thread_id) and appears nowhere the user can connect it to a session. A user setting this cannot tell whether it caps their Codex sessions or something else. "compare" in the same sentence names no control in the UI (the affordance is "Refresh") and is lowercase beside title-cased Push and Pull.
findings.fix: Rename the label and its aria-label (line 464) to "Session size limit" and rewrite the description as "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read. Sessions over the cap are skipped when comparing, pushing and pulling."

findings.title: Stored-session checkboxes announce "thread" plus a raw internal id, while identical local rows announce a session title
findings.evidence: const identityLabel = `${title}, ${entry.provider_display_name} thread ${entry.thread_id}`;
findings.impact: This string is both the checkbox `aria-label` and its hover `title` (lines 1393 and 1398), so a screen-reader user selecting a stored session hears "Include Untitled thread, Codex thread 0198f3a4-4d2c-7f5e-b8a1-9c0d2e4f6a7b" and a mouse user gets the same UUID in a tooltip. Local session rows in the same list use `session.title || "Untitled session"` (line 1206) with no id and no "thread". Two rows sitting next to each other in one list therefore use different nouns and different amounts of internal detail for the same kind of object, and the stored row's fallback name is "Untitled thread" (line 1377) where the local row's is "Untitled session" (line 1164).
findings.fix: Build the stored row's identity label the same way as the local one: `${title}, ${entry.provider_display_name} session`, dropping `entry.thread_id`; and change the fallback at line 1377 from "Untitled thread" to "Untitled session" so both lists agree.

findings.title: The new capture-budget message says "conversations" in Push review and "sessions" in the activity list for the same blocker
findings.evidence:
title: `${capturePendingCount} conversation${capturePendingCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} wait for the next round`,
      message: "This review's 512 MB capture budget filled before their turn. Push the selected conversations first, then open Push review again.",
findings.impact: Both of these strings are new in the working tree and describe the identical `capture_budget` blocker. ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1120 renders the per-row version as "Not in this round — the review's 512 MB capture budget filled before this session's turn. Push the selected sessions first, then open Push review again." The banner sits directly above the rows that carry the per-row text, inside a tab titled "Sessions" (reviewSteps.ts:18), so a user reads a banner about "conversations" and rows about "sessions" and has to guess they are the same set. PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:136 makes it worse inside one sentence: "…conversations are newer in X. Review them in Pull — they stay held afterwards while your other sessions push."

findings.title: Hovering the active primary-nav destination erases its selected state: the ink edge and the fill both drop out
findings.impact: `:hover:not(:disabled)` is (0,3,1); `.active` is (0,2,1), so hover wins regardless of order. Verified by computed style (`:hover` rewritten to an equal-weight class): the active row's border goes from rgb(239,231,212) (`--accent`, cream) to rgb(46,41,37) (`--border`, all but invisible on the dark rail) and its background from rgb(39,35,30) to rgba(255,238,217,0.067). Only the 2px cast shadow survives, so the current section reads as an unframed row with a shadow floating beside it. The retheme caused this: at HEAD the same defeat swapped `--border-mid` for `--border` — two quiet neutrals — whereas it now swaps the highest-contrast ink in the palette for the lowest. `.sidebar-profile-item` right below it (L8815/L8820) is written correctly at equal specificity, which is the proof this one is an accident.
findings.fix: In src/App.css raise the active rule above hover, e.g. change L8734 to `.sync-primary-nav button.active, .sync-primary-nav button.active:hover:not(:disabled)`, or scope hover with `.sync-primary-nav button:hover:not(:disabled):not(.active)`.

findings.title: Hovering the open Push/Pull button strips its primary fill, so the "this review is open" signal disappears under the cursor
findings.impact: `.sync-path-sync.active` is applied while a Push or Pull review is open (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2613 and :2665). The hover rule at L2868 is (0,3,0) against the active rule's (0,2,0), so hover wins. Measured: active-not-hovered renders background rgb(173,128,90) with rgb(22,18,16) ink (the caramel primary); active-and-hovered renders background rgb(39,34,29) with rgb(239,231,212) ink — i.e. an ordinary button. Because the pointer is on the button immediately after the click that opened the review, the lit state is invisible exactly when the user looks for confirmation. The retheme touched both rules in this diff (it removed `border-color` from each), so the active state now hangs entirely on a background the hover rule overwrites.
findings.fix: In src/App.css scope the hover rule at L2868 as `.sync-path-sync:hover:not(:disabled):not(.active)` and add a dedicated `.sync-path-sync.active:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--button-primary-hover); color: var(--button-primary-text); }`.

findings.title: Duplicate `border-radius` in the settings switch thumb: the retheme's pill is defeated one line later by the old 2px square
findings.impact: The retheme rounded the switch track to `var(--r-pill)` (L4308, verified computed as 999px) and added `border-radius: 50%` to the thumb, but left the old `border-radius: 2px` on the next line, which wins. Computed `::before` border-radius is 2px. Every toggle on the Settings page therefore renders a stadium track with a near-square 12px block sliding inside it — the one control in the app whose two halves disagree about the retheme's corner language. This is the only duplicated property in any block in the whole 10989-line file, so it is plainly an unfinished edit.
findings.fix: In src/App.css delete the `border-radius: 2px;` on L4322, leaving the `border-radius: 50%;` on L4321.

findings.title: The switcher menu has no max-height or scroll, and the retheme moved its verbs into a footer that a long list pushes off-screen
findings.impact: No `max-height` and no `overflow` on `.sync-path-menu` (verified: computed `overflow: visible`, `max-height: none`), while `html, body, #root { overflow: hidden }` at App.css:7-11 means anything past the window bottom is unreachable by pointer. The project switcher lists every other project unbounded (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2360 `projects.filter(...)`). Measured at the app's minimum window (800×560 per tauri.conf.json) with 19 targets: menu top y=95, height 813px, bottom 908px — 9 rows below the fold, plus the entire footer. The retheme made this materially worse in two ways: rows went from ~31px to a 34px `min-height` (L3099), and `.sync-path-menu-foot` (L3212) is now the LAST child, so the verbs ("Storage settings…", "Unlink…") and the tails ("Link storage…", "Add storage…") — which rendered as the FIRST group before this change — are the first things scrolled out of existence. Chrome measures 166.7px, so any switcher with 9 or more targets loses content at the minimum window size.
findings.fix: In src/App.css give `.sync-path-menu` a bounded scroll body: add `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px)` and put the switcher's list groups in their own `overflow-y: auto` region so `.sync-path-menu-current`, `.sync-path-menu-search` and `.sync-path-menu-foot` stay pinned while only the target rows scroll.

findings.title: Tool-call action labels dropped to 9px uppercase and fail 4.5:1 on the expanded row in the light theme
findings.impact: The retheme took the tool row's primary identifier from `--type-sm` (12px, sentence case, sans) to `--type-3xs` (9px, uppercase, mono with 1px tracking). Measured contrast against the real stylesheet in the light theme on an expanded row (`.session-detail-tool-call[open] > summary` background `--surface-row-active` = rgb(240,227,213)): `cat-read` labels render rgb(44,119,156) at 3.94:1 and `cat-file_edit` rgb(142,100,15) at 4.18:1 — both under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA floor for text this size, and 9px leaves no headroom for the shortfall. (Closed rows measure 4.74 / 5.03:1 and pass; the dark theme passes everywhere at 8.8–12.6:1.) A user reading a session transcript in light mode cannot reliably tell READ from EDIT rows once a call is expanded.
findings.fix: In src/App.css either raise `.session-detail-tool-name` back to `--type-xs`/`--type-sm` at L7599, or darken the two light-theme mixes so they clear 4.5:1 on `--surface-row-active` — e.g. give `--session-detail-link` and `--session-detail-amber` light-theme overrides in the `:root[data-theme="light"]` block (they are currently only declared once, at L6850-6851, tuned for the page background rather than the expanded row).

findings.title: Session titles and commit subjects were moved to a display face whose bundled subset has no Latin-Extended, Cyrillic or CJK coverage
findings.impact: The retheme switched two user-data nodes from `--font-sans` to `--font-display` (this rule, and `.sync-history-commit-heading strong` at L5171). The bundled `public/fonts/Baloo2-Variable.woff2` is a 33KB subset; loaded in a browser and probed character by character it covers Latin-1 and part of Latin-Ext (é ü ñ ß ć ā — and the chrome punctuation — · … ’ “ ”) but NOT Ł ę ř İ, any Cyrillic, or any CJK. Session titles and git commit subjects come straight out of the user's own prompts and repository, so a title like "Fix ł escape" renders most of its glyphs in Baloo 2 and one from a fallback face mid-word, and a Russian or Chinese title silently drops to a completely different typeface beside its English neighbours in the same list. All app-authored chrome strings were checked and are fully covered, so only these two user-data selectors are exposed.
findings.fix: In src/App.css revert `.sync-history-thread-title > strong` (L9638) and `.sync-history-commit-heading strong` (L5175) to `font-family: var(--font-sans)`, keeping the display face for chrome only — or re-subset Baloo2-Variable.woff2 with Latin-Extended coverage and accept that non-Latin scripts still fall back.

findings.title: `--button-primary-border` is declared in both themes but no longer referenced anywhere
findings.impact: The retheme removed all three consumers (`.btn-primary` L328 at HEAD, `.sync-path-sync.active`, and the RetroTheme `.btn.btn-primary`) when it made every box draw its edge from `--box-border`, but left the token declared at L8011 (dark) and L8120 (light). A maintainer editing the primary-button palette will change a value that paints nothing, and the file's own comment claims it is "the palette's single source of truth". Verified by a full declaration-vs-`var()` census: this is the only token the cutover newly orphaned (the other six unused tokens were already dead at HEAD).
findings.fix: Delete `--button-primary-border` from both palette blocks in src/App.css (L8011 and L8120).

findings.title: Departure Mono is still shipped in public/fonts but no production code references it any more
findings.impact: This `@font-face` replaced the Departure Mono one, and `--font-pixel` is gone from the file, but `public/fonts/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2` (22KB) and `DepartureMono-OFL.txt` remain in the bundle. Grepping the production tree finds no remaining reference — the only consumer left is the untracked specimen `codex-retheme-mockup.html` at the repo root. The 22KB rides in every shipped build and the OFL notice now attributes a font the app does not use, which is a licensing-manifest inaccuracy as well as dead weight.
findings.fix: Delete public/fonts/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2 and public/fonts/DepartureMono-OFL.txt once codex-retheme-mockup.html is either updated or removed; keep Baloo2-OFL.txt, which is now the live attribution.

findings.evidence:

findings.impact: There is no way at all to delete a file or folder from a storage repository. A user who pushes a file by mistake (a secret, a large binary, a stale folder) can never remove it through the app: the per-card trash button is unreachable, `pushProjectContentRemovals` in ProjectSync.tsx is only ever assigned `new Set()` (lines 849, 1815, 2102, 2127, 3400, 3444, 3451), and `publishPendingPush` therefore always posts an empty `project_content_removal_ids` to a backend that still accepts them. Everything downstream is silently inert: the Push footer's impact bar always reads "0 Delete files · 0 Delete folders", the H06 deletion-acknowledgement checkbox (`deletionTarget="storage"`) can never appear, and the `catalog-card removal` / "Removes from storage" states are unreachable. `git show c002338 -- src/components/project-sync/PushResourceWorkspace.tsx` shows the line `-              onToggleRemoval={onToggleProjectContentRemoval}` was deleted along with the whole prop, while every consumer of it was left standing — this is a dropped wire, not a cutover. The frontend suite stays green because tests/frontend/project-files.integration.test.tsx:262 and :377 pass `onToggleRemoval` / `projectContentRemovals` straight into the child components, so no gate exercises the shell wiring.
findings.fix: Restore the `onToggleProjectContentRemoval` prop on PushResourceWorkspace (Props interface + destructure) and pass `onToggleRemoval={onToggleProjectContentRemoval}` at src/components/project-sync/PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:820, wiring it in ProjectSync.tsx beside `onToggleProjectContentWarning` (line 3434) to a `setPushProjectContentRemovals` toggle. Add a shell-level test that renders PushResourceWorkspace from ProjectSync's props and asserts the `Remove … from storage` button exists, so the wire cannot be dropped again silently.

findings.title: Catalog Pull tells the user "nothing was changed" on failure paths that run after every selected resource has already been overwritten on disk
findings.impact: The frontend asserts a fact it cannot know. In src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/service.rs the apply loop (line ~2005) writes every selected resource to the provider home and collects per-item outcomes as *results*, not errors; only afterwards does `catalog.mutate_scope_links(...)?` run (line 2049) and propagate an `Err` — "the scope link disappeared while accepting Pull", "the scope link changed while accepting Pull", or any IO failure persisting the links document. On that path the user's local skills/pets/plugins have already been replaced by the stored versions (including the `requires_destructive_approval` overwrites they just approved on the ack chips), the review closes, and the toast says nothing was changed — so the user has no reason to look for damage or restore the preserved copies. The identical false claim exists on the Push side at line 1069 ("Push failed — nothing was published."), where `engine.publish(...)` at service.rs:1729 has already advanced the storage revision before the same `mutate_scope_links` can fail.
findings.fix: Stop asserting a rollback the caller cannot verify. Have `apply_catalog_scope_pull` / `apply_catalog_scope_push` return a structured failure that distinguishes "refused before any write" (all the pre-flight `return Err` guards) from "failed after applying", and make StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1150 and :1069 render the neutral "Pull couldn't finish — check the results below" plus the per-item outcomes in that second case. At minimum, change both strings to name the uncertainty ("Pull failed — some items may already have been applied; refresh to compare").

findings.title: The path-bar Push button commits the review without the project-file deletion acknowledgement the footer Push requires
findings.evidence:

      || pendingPushBlockingCount > 0

// contrast with the Pull review two hundred lines below, which does propagate its gate:
    continueDisabled: !pullReviewPrimary || pullReviewPrimary.disabledReason !== null,
findings.impact: While a Push review is open, the path-bar Push button is the review's primary — `onContinue` calls `publishPendingPush()` directly (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2674) — but it is gated by a different, weaker predicate than the footer button. `pushReviewBlockers` explicitly skips removals (`if (projectContentRemovals.has(resourceId)) continue;`, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:190), so `pendingPushBlockingCount` is 0 for a selection whose only content is deletions. The footer Push is disabled with title "Approve the selected project file deletions" (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:612); the path-bar Push, two rows above it on the same screen, is live and deletes the files from storage with the acknowledgement checkbox still unticked. The deletion state lives in `useState` inside PushResourceWorkspace (line 491) and is never lifted, so the shell structurally cannot see it. This is masked today only because the removal control itself is unreachable (finding 1) — restoring that wire makes this bypass live immediately, and it defeats the H06 repair it was built to enforce.
findings.fix: Mirror the Pull pattern: add an `onPrimaryChange`-style callback to PushResourceWorkspace that reports its computed `pushDisabledReason` upward, and set `continueDisabled` / `continueTitle` at ProjectSync.tsx:3393 from that single value instead of recomputing a subset of the gates in the shell.

findings.title: The irreversible "Clear storage data" confirmation uses the default info dialog, so Return confirms the wipe on a button labelled "Ok"
findings.impact: node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog/dist-js/index.js:199 shows that omitting `okLabel`/`cancelLabel` produces the plain `OkCancel` button pair and that `kind` defaults to `info`. The single most destructive remote action in the app — deleting every synced project repository and Library resource from an R2 bucket or backup folder, with no undo — therefore presents an informational-icon dialog whose default (Return-activated) button reads "Ok", identical in weight to a routine confirmation. The app already knows the safe pattern and uses it three rows away: SettingsPage.tsx:213 and :258 pass `{ kind: "warning", okLabel: "Delete logs" / "Reset Mallard", cancelLabel: "Cancel" }` for strictly smaller consequences. The same weak form is used for every other destructive confirm outside SettingsPage: unlinkStorage (2843), removeProject (2640), removeCatalogScope (1582), resetProjectSyncMetadata (2679), removeStorage (3290), and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1160. The dialog also never names how many repositories or resources will be destroyed, though the storage page has just listed them.
findings.fix: Pass `{ title: "Clear storage data", kind: "warning", okLabel: "Clear storage data", cancelLabel: "Cancel" }` at ProjectSync.tsx:3243 and apply the same three-key form to the other destructive `confirm` calls listed above. Feed the loaded repository count into the message so the dialog names the specific items ("…deletes 4 project repositories and 12 Library resources from “Team bucket”").

findings.title: The new path-bar switcher menus render destructive commands as unlabelled icon pills
findings.impact: Every crumb menu that carries a `menuHeader` becomes a "switcher", and its first unlabelled group — the object's verbs — is rendered as 32×32 icon-only pills (App.css:3236-3274: `min-width: 32px; padding: 0`, and only `.sync-path-menu-verb.danger { color: var(--danger-text) }` to tell them apart). Before this working-tree change every one of these was a full-width labelled row. The result is that the project crumb now shows four bare glyphs — folder, terminal, pencil, trash — where the trash is "Reset local sync state…" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2417) sitting 8px from the pencil that is "Rename project…"; the storage crumb reduces "Unlink from <project>…" to a bare link-off glyph (line 2283); the Catalog row crumb reduces "Remove this Catalog row…" to a bare trash beside "Rename profile…" (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1310). The only text is a hover tooltip, and the one `.sync-path-menu-cap` caption line is spent on the Agent profile item because it happens to be the only verb with a `detail`. A user picking "rename" from a four-icon row and hitting the neighbouring glyph lands in a wipe confirmation instead. The switch targets below, which are not destructive, keep their full text labels.
findings.fix: In `renderPill` (SyncPathBar.tsx:223) render `{item.label}` for verbs too, or at minimum for any item with `danger: true`, and let `.sync-path-menu-verbs` wrap. If the icon cluster is kept for the safe verbs, move every `danger` item out of the footer strip and back into a labelled row (`renderItem`) below a separator.

findings.title: Dead "Remove storage" trash button in the storage editor header
findings.impact: `onRemove` is declared on `StorageEditor` (line 162) but is never passed by any caller: the only production mount is ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1935, whose prop list runs to line 2104 without it, and `grep -rn "onRemove=" src/ tests/` returns nothing. The destructive control in the storage editor header therefore never renders, and App.css:2069 (`.sync-storage-card > header .danger`) styles an element that cannot exist. A maintainer reading StorageSettings.tsx reasonably concludes the editor offers a Remove action; it does not, and removal is only reachable from the sidebar row and the path-bar overflow menu.
findings.fix: Either delete the `onRemove` prop, the button at StorageSettings.tsx:273-275, and the App.css:2069 rule, or pass `onRemove={() => onRemoveStorage(editedStorageConfig.id)}` at the ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1935 mount so the header action matches the overflow menu's "Remove storage…" item.

findings.title: Dead "clear" button in LogPanel — its render branch is mutually exclusive with a required prop
findings.impact: `onManage` is a required (non-optional) prop of ActivityLogDrawer (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:50) and is always forwarded to LogPanel (line 215), and ProjectSync.tsx:3884 always supplies it. `!onManage` is therefore never true in production, so the log-clear affordance and its App.css:555 `.log-clear-btn` rule are unreachable code. Nothing is broken for the user, but the file reads as if the drawer can clear its own log when the only clearing path is Settings → Logs → "Delete all retained activity logs".
findings.fix: Delete the `onClear` prop, the branch at LogPanel.tsx:323-327, and the `.log-clear-btn` rule in src/App.css:555.

findings.impact: The new `comparison-failed` banner (added in this working tree) puts a plain ghost button on the same action that the push-error notice presents as a red, trash-marked destructive button. r.coverage:
Lens: destructive and irreversible actions, verified against the dirty working tree on 789eea5.

Read in full or in the relevant region: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx (selection sanitizing, pushReviewBlockers/BlockingCount, pushProjectFileCommitImpact, banners, footer, ProjectFilesReviewPage mount), ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx (whole file), ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx (rowIsSelectable, subtreeSelection/setSubtree, renderTileHead, renderCard, pullOperationLabel, rowPresentation), RestorePlanView.tsx (pullProjectFileCommitImpact, deletionSignature, primaryDisabledReason, onPrimaryChange, footer, banners), ProjectSync.tsx (all 16 confirm() call sites, publishPendingPush, publishProject, applyReview, clearStorageData, removeStorage, removeProject, removeCatalogScope, resetProjectSyncMetadata, unlinkStorage, discard*Draft, repairConversationPaths, inlineStorageReview for push and pull), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx (storagePathOverflow, storageMenu, project crumb menu, path-bar Push/Pull action group, storageActionLockedForReview, gate notices, StorageEditor mount), StorageCatalogPage.tsx (openPull/runPull/openPush/runPush, unlinkStorage, pull ack chips + needsAck + pullReviewBlocked, path-bar crumbs and Sync actions, selection bars), SettingsPage.tsx (cleanupLogs, resetMallard, SettingsRow, Local data group), StorageSettings.tsx (StorageEditor props + header), SyncPathBar.tsx (whole PathBarMenu incl. the new switcher branch, renderItem/renderPill, keyboard handler), menuKeyboard.ts, ProjectSidebar.tsx (remove buttons), LogPanel.tsx + ActivityLogDrawer.tsx, ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx, pullReviewModel.ts (preserve/local-copy path), ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx header comment.

Backend cross-checks (read-only) for claims the frontend makes about rollback: src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/service.rs apply_pull_with_repositories (1911-2070) and apply_push_with_repositories (1637-1780), src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/resource_commands.rs. Whether Catalog Pull items can exist with actions but no default_action_id — which would let a selected-but-unchosen row be silently dropped by runPull while still counting in the header — depends on backend plan shape I could not confirm, so it is not reported.
