findings.title: M10 (still open, now a safety bypass) — the path-bar Push commits the review, skipping the deletion acknowledgement the footer enforces
findings.impact: With project-file deletions selected in a Push review, the footer Push is correctly disabled with title "Approve the selected project file deletions" (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:612), but the path-bar Push button — visible at the same time, above the review (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2727 renders SyncPathBar, :3228 renders the review below it) — calls publishPendingPush() directly. pushReviewBlockers (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:169-212) never considers deletions, and deletionApproved is local state inside PushResourceWorkspace with no callback out. So one click on the path-bar Push deletes the selected files and folders from storage with the acknowledgement checkbox still unticked. The Pull side does not have this hole: RestorePlanView publishes its gate through onPrimaryChange (RestorePlanView.tsx:393-397) and ProjectSync.tsx:3475 consumes it — the asymmetry confirms this is an oversight, not a design choice. tests/frontend/project-files.integration.test.tsx:389-390 asserts only the footer markup, so nothing catches it.
findings.fix: Give PushResourceWorkspace the same `onPrimaryChange` contract RestorePlanView has: lift `pushDisabledReason` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:608-616, including the deletionApproved clause) out to ProjectSync and use it for `inlineStorageReview.continueDisabled` and `continueTitle`. Also reset `deletionApproved` whenever `projectContentRemovals` changes, so an approval of 2 deletions cannot carry over to a later selection of 40.

findings.title: H02 (still open) — portalled details popovers still never receive focus, so their copy actions are unreachable by keyboard
findings.impact: All three popovers — file details (ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:118), session debug info (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:912), Catalog paths-and-digests (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:289-293) — open without moving focus into the panel, and the panel <div role="dialog"> has no tabIndex so it is not focusable. Because TopLayer portals the panel to the end of document.body, the next Tab from the trigger lands on the following control in the row, which is outside both rootRef and panelRef, and the focusin handler immediately closes the popover. A keyboard-only user can open these panels but can never reach any Copy button inside them — the panel's entire content is unreachable. aria-controls and the polite copy-result status were added since the prior audit, but the focus defect is unchanged.
findings.fix: On open, move focus to the panel (add tabIndex={-1} to the role="dialog" div and focus it in an effect) or to its first copy button, in all three components. Only arm the focusin dismissal after focus has entered the panel, and restore focus to the trigger on close.

findings.title: M04 (still open) — the two custom focus rings are still translucent and fall below 3:1
findings.impact: Both selectors set `outline: none` (App.css:5215 and 5367) and replace it with a translucent ring. Composited against the surfaces they sit on, the sync indicator's 35% ring measures 2.85:1 in dark and 2.12:1 in light; the metric's 45% ring measures 3.91:1 in dark but 2.72:1 in light. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for focus indicators. Every one of these elements is tabbable (tabIndex={0} on the metric chips, e.g. ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:225, 234, 255), so a keyboard user tabbing through an activity row in light mode cannot see where focus is. The css-hygiene gate measures notice fills and status badges but not focus rings, so nothing catches this.
findings.fix: Drop the `outline: none` at App.css:5215 and 5367 and let the global 2px `--accent` outline (App.css:38-44) apply, or raise the color-mix to an opaque replacement that measures ≥3:1 on --surface-row, --surface-row-hover and --surface-card in both themes. Extend the css-hygiene contrast gate to cover focus-indicator tokens so it cannot regress silently.

findings.title: M02 (still open) — five role="radio" groups still implement no radio keyboard behaviour
findings.evidence:

findings.impact: AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905/937, StorageSettings.tsx:230, and SettingsPage.tsx:391 all declare role="radiogroup" with role="radio" buttons. None has a roving tabIndex and none has an onKeyDown — grep for ArrowRight/ArrowLeft across these five files returns nothing. A screen-reader user is told "radio group, 1 of 3" and presses Arrow keys as the pattern requires; nothing happens. findings.title: M03 (still open) — three menu-button patterns still open without moving focus, and the path-bar menu closes on Tab
findings.impact: Activating a path-bar crumb menu with Enter or Space opens it but leaves focus on the trigger (only ArrowDown/ArrowUp call focusMenuOption, lines 555-558). Because the same handler closes the menu on Tab, a user who opens a menu the ordinary way and then presses Tab loses it — the only way in is an Arrow key they have no cue to press. The app-actions menu (ProjectSync.tsx:2764-2801) and the R2 agent-setup split menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2032-2077) are worse: neither moves focus on open, neither supports Arrow/Home/End at all, and their Escape handlers (ProjectSync.tsx:1318-1324, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278-1282) close the menu without restoring focus to the trigger.
findings.fix: Call focusMenuOption(crumb.id, "first") from the click handler in SyncPathBar too, and stop swallowing Tab as a close (let it move focus into the menu, or close and let the browser continue past the trigger). Port SyncPathBar's PathBarMenu — which already has moveMenuFocus, typeahead and focus return — over the app-actions and agent-setup menus instead of maintaining three patterns.

findings.title: M01 (still open) — the Logs resize separator is still mouse-only and 16px thick
findings.evidence:
<div
          className="log-resizer"
          role="separator"
          aria-label="Resize log"
          aria-orientation="horizontal"
          onMouseDown={onStartResize}
          onDoubleClick={onResetHeight}
        />
findings.impact: The separator has no tabIndex, no aria-valuemin/max/now and no onKeyDown, so a keyboard or switch user cannot resize the Logs drawer at all and a screen reader announces a separator with no value. The sidebar separator three components away (ProjectSync.tsx:3695-3709) already implements the full contract — tabIndex={0}, the three value attributes, pointer events and resizeSidebarWithKeyboard — so the correct pattern exists in the codebase and was simply not applied here. The pointer target is also thin: App.css:10601-10603 sets `height: calc(var(--retro-gutter) + 8px)` with --retro-gutter: 8px, giving a 16px drag strip, under the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum.
findings.fix: Reuse the sidebar separator's props verbatim in ActivityLogDrawer: tabIndex={0}, aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow off the drawer height bounds, onKeyDown with Arrow Up/Down + Home/End, and pointer events instead of mouse events. Raise the strip to at least 24px of hit area while keeping the 4px visible pill.

findings.title: M05 (still open) — four main views have no h1, no view has aria-current, and no route updates the window title
findings.evidence:
<main className="sync-main sync-project-links-page sync-settings-page">
        <section className="profile-links-section" aria-label="Settings">

          <section className="sync-settings-group" aria-labelledby="settings-appearance">
            <h2 className="settings-section-title" id="settings-appearance">
findings.impact: Settings, StorageIndexPage, StorageCatalogPage and CatalogIndexPage contain no <h1> — Settings jumps straight to seven h2 sections, so a screen-reader user navigating by heading level finds no page title and cannot tell which page they landed on. `grep -rn aria-current src/components/` returns only SyncPathBar, so the sidebar's selected project, storage and Catalog rows and the five primary-nav destinations convey "current" through `className="active"` alone (ProjectSidebar.tsx:709-751) — invisible to assistive technology. `grep -rn "document.title" src/` returns nothing, so the window title never changes across the entire app.
findings.fix: Add one h1 per main view (visually hidden where the path bar already shows the name), set aria-current="page" on the active .sync-primary-nav button and aria-current="true" on the selected sidebar row, and set document.title from the same state that drives the path-bar crumbs.

findings.title: M06 (still open) — R2 setup still blocks Test and Finish without saying which field is wrong
findings.evidence:
<input
                value={storage.bucket ?? ""}
                onChange={(event) => set({ bucket: event.target.value })}
                placeholder="Example: codex-sync-backups"
                disabled={disabled}
                required
findings.impact: storageConfigReady (StorageSettings.tsx:104-114) requires isCloudflareR2BucketName(bucket), isCloudflareR2AccountId(accountId), and endpoint.accountId === accountId. Only the S3 API URL exposes aria-invalid (line 357); bucket, account ID, access key and secret carry no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby and no error text. Both the "Test connection" and "Finish setup" buttons (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2185 and 2194) gate on `!storageReady` with no title attribute giving a reason. A user who types a bucket name with an underscore, or an account ID of the wrong length, sees two dead buttons and no indication anywhere on the page of which of five fields is at fault.
findings.fix: Validate bucket, account ID and access key on blur; set aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at a per-field message with the expected format. Add a title/disabled-reason on the Test and Finish buttons naming the first unsatisfied requirement, the way pushDisabledReason already does in PushResourceWorkspace.

findings.title: M08 (still open) — three entry-failure states render an error with no Retry, and the Files scan error hides its own rescan
findings.impact: The component receives an `onRescan` prop (line 274) and renders a Rescan button for it — but only inside the success branch, guarded by `fileEntries.length > 0` (line 350). On a scan failure the error branch returns before that, so the page shows an error box and nothing else; the only way to retry is the unlabelled refresh glyph in the path bar (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2592-2608). The same pattern repeats in ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:541-560 (draft-load failure renders a Notice and no other control at all) and AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:344-354 (mount listing failure renders a Notice with no Retry, and there is no initial loading state — the form renders with an empty provider list while the fetch is in flight).
findings.fix: Render the Rescan button inside the error branch of ProjectFilesActivityPage (it already has onRescan in scope). Add a Retry action to the ProjectSetupWorkspace draft-load Notice and to the AddCatalogScopeWorkspace mount-failure Notice, plus an explicit loading state for the latter — SettingsPage.tsx:296-307 already has the exact Notice-with-Retry recipe to copy.

findings.title: M13 (still open) — clipped root overflow, a fixed 220px sidebar floor and fixed-pixel control heights still break text-resize reflow
findings.impact: Root and .sync-app (App.css:804-811) both clip overflow, so anything that outgrows the viewport is unreachable rather than scrollable. MIN_PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH is a hard 220px (ProjectSync.tsx:189) and App.css:10855-10856 states outright "The sidebar has no responsive size step" — at the 800px window floor the sidebar takes 27% of the width regardless of text size. Text-bearing controls keep fixed pixel heights against rem-based type: .sync-primary-nav button is `height: 38px` with `font-size: var(--type-md)` (App.css:8708-8719) and .sync-segmented button is `height: 25px` with `font-size: var(--type-2xs)` (App.css:2071). At the 200% OS text setting the segmented control's label renders ~27px tall in a 25px box and the nav labels fill their box edge to edge; at 400% zoom both clip, with no scroll path out because of the root clip.
findings.fix: Convert the fixed `height` on .sync-primary-nav button, .sync-segmented button and the other 27 fixed-height text controls to `min-height` so they grow with their content. Give .sync-app a scroll path (overflow: auto on the workspace column) instead of clipping at the root, and add a narrow/large-text mode that collapses the sidebar automatically rather than relying on the user finding the toggle.

findings.title: M11 (still open) — the session title lives only in the path bar and truncates to 6 characters at the narrow floor
findings.evidence: {title}
findings.impact: The only visible session title is the path bar's leaf crumb. Under the retheme's container queries that crumb is capped at `max-width: 9ch` below 760px and `max-width: 6ch` below 640px (App.css:3025-3030 and 3046-3052), and .sync-path-crumb > span sets overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis (App.css:2644-2649). At the documented 580px pathbar floor (800px window less the 220px sidebar) the page's only title reads as roughly "Fix a…" — the retheme made this worse than the prior audit found it. The provider-launch and open-in-terminal actions are still icon-only at every width (lines 95-111), identifiable only by tooltip.
findings.fix: Render the visible title in the content area of SessionDetailHeader (drop sync-visually-hidden from the h1, or add a visible title row) so the truncated crumb is a location marker rather than the only name. Show the action labels beside their glyphs above the 760px container step.

findings.title: M12 (still open) — 9px and 10px type still carries meaningful content across 91 selectors
findings.impact: Body text is --type-md = 13px (App.css:8203-8205). --type-3xs resolves to 9px at the default root and is used in 26 selectors, --type-2xs to 10px in 65 more. These are not decorative marks: App.css:1740 sets .sync-bundle-context small to 9px monospace for a repo identifier, :1727 sets bundle-choice metadata to 9px, :2079 sets the R2 form's field names to 9px uppercase, and :1459 sets .sync-fact-grid dt labels to 9px. At 9px a monospace identifier is at the edge of legibility on a standard display and the reading cost compounds with the muted --text-3/--text-2 these selectors also use.
findings.fix: Retire --type-3xs for anything a user has to read and set an 11px (--type-xs) floor for metadata, identifiers, counts and field names. Keep 9-10px only for short non-essential marks, and recheck the affected rows' line-height and wrapping after the bump.

findings.title: M14 (still open) — delayed loading content is still a named region, never announced
findings.evidence:
<div
      className="loading-scaffold"
      role="region"
      aria-label={label}
    >
      <div className="loading-scaffold-caption">
        <span className="status-loader" /> {label}…
findings.impact: After the 150ms gate the scaffold inserts a named region, which is discoverable by landmark navigation but is not announced when it appears. Combined with M05 — no route change moves focus to a heading and no route updates the window title — a screen-reader user who clicks a project, a Catalog scope or a storage gets no signal that anything happened until the content lands. `grep -rn aria-busy src/components/` shows aria-busy is used on five inner elements but never on the main region that the scaffold replaces.
findings.fix: Keep the named region and add a sibling role="status" that announces the label once for user-initiated loads, plus aria-busy on the enclosing <main>/<section> for the duration of the load.

findings.title: M07 (still open) — "repo" names both a Git repository and a Mallard identity in one sentence, and Settings swaps thread for session mid-description
findings.evidence:
? "Connect to this repository's repo"
                : missing
                  ? "Choose the remote repo"
                  : "Choose a repo from this storage"}
findings.impact: "Connect to this repository's repo" is unparseable without knowing that Mallard's sync identity is internally a bundle renamed to "repo" by terminology.ts:1-6 while "repository" means the Git checkout. The same dialog then says "already has this repository in another repo" (line 106) and "Create separate repo" (line 170). Settings has the parallel problem: the row is labelled "Thread size limit" (SettingsPage.tsx:455) and described as "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read. Threads over the cap are skipped" (line 476), while eighty lines later "Worker threads that scan and compare local sessions" (line 531) uses "threads" in the OS sense — three meanings for two words on one page.
findings.fix: Say "Git repository" for the checkout and pick one distinct noun for the Mallard identity ("sync repository" or keep "repo" but never in the same sentence as "repository"). Standardise on "session" for provider activity everywhere the user sees it, and rename the Performance rows to "Session size limit" and "Scan workers".

findings.title: M15 (still open) — the fresh-install main pane still has no first action, and names Codex on a two-provider app
findings.evidence:
Project history

Select a completed project to view its Codex history.
findings.impact: On a fresh install this is the entire content of the dominant pane: an instruction to select something that does not exist, and no button. The three "Add your first…" actions are in the sidebar, which the user may have collapsed. The copy also hardcodes "Codex" even though the app supports Claude as a first-class provider (agentProviders, ProviderMark, the Claude scan path), so a Claude-only user is told to look for Codex history.
findings.fix: Replace the subtitle with one sentence explaining what a project is and add a primary "Add project" button in this pane, wired to the same onAddProject the sidebar uses. Drop the provider name or derive it from the configured providers.

findings.title: M09 (still open) — R2 setup still finishes without a successful connection test, and never says the test is optional
findings.evidence:
<button
                    type="button"
                    className="btn btn-primary"
                    disabled={busy || !!storageConflict || !storageReady || !!runningAction}
                    onClick={() => void saveEditedStorage()}
                  >
findings.impact: "Test connection" (line 2185) and "Finish setup" (line 2194) share the identical `!storageReady` gate; nothing consults storageTestVerified, and no copy tells the user the test is optional. A user who fills all five fields with a mistyped secret can press Finish, get a storage that looks configured in the Storages index, and only discover the failure at the first Push. The receipt invalidation the prior audit asked for was added (line 1956 clears storageTestVerified on any field edit), so this is the remaining half of the finding.
findings.fix: Either require storageTestVerified before enabling Finish for kind==="s3", or leave Finish open and add a short warning beside it when the connection has not been verified since the last edit.

findings.title: L01 (still open) — the drawer is titled lowercase "log" and a genuinely empty log claims a filter mismatch
findings.evidence: log
findings.impact: The sidebar destination says "Logs" (ProjectSidebar.tsx:749), the drawer's region label is "Logs" (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:187) and Settings has a "Logs" section, but the drawer's own visible title is lowercase "log". Separately, LogPanel.tsx:358 renders "No entries match these filters." whenever lines.length === 0 — including a first run where nothing has ever been logged, sending the user to hunt through the type and level filters for a cause that does not exist.
findings.fix: Title the drawer "Logs". Distinguish the two empty cases: when the filters are at their defaults and the fetch returned nothing, say "No activity logged yet"; keep the filter sentence only when a filter is actually narrowing.

findings.title: L04 (still open) — the project overview count line is unpluralized on all three nouns
findings.evidence: {projects.length} projects · {storages.length} storage · {links.length} links
findings.impact: The heading of the Project links page renders "1 projects · 3 storage · 1 links" — "storage" never pluralizes and "projects"/"links" never singularize. This is the first line of counts a new user reads on the index page.
findings.fix: Pluralize each noun from its own count, e.g. `${n} ${n === 1 ? "project" : "projects"}`, matching the pattern already used in ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx:32-33.

r.coverage:
Read docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md in full (463 lines) and verified each of its 28 findings against the current dirty working tree on top of 789eea5.

VERDICT PER PRIOR FINDING

Genuinely fixed — not reported:
- H01 (closed Logs controls tabbable): fixed. ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:190-218 now unmounts both the resizer and LogPanel while closed (`{open && ...}`); the drawer carries id="activity-log-drawer", role="region", aria-label="Logs", tabIndex={-1}; ProjectSync.tsx:3679 focuses it on open and :3888-3890 restores the trigger on close; ProjectSidebar.tsx:742-747 has id="activity-log-trigger" with aria-controls and aria-expanded.
- H03 (--text-3 contrast): fixed and gated. App.css:8043 and :8149 now set `--text-3: var(--text-2)` in both themes; tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx:120-142 measures --text-3 against 13 opaque surfaces at a 4.5 floor. I ran `npx tsx --test tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx` — 2/2 pass.
- H04 (Sessions/Files switch hidden in breadcrumb): substantively addressed and deliberately redesigned. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2500-2534 now makes the crumb an interactive button labelled "Sessions"/"Files" with an icon, a chevron (SyncPathBar.tsx:564) and menuLabel "Switch view"; the code comment records the rejection of a two-button pill. The remaining objection is a design preference, so not reported.
- H05 (nav destinations unpredictable): fixed. ProjectSync.tsx:1469-1494 gives openStorageIndex, openProjectsIndex and openCatalogIndex one stable destination each.
- H06 (weak deletion impact at commit): fixed in the review footers. ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx renders add/replace/delete-file/delete-folder counts plus a required acknowledgement, wired into PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:849-856/612 and RestorePlanView.tsx:659-663/379. (The path-bar bypass of that gate is reported as M10.)
- H07 (narrow rules hide Push/Pull labels): fixed. App.css:3009-3059 replaced the viewport media queries with `@container sync-pathbar` steps at 760px and 640px that reduce padding, root/ancestor names and branch detail while keeping the two verbs' labels; the comment states the rule explicitly.
- H08 (missing-profile recovery): fixed. ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1796-1813 renders a direct "Choose Agent profile" button.
- L02 (no Settings save receipt): the code now documents this as a deliberate choice ("the select showing the new value is the receipt", SettingsPage.tsx:322-323) and failures do surface with Retry. No user consequence — dropped.
- L03 (two segmented-control patterns): confirmed still divergent (App.css:2071 height 25px/--type-2xs vs :4346-4353 height 28px/inherited 13px), but the only real consequence is the 10px type, already covered by M12 — dropped as a style-consistency item.
- L05 (pointer targets): mostly resolved or passing. The sidebar handle grew from 7px to 12px (App.css:8915-8920). The 22×22 targets sit at 2px gaps beside 22-26px neighbours (App.css:5471-5476, :6061), so 24px circles do not intersect and SC 2.5.8's spacing exception applies. The one genuine miss — the 16px Logs resize strip — is folded into M01.

Still standing — reported above: H02, M01, M02, M03, M04, M05, M06, M07, M08, M09, M10, M11, M12, M13, M14, M15, L01, L04.

FILES READ IN FULL OR IN THE RELEVANT REGIONS
src/components/project-sync/: ProjectSync.tsx, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx, ProjectActivityPage.tsx, ProjectSidebar.tsx, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx, RestorePlanView.tsx, SettingsPage.tsx, StorageSettings.tsx, ActivityLogDrawer.tsx, ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx, ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx, ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx, StorageIndexPage.tsx, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx, SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx; session-detail/SessionDetailHeader.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx; sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx, TopLayer.tsx; storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx; components/LogPanel.tsx, LoadingScaffold.tsx; src/terminology.ts; src/App.css (token blocks 7904-8200, path bar 2534-3075, log drawer 470-530 and 10575-10650, focus rules, retheme layer 8200-10990); tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx and project-files.integration.test.tsx.

MEASUREMENTS RUN
- Ran the css-hygiene gate (passes) to confirm H03.
- Computed WCAG contrast for the two color-mix focus rings against --surface-row, --surface-row-hover, --surface-card and --bg-2 in both themes with a local sRGB/compositing script: indicator 2.85 dark / 2.12 light; metric 3.91 dark / 2.72 light.
- Counted small-type selectors: 26 uses of --type-3xs (9px), 65 of --type-2xs (10px).
- Traced the Push commit path from the path-bar button through inlineStorageReview.onContinue to publishPendingPush and confirmed pushReviewBlockers never reads the deletion acknowledgement, and that PushResourceWorkspace exports no onPrimaryChange while RestorePlanView does.

NOT CHECKED
- No running Tauri app, so no VoiceOver, forced-colors, real 200% text or 400% zoom verification; the M12/M13 claims are read off the CSS and the fixed-height/rem interaction rather than measured on screen.
- No browser rendering pass: the container-query truncation figures for M11 are computed from the CSS caps, not screenshotted.
- Excluded per instructions: src/*mockup*.tsx and the four root *.html specimens. I checked that none of them is imported by the production tree and did not find a class collision, but I did not diff their full class inventories against App.css.
- I did not re-verify the prior audit's Rust/native claims or run the full frontend suite (only the css-hygiene gate).

findings.title: The new switcher menu puts every project verb in a footer under an unbounded list, and the menu has no max-height, so the verbs fall off the bottom of the window with nothing to scroll
findings.impact: Measured in a browser against the real App.css: the project switcher opens at y=64 and grows 34px per row. With 12 other projects its footer strip sits at y 584-658; at the 800x560 minimum window every verb pill (Reveal in Finder, Agent profile…, Rename project…, Reset local sync state…) and the "Add project…" pill are entirely below the 560px viewport, and `html, body, #root { overflow: hidden }` plus `.sync-app { overflow: hidden }` mean there is no scrollbar to reach them — the project's whole command set becomes unreachable by mouse. At the shipped default 1100x720 window the same happens from 15 other projects. Arrowing to them instead scrolls `.sync-app` itself (measured scrollTop 168), sliding the sidebar, traffic-light strip and path bar off the top of the window while the menu is open. Before this change the verbs were the FIRST group in the list, so a long project list only cut its own tail; moving them into a footer under the list makes the verbs the first thing lost.
findings.fix: In src/App.css give `.sync-path-menu` a `max-height: calc(100vh - 96px)` (or a measured cap) with `overflow-y: auto`, and pin `.sync-path-menu-current`/`.sync-path-menu-search`/`.sync-path-menu-foot` outside the scrolling region so the verbs stay visible while only the switch-target list scrolls. The page already owns a primitive that does the measuring — `useDebugPopoverPlacement` in src/components/sync-review/debugPopoverPlacement.ts computes exactly this `maxHeight` against `window.innerHeight` for the 380px debug panel; reuse it for `PathBarMenu` rather than a second, unclamped absolute box.

findings.title: The open Logs drawer paints and takes clicks over any path-bar menu that reaches it, because `.sync-pathbar { z-index: 6 }` traps the menu's z-index 30 inside its own stacking context
findings.impact: Measured at a 900x600 window with Logs open and 8 other projects in the switcher: the menu spans y 64-445, the drawer starts at y 352, and `document.elementFromPoint` at the centre of the menu's footer strip returns the drawer's `log-line`, not the menu. The "Add project…" pill and the verb pills under it are visibly drawn over by the log list and cannot be clicked at all — the click lands on a log row. `.sync-pathbar` has `z-index: 6` so its descendants can never rise above the drawer's 20 no matter what `.sync-path-menu` declares.
findings.fix: Remove the `z-index: 6` from `.sync-pathbar` (it only needs to sit above `.sync-main`, which the drawer's own 20 already handles), or raise the bar above `--z-log` and give the drawer a lower token. The durable fix is to render `PathBarMenu` through the existing `TopLayer` body portal (src/components/sync-review/TopLayer.tsx) with `useDebugPopoverPlacement`, the way ProjectFileDetailsMenu, the session debug popover and the Catalog info panel already do.

findings.title: The Logs drawer resize clamp budgets only `.sync-main`'s 120px floor and ignores 84px of shell chrome, so a dragged-open drawer runs past the bottom of the window
findings.impact: The workspace column is `.sync-app`'s 16px vertical padding + the 52px path bar + its 8px `margin-bottom` + `.sync-main`'s 120px `min-height` + the drawer's 8px `margin-top` = 204px of chrome, not 120px. Measured at the 800x560 minimum window with the drawer dragged to the clamp's own maximum (440px): `.sync-main` bottoms out at its 120px floor and the drawer runs from y 196 to y 636 — 76px past the 560px window — and `.sync-app { overflow: hidden }` clips it with no scrollbar. The bottom 74px of the log body is permanently outside the window, and because the body auto-scrolls to the newest line, the newest log line sits in the invisible strip. The retheme widened this shortfall (gutters 3px→8px, `.sync-app` padding 6px→16px, tile borders 1px→2px) from 64px to 84px.
findings.fix: Change both budgets in ProjectSync.tsx to account for the real chrome, e.g. `window.innerHeight - 204`, or better, measure the workspace column: clamp against `workspaceRef.current.clientHeight - pathBarHeight - MIN_MAIN_HEIGHT - 2 * GUTTER` so the number cannot drift again the next time `--retro-gutter` changes.

findings.title: The switcher menu is a hard-coded 380px anchored at `left: 0` with no viewport clamp, so the third crumb's menu is cut off at the window edge
findings.impact: Every crumb menu is rendered with `align="start"` (SyncPathBar.tsx:587), so the box always grows rightward from its crumb. Measured with long storage and project names at a 1042x720 window with the 220px sidebar: the third crumb's switcher spans x 724-1104 and 62px of it is clipped by `.sync-app { overflow: hidden }`. The clipped strip is the right edge of the menu, which is exactly where `.sync-path-menu-check` (`margin-left: auto`) and `.sync-path-menu-tail` (`margin-left: auto`) live — so the tick that identifies the current view and the right-aligned "Add…" pill are the first things to disappear. Overflow is 380 - 0.4 x (bar inline size), so it recurs at any window width whenever the bar lands between roughly 760px and 950px — including a 1400px window with the sidebar dragged to 560px (66px clipped). In production this hits the non-Git project's Sessions/Files switcher, the one surface the prior audit already flagged as hard to discover.
findings.fix: Stop sizing the menu in absolute px against nothing: use `width: min(380px, 100vw - 32px)` at minimum, and give `PathBarMenu` the same measured placement the rest of the app already uses (`useDebugPopoverPlacement` clamps `left` to `Math.min(anchor.left + INSET, window.innerWidth - width - EDGE)`), or flip to `align="end"` when the anchor sits in the right half of the bar.

findings.title: The retheme's wider gutters pushed the path bar under its own 760px breakpoint at the shipped default window size, so the storage name and branch name are hidden with no resize
findings.impact: The comment's arithmetic (`window - sidebar`) omits 56px of chrome the bar actually loses: `.sync-app`'s 16px padding, the 12px resizer (8px net), the tile's 2x2px ink border and the bar's own 28px padding. Measured against the real stylesheet at the shipped default window (tauri.conf.json: 1100x720) with the default 298px sidebar, the container resolves to 748px, so the ≤760px rules fire on first launch: the storage crumb's name computes to `display: none` (only a drive/cloud icon marks which storage Push and Pull act on) and both `.sync-history-branch-name` and the `History only` state chip compute to `display: none`. Rendering the same markup against `git show HEAD:src/App.css` gives 765px and `display: block` — this is a regression introduced by the uncommitted gutter change (`--retro-gutter` 3px→8px, `--box-border` 1px→2px, resizer 7px→12px), which ate 17px of bar without moving the breakpoint.
findings.fix: Re-derive the ladder against the bar's real inline size: at the 800x560 floor the container measures 524px, not 580px, so the two steps should be about 700px and 580px rather than 760px and 640px. Update the comment's arithmetic to include the shell chrome, and add a test that asserts the container size at the default window rather than the raw window width.

findings.title: Step notes keep the 68ch prose cap while every other box on the same session-detail rail runs full width, leaving a ragged column
findings.impact: SessionDetailEvent.tsx:487 renders a step as `<div className="session-detail-event-copy session-detail-intermediate-prose">`, outside any `.session-detail-card`, so `max-width: 68ch` still applies to it while prompts, replies, checkpoints and tool rows are uncapped. Measured at 1440x900 with the 220px sidebar: the prompt, reply, checkpoint and tool boxes are all 1047px wide (right edge 1374) and the step note is 557px (right edge 883) — 490px short. Now that the step is drawn as an ink-edged box rather than a bare indent, the mismatch reads as a broken card, and it directly contradicts the rule the new CSS comment states ("Every box on the rail runs to the content's right edge"). The `@container session-detail-layout (max-width: 720px)` override only removes the cap at narrow widths, so the defect appears exactly when the window is large.
findings.fix: Add `.session-detail-intermediate-prose { max-width: none; }` after the `.session-detail-event-copy` rule (or move the 68ch cap onto a `.session-detail-response-prose`-style class that only bare prose carries) so every box on the rail shares one right edge.

findings.title: `overflow: hidden` on the new prompt/reply card clips the file-path hover tooltip that is meant to float above it
findings.impact: SessionDetailEvent.tsx:158-196 attaches `data-tooltip` to every in-project markdown link, and both prompts and (new in this change) replies now render inside `.session-detail-card`. The tooltip is anchored `bottom: calc(100% + 8px)` — above the link — so for a link on the first line or two of a card it sits above or across the card's top edge. Measured with a real project path (`~/Desktop/.../PushResourceWorkspace.tsx`): the tooltip is 54px tall and 22px of it (41%) is clipped away by the card, cut flat against the card's 2px border. The `z-index: 60` the author gave it cannot help — an ancestor's `overflow: hidden` clips regardless of stacking. Agent replies were open prose before this change and had no clipping ancestor at all, so every reply link is newly affected.
findings.fix: Drop `overflow: hidden` from `.session-detail-card` (the head band already gets its own corner from the card radius, and `.session-detail-card > .session-detail-event-copy` can carry the rounding if needed), or move the tooltip out of flow — render it through `TopLayer` with measured placement the way the other popovers in this codebase do.

findings.title: The switcher's new search field cannot be reached by keyboard: arrow keys skip it and Tab closes the menu
findings.impact: The input carries no menu role, so `menuOptions()` never returns it and `moveMenuFocus` can never focus it; Tab from inside the menu closes the menu (SyncPathBar.tsx:258) and Tab from the trigger closes it too (SyncPathBar.tsx:516 and :551). A keyboard user who opens the switcher with Enter or ArrowDown therefore has no way at all to reach the filter field — the only route in is a mouse click. Since the field only appears once there are six or more switch targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR), the users who most need it (many projects, many storages) are exactly the ones who lose it. The same field is also invisible to a screen reader in menu mode, because `role="menu"` admits only the menuitem family.
findings.fix: Focus the search input when the menu opens with a keyboard (extend `focusMenuOption` to prefer `.sync-path-menu-search` when present), let ArrowUp from the first option return to it, and stop treating Tab as a blanket close while focus is in the field. If the field must stay, the container should be `role="dialog"`/combobox-shaped rather than `role="menu"`, since a menu may not contain a textbox.

findings.title: The Settings toggle thumb declares `border-radius: 50%` and then immediately overrides it with `2px` in the same rule
findings.impact: The later declaration wins, so the retheme's intended round thumb never renders: the Settings switches draw a near-square 12px thumb inside a fully pill-shaped 999px track (`.sync-settings-switch { border-radius: var(--r-pill) }`, and `--r-pill` moved from 4px to 999px in this same change). The first declaration is dead. This is the only genuine duplicate-property collision in the 10,989-line stylesheet — a scripted pass over every rule block found no other.
findings.fix: Delete one of the two lines in src/App.css — keep `border-radius: 50%` if the round thumb was the intent of the pill-track retheme, otherwise drop it.

findings.title: `.sync-log-drawer.open { height: clamp(190px, 30vh, 280px) }` is dead — the drawer always carries an inline height that outranks it
findings.impact: An inline style always beats a stylesheet declaration, and `height` is set inline whenever the drawer is open, so the viewport-relative rule never applies in any state: closed, `.log-drawer { height: 0 }` wins and the `.open` selector does not match; open, the inline value wins. The drawer therefore always starts at the hard-coded 240px from `useState(240)`, including on a 560px-tall window where the intended clamp would have given 190px and left `.sync-main` 48px more room. A maintainer reading the stylesheet is told the drawer is responsive when it is not.
findings.fix: Either delete the rule from src/App.css, or move the clamp into the component (initialise `logHeight` from `Math.min(280, Math.max(190, window.innerHeight * 0.3))`) so the documented behaviour is the one that actually ships.

WHAT I READ AND RAN

Test infrastructure (complete): scripts/run-frontend-integration-tests.mjs and all 17 files in tests/frontend/. Established the two gate shapes precisely:

1. DOM-less render. Every rendering test uses `renderToStaticMarkup` from react-dom/server under `node --test` on esbuild-bundled CJS. There is no DOM, no layout, no CSS, no event dispatch, no useEffect, no refs. It can assert markup strings and inline `style` attributes and nothing else. Consequence: focus management, keyboard handlers, cascade, and any geometry are all invisible to it. Only 28 modules are ever imported by a test; `src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx` is NOT among them — it is only ever `readFileSync`'d as text (project-sync-cutover.integration.test.tsx:510, project-activity.integration.test.tsx:275). SettingsPage/StorageIndexPage render it transitively but only with a single root/leaf crumb, so the entire new switcher branch (header, search, verb pills, tail pills, footer) has zero render coverage.

2. Source-text "CSS gates". Twelve tests `readFileSync("src/App.css")` and regex the string: project-sync-cutover:99/148/166/231/241/409/728/737, project-activity:389/521/950/961/1044/1083/1373/1726/1936, resource-inventory:631/696, storage-catalog:385/389/421/457/563/573, activity-log:92, catalog-scope-removal:44. These match declaration text, so a declaration that parses but loses the cascade (duplicate property in a block, or an identical selector restated later in the RetroTheme layer) passes every one of them.

The single exception is tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx, which does resolve var() hops and composite translucent fills — but only for four notice ink/fill pairs, seven `--thread-status-*` badges, and `--text-3` against a hard-coded list of thirteen surfaces. It never measures `--surface-subtle`, `--surface-footer` composites, any `color-mix()` value (it asserts plain 6-digit hex and would throw), or anything outside `:root` / `:root[data-theme=…]` blocks.

Verification work I ran: parsed App.css into (selector, declarations, line) and diffed same-selector property conflicts across the file; scanned for duplicate declarations inside a single block (found exactly one real hit, App.css:4321); resolved every `var()` in the file against declared tokens to find undeclared references (4 hits, 3 of them set inline by JS); reimplemented the css-hygiene contrast maths and swept every `--text-*` against every `--surface-*`/`--bg-*`/`--button-bg*` token in both themes, plus hand-computed the `color-mix()` values for `--session-detail-amber`/`--session-detail-link`/purple that the gate cannot parse; cross-referenced every className in the non-mockup TSX tree against the classes App.css defines; decoded public/fonts/Baloo2-Variable.woff2's table directory to confirm it really carries `fvar`/`avar`/`STAT` for the declared 400-800 axis.

Source read in full or in the relevant region: SyncPathBar.tsx, menuKeyboard.ts, the whole `.sync-path-*` CSS block (App.css:3061-3330), SessionDetailEvent.tsx, sessionDetailModel.ts, SessionDetailToolbar.tsx, SessionDetailTimeline.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx, ProjectSidebar.tsx divider maths, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx banner block, ProjectActivityPage.tsx `sessionSyncPresentation`/`syncHoldDetail`, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx crumb-menu construction (lines 1690-1790, 2273-2450), ProjectSync.tsx `appActions`/`resetProjectSyncMetadata`, StorageCatalogPage.tsx's hand-rolled `.sync-path-menu`, Icons.tsx, ThreadStatusIcon.tsx, tauri.conf.json, and the whole 2719-line `git diff HEAD -- src/App.css`. Backend cross-checks: service.rs `fit_capture_budget` / `thread_comparison_error`, provider_capture.rs `MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES`. Prior audit docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md read in full; H03 was verified as re-introduced in a different form (finding 4) rather than re-reported.

THE THREE UNCOMMITTED TEST CHANGES

project-activity:2636 — literal `3px`→`8px` in the grid-template-rows regex. Correctly tightened; still pins a literal.
session-detail:185-192 and 339-343 — filter defaults flipped to `toolCalls: false` / `intermediateSteps: false`, card markup regexes rewritten for the new stamp-band shape. Equal strength, not loosened.
project-sync-cutover:14-15, 572-642 — five assertions rewritten to import `SECTION_DIVIDER_NET`/`SECTION_DIVIDERS_HEIGHT` from the module under test. This IS a loosening; reported as finding 10.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK

No browser or Tauri run — every layout claim (finding 2 especially) is computed from the CSS box model plus the tauri.conf.json 800×560 minimum and 1100×720 default, not measured on screen. I did not exercise VoiceOver, forced-colors mode, or OS text scaling. I did not run the suite (`npm` is blocked by the Oracle SWG MITM per the project's own notes), so I confirmed gate behaviour by reading the assertions rather than by mutating source and watching a test fail. I deliberately dropped one candidate as unconfirmable: App.css:9847 uses `:not()` with a complex descendant argument (`:not(.sync-project-file-tile .sync-history-thread-card)`), which older WKWebView drops wholesale, taking the Catalog card's box with it — but tauri.conf.json sets no `minimumSystemVersion`, and I could not confirm the WebKit floor this ships against. findings.title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard, and is an illegal child of role="menu"
findings.impact: A user with ≥6 switch targets (7+ projects, or 7+ storages) can only use the new filter with a mouse. Opening the menu from the keyboard runs `focusMenuOption(crumb.id, "first")` (line 429), which focuses `menuOptions()` — `'[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]'` (menuKeyboard.ts:11) — so focus lands on the first target row, never the input. Arrow keys only cycle those same roles, printable characters are swallowed by the type-ahead below, and Tab is intercepted at line 256 (`if (event.key === "Tab") { onClose(false); return; }`) which closes the menu. There is no key that puts the caret in the field, which also makes the `if (typing)` Enter branch at lines 265-271 unreachable. Separately, a screen reader in menu-navigation mode does not expose a bare `<input>` as a child of `role="menu"` at all — the file's own comment eight lines above says so: "A `role="menu"` admits only the menuitem family."
findings.fix: In src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx, make the field part of the widget's keyboard contract: give the menu `role="dialog"` (or move the input outside the menu and wire it with `aria-controls`/`aria-activedescendant` as a combobox), autofocus the input when a searchable switcher opens instead of `focusMenuOption(..., "first")`, and let ArrowUp from the first option return to it. If the menu role is kept, the input must not live inside it.

findings.evidence:
<div

findings.title: Nine standalone specimen modules live inside src/ and are type-checked by the release build
findings.impact: `tsconfig.json` sets `include: ["src"]` and `npm run build` is `tsc && vite build`, so all 4,152 lines of catalog-groups-mockup, files-activity-redesign-mockup, files-review-mockup, files-selection-mockup, pathbar-mockup, sidebar-collapse-mockup, plugin-icons, no-commit-icons and plug-diagonal are compiled on every release (verified with `tsc --listFiles`). They import live production components (`ProjectSidebar`, `SyncPathBar`, `SyncReviewTabs`, `ThreadStatusIcon`, `ProviderMark`, `Notice`, `Icon`) and production types, so a signature change in the real tree fails the release build from files that ship nothing — this very change already had to edit catalog-groups-mockup.tsx and files-selection-mockup.tsx just to follow the `--font-pixel` → `--font-display` rename. Each also calls `createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!)` at module scope, so an accidental import would mount a second React root over the app.
findings.fix: Move the nine specimen modules and their root .html harnesses into a `specimens/` directory outside `include`, or add them to `exclude` in tsconfig.json with a separate `tsconfig.specimens.json` for when you want them checked. At minimum, wrap each `createRoot` call in a guard so the module is inert unless it owns the page.

r.coverage:
Walked the production import graph transitively from src/main.tsx with a script (69 files reachable; only the 6 *mockup*.tsx plus plugin-icons.tsx, no-commit-icons.tsx, plug-diagonal.tsx and vite-env.d.ts unreachable) and confirmed no mockup is imported by the real tree and no `mockup-*` class appears in App.css. Read in full or in the relevant regions: SyncPathBar.tsx (all 660 lines of the switcher rewrite), menuKeyboard.ts, SessionDetailEvent.tsx + sessionDetailModel.ts diffs, SessionDetailTimeline.tsx, SessionDetailToolCall.tsx, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx (banner zone + blockers), ProjectActivityPage.tsx (BranchPicker, sessionSyncPresentation, syncHoldDetail, activityHeaderCounts), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx (all six crumb-menu builders, the R2 split menu and its effects), StorageCatalogPage.tsx (crumb menus, ResourceCard action menu, openChoices effects), ProjectSync.tsx (appActions, windowActions, showsPathBar), ProjectSidebar.tsx diff, SiblingRepoNotice.tsx, LoadingScaffold.tsx, TopLayer.tsx, Icons.tsx, and the four modified test files. Ran `git diff HEAD` on every changed frontend file and `git show HEAD:src/App.css` for a before/after comparison.

Scripted checks I ran against the working tree: (1) class selectors declared in App.css vs. every literal and dynamically composed className in production TSX, resolving each apparent orphan against its type union (SessionCountQuality, SessionTimelineEventKind, SessionToolCategory, SessionToolCallStatus, ActivityLogLevel) before calling it dead; (2) CSS custom properties used-but-undefined and defined-but-unused; (3) duplicate selector blocks with conflicting declarations, then checking each hit's @media/@container context so responsive overrides were not miscounted; (4) HEAD-vs-working-tree class-set diff (no selector was removed while still emitted, and none added without a producer); (5) `*Props` interface fields never referenced and referenced only once; (6) `useState` pairs whose setter is never called or getter never read; (7) exported symbols with no importer, separated into prod/test/mockup consumers; (8) IconName union members never rendered. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` are on, which is why the unused-local and unread-prop categories came back empty.

What I could not check: I did not run the app or the frontend test suite, so every rendering claim is from source and stylesheet reading rather than measurement. The three sizing judgements — the switcher menu clipping past the 560px minimum window height, the 380px fixed switcher width against a narrow bar, and the traffic-light/titlebar clearance after the trafficLightPosition change — are computed from the declared token values (3.25rem bar, 8px `--retro-gutter`, `html{font-size:100%}`, `html,body,#root{overflow:hidden}`); I report only the height clipping, and dropped the horizontal-overflow and traffic-light concerns as unverified. I also did not audit the Rust changes beyond tracing where `ConversationBlocker::CaptureBudget` is produced, which I did only to establish that it reaches the frontend on the push-review path alone.

findings.title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard — every route into it closes the menu
findings.impact: Once a project or storage switcher lists 6+ targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR, line 129 — reached at 7 projects, and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2431 puts every other project in that list), a search box is painted at the top of the menu that a keyboard-only or screen-reader user can never focus. Opening the menu with ArrowDown lands on the first menuitem; Tab or Shift+Tab from there — or from the opener — closes the menu before the browser moves focus, because React flushes the discrete state update to `hidden` before the Tab default action runs. Typing characters instead runs the menu's own typeahead (line 283-303), which jumps focus but leaves the visible filter box empty, so what the user sees and what the keyboard does disagree. The field is mouse-only. The same uncommitted diff even added `.sync-path-menu-search:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring) }` (App.css) for a state that cannot occur.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx, give PathBarMenu a ref to the search input and focus it (not the first menuitem) when `searchable` and the menu opens — both from `focusMenuOption` (line 422) and the opener's ArrowDown/ArrowUp handlers. Then let Tab move between the input and the list instead of closing: in the menu-root `onKeyDown` (line 258), only close on Tab when focus is on a menuitem and the input is absent, and drive the typeahead buffer from the input's value when it is present so filtering and focus agree.

findings.title: Activity log drawer's resize handle is mouse-only; the identical sidebar handle beside it is fully keyboard-operable
findings.impact: A control announced as "Resize log, separator" has no tabIndex, no key handler and no aria-valuenow, so a keyboard or screen-reader user cannot resize or reset the log drawer at all — no ArrowUp/ArrowDown, no Home/End, and the double-click reset is unreachable too. logHeight is stuck at the 240px default (ProjectSync.tsx:398, not persisted) for the entire session, so on a short window the log body is a few rows tall and a keyboard user has no way to enlarge it. The sidebar separator 200 lines away in ProjectSync implements the whole pattern, so this is an omission, not a design position.
findings.fix: Mirror the sidebar separator in ActivityLogDrawer.tsx: add `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow={height}`, and an `onKeyDown` that steps `height` by a fixed amount on ArrowUp/ArrowDown and jumps to the min/max on Home/End (calling a new `onResizeBy`/`onSetHeight` prop that ProjectSync wires to `setLogHeight` with the same clamp used at ProjectSync.tsx:676). Keep `onDoubleClick={onResetHeight}` and add Home/End or Escape as its keyboard equivalent.

findings.title: Switcher mistakes a lone "Add storage…" group for the object's verbs and renders it as a bare "+" glyph
findings.impact: The storage-editor crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707-1731) builds its menu as `[ ...(otherStorages ? [{label:"Switch to", …}] : []), { items:[add-storage] } ]`. When the user has exactly one storage — the first-run state — the "Switch to" group is omitted, so the *only* populated group is the unlabelled `add-storage` group. Position, not intent, decides the role: `populated[0]` is unlabelled, so it is claimed as `verbs` and rendered by `renderPill(item, false)`, which emits only `{item.icon && <Icon/>}` and drops the label. `lists` is empty, `caption` is empty (add-storage has no `detail`). The Storage switcher therefore opens as a 380px panel containing the current-storage row and a footer holding one unlabelled 32px "+" circle and nothing else. Add a second storage and the identical command re-renders as a right-aligned text pill reading "Add storage…" — the same item changes shape and loses its name based on how many storages exist.
findings.fix: Role assignment must not be inferred from array position when the caller's array is conditionally built. Either mark the roles on the group (`role: "verbs" | "targets" | "tails"` on PathBarMenuGroup) or, minimally, treat the first unlabelled group as verbs only when a labelled group follows it: `const verbs = switcher && populated[0] && !populated[0].label && populated.some((g) => !!g.label) ? populated[0].items : []` — the trailing unlabelled group then correctly falls through to `tails` and keeps its label.

findings.title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard at all
findings.impact: There are exactly three ways focus can enter an open path menu, and none of them can land on this input. (1) Opening with Enter/Space leaves focus on the crumb toggle. (2) Opening with ArrowDown/ArrowUp calls `focusMenuOption`, which uses `menuOptions()` — selector `'[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]'` (menuKeyboard.ts:11) — and the input carries no such role, so it is skipped. (3) Tab, the only key that would reach a `tabIndex`-default element, is intercepted and closes the menu, both on the toggle (`if (event.key === "Tab") { setOpenMenu(null); return; }`, line 516/551) and inside the panel (`if (event.key === "Tab") { onClose(false); return; }`, line 258). Printable keys are swallowed by the type-ahead branch at line 283. The field appears whenever a switcher has >= 6 targets, which the Project switcher reaches for any user with six or more projects — so a keyboard-only user sees a filter box on screen that they can never focus or type into (WCAG 2.1.1). The Enter-to-take-first-match branch at line 268 is likewise unreachable, since it only fires when `event.target instanceof HTMLInputElement`.
findings.fix: In SyncPathBar.tsx, give the input `role="searchbox"`/`tabIndex={0}` and include it in the roving order explicitly: focus it (rather than `options[0]`) when `searchable` and the menu opens via `focusMenuOption`, and special-case it in the panel's Tab handler so Tab from the field moves into the list instead of closing. Alternatively drop the input and route the existing type-ahead buffer into `setQuery` when `searchable`, so one keyboard mechanism serves both.

findings.title: Disabled-reason text is silently dropped for every item the switcher renders as a pill
findings.impact: `renderPill` puts `disabledReason` only in a `title` tooltip; unlike `renderItem` (line 190-191) it never renders it as a visible second line. Two live callers depend on the old behaviour and their own comments say so. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2314-2323 — "Stays put at zero candidates and says why, instead of vanishing from the DOM for a reason the user cannot see" — now shows "Link storage…" greyed at 50% opacity with the sentence "Everything you've added is already linked" nowhere on screen. StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239 does the same with "This row is not linked to it yet" on the greyed Unlink verb, which is icon-only, so a greyed link-off glyph is the entire message. Because these are `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`) buttons reached by arrow keys, a keyboard user focuses an inert control whose explanation is in a `title` that never renders on focus. The existing gate (project-sync-cutover.integration.test.tsx:520) asserts the source text `disabledReason: workspaceAvailableStorages.length === 0` in the *caller*, so it stays green while the renderer discards it.

findings.title: Switch targets suppress their path detail, so "(unnamed)" and misconfigured storages become indistinguishable rows
findings.impact: Every switch target passes `target === true`, and all three switcher callers mark their disambiguating second line as a path: storages via `storageSubtitleIsPath` (true for *all* local storages, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:215-217), projects via `detailIsPath: true` (line 2438), catalog scopes via `detailIsPath: true` (line 1327). So the only text left on the row is the name. Concretely: `storageSubtitle` returns `compactProjectPath(storage.local_dir || "Folder not configured")` (line 208) and marks it a path — a local storage with no folder configured now renders in the Switch-to list as an ordinary row identical to a working one, its "Folder not configured" warning suppressed. A keyboard or screen-reader user can therefore never reach the Path / Type / Mode / Modified / Blocked copy buttons or the Copy all button — the file's full path and its blocked-reason are keyboard-inaccessible. findings.title: Pull review's Rescan wipes the plan first, so a failed replan deletes the review and shows no error at all
findings.impact: `planRestore` synchronously runs `setRestorePlan(null)` before its first await, and `inlineStorageReview` is built as `pendingPush ? … : restorePlan && restoreBinding ? … : null` (line 3395/3471), so the open Pull review unmounts the instant Rescan is pressed. On failure it never comes back, and `restoreError` — which the catch sets — is rendered in exactly one place, `error={restoreError}` on `<RestorePlanView>` at line 3500, which no longer exists. `grep restoreError` returns only the useState at line 424 and that one prop. So a user who presses Rescan on the Pull review's Project files step and hits a transient R2/plan failure watches the whole review vanish back to the activity page with zero explanation, losing their reviewed selection and being given no indication anything went wrong.
findings.fix: In `planRestore`, do not clear `restorePlan` until the new plan resolves (keep the old plan visible with a busy flag), and give `restoreError` a renderer that survives `restorePlan === null` — e.g. route the returned message through `setStorageNotice({kind:"action_failed", action:"pull", …})` the way `beginProjectRestore` (line 2513) already does, and have `onRefreshPlan` consume the returned failure instead of discarding it with `void`.

findings.title: A failed project-file scan leaves the Push review showing a "Scanning project files…" skeleton forever
findings.impact: The branch keys on `!scanned`, not on `loading`. `scanPendingProjectFiles` (ProjectSync.tsx:1962) only sets `projectContentScanned: true` inside the success updater; on failure it does `setPushError(...)` and clears `projectContentLoading` in the finally. So after a failed scan of a non-Git project's folder, the Push review's "Project files" step renders a spinning skeleton plus the caption "Scanning project files…" indefinitely, inside a `role="region"` announced as "Scanning project files", directly above the red error notice saying the scan failed. The page simultaneously claims work is in progress and reports it failed, and the user has no way to know the skeleton will never resolve.
findings.fix: Gate the scaffold on the in-flight flag, not the scanned flag: render `<LoadingScaffold>` only when `loading` is true, and when `!scanned && !loading` render a failed-scan state naming the failure with the Rescan button beside it (the toolbar's Rescan at line 556 is already the retry — bring it into the empty slot).

findings.title: The new path-bar switcher's filter field cannot be reached by keyboard
findings.impact:
Three routes to the field are all closed. (1) Opening the menu from the keyboard calls `focusMenuOption(crumb.id, "first")` (line 421-429), which picks `menuOptions(root)[0]`; `menuOptions` selects only `[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]` (menuKeyboard.ts:11), and the input carries no role, so focus lands on the first switch target. (2) Arrow keys go through `moveMenuFocus`, which walks the same list. (3) Tab inside the menu closes it (line 258), and Tab on the opener button also closes it (lines 516/551). So the filter — which only appears once there are six or more switch targets, i.e. exactly the case where the list is long enough to need it — is pointer-only. It is also an `` and a `

` placed as direct children of `role="menu"`, which admits only the menuitem family, so screen readers in menu-navigation mode never encounter either the field or the "No match." result.
findings.fix: Make the field part of the menu's keyboard contract: focus it (not the first item) when a `searchable` menu opens, let ArrowDown/ArrowUp step between it and the list, and stop treating Tab as an exit while focus is in the input. Structurally, move the search box out of the `role="menu"` element — wrap the popover in a plain container that holds the input and a nested `role="menu"` for the items, and give the "No match." line a live announcement.

findings.title: A failed "Load 50 more" hides the button, mislabels the failure, and the only retry throws away every loaded page
findings.evidence:

        <button
          type="button"
          className="btn session-detail-load-more"
          disabled={loadingMore || loading}

// line 78-87:
      {error && (
        <Notice severity="danger" timing="blocking" title="Timeline unavailable"
          action={<button … onClick={onRetry}>Try again</button>}>
findings.impact: `requestTimelinePage` preserves the loaded events on an append failure (`if (!append) { setEvents([]); … }`, SessionDetailPage.tsx:246-249) but still sets `timelineError`. The render then hides the "Load 50 more" button because `!error` is false, and titles the box "Timeline unavailable" while the whole transcript is still visible below it. The only offered recovery, `onRetry` → `retryTimeline` (SessionDetailPage.tsx:315), bumps `timelineReloadEpoch`, which re-runs the first-page effect and replaces `events` with page one. A user who has paged through 500 events and hits one transient failure loses 450 of them and has no way to just retry the page that failed.
findings.fix: Distinguish an append failure from a first-page failure: keep a `timelineAppendError` separate from `timelineError`, render it beside a still-enabled "Load 50 more" (retrying `requestTimelinePage` with the same `nextCursor` and `append: true`), and reserve the "Timeline unavailable" whole-page box for the `!append` case where `events` really is empty.

findings.title: Connecting to a remote repo swallows the follow-up Pull-plan failure entirely
findings.impact: `planRestore` does not throw on a planning failure — it catches, calls `setRestoreError(message)` and returns the message (line 2354-2362). `beginProjectRestore` consumes that return value and converts it into a storage-card notice (line 2489/2513), but `connectStorageBundle` awaits it and discards it, and the surrounding catch never fires. Since `restoreError` has no renderer while `restorePlan` is null (see the Rescan finding), the user picks a repo in the "Choose a repo from this storage" dialog, presses "Connect and review Pull", the dialog closes, and nothing happens: no review, no error, no notice — only the earlier "Repo connected" toast if one was emitted.
findings.fix: Capture the return of `planRestore` here the way `beginProjectRestore` does and, when it is non-null, raise `setStorageNotice({ projectId, storageId, kind: "action_failed", action: "pull", message })` so the failed plan lands on the storage card.

findings.title: A failed Catalog scope listing is swallowed and the UI then tells the user they have no Catalog rows
findings.impact: `refreshCatalogScopes` is one of the reads in `loadShell`'s `Promise.allSettled` whose result is deliberately skipped (`const [projectsResult, , , , repositoryKindsResult] = await projectReads;`, line 1027), and it also eats its own rejection here, so nothing is added to `failures` and `backendError` stays null. `catalogScopes` therefore holds its initial `[]`, and both surfaces that read it assert a fact rather than an unknown: the sidebar renders "Add your first resource" (ProjectSidebar.tsx:953-958) and CatalogIndexPage renders "Add a resource to sync an agent profile through storage." (CatalogIndexPage.tsx:47). A user whose configured Catalog rows failed to list sees them silently gone, is told to add their first one, and may create a duplicate row for a home that is already registered.
findings.fix: Keep the failure: have `refreshCatalogScopes` return a failure string that `loadShell` pushes onto `failures` (so it reaches the shell's `backendError` notice with its existing Retry), and make CatalogIndexPage take a `failed` prop so it renders "Couldn't list Catalog resources" with a retry instead of the zero-state copy.

findings.title: An autosave failure in project setup disables Finish permanently with no retry control
findings.impact: The debounced autosave clears `dirtyRef.current` before it calls `updateSetupDraft` (line ~300), so a failure leaves `saveState === "error"` with nothing marked dirty — the effect will not run again on its own. The footer then reads "Not saved", Finish is disabled, and the only two controls are Discard (which destroys the draft) and the disabled Finish. The single escape is to guess that editing an unrelated field re-arms the autosave. A user who hits a transient write failure on the setup page is left with a project they cannot finish and a button that gives no reason for being dead.
findings.fix: On a save failure restore `dirtyRef.current = true` so the next effect run retries, and render a "Save again" button beside the "Not saved" text that calls the same `updateSetupDraft` path directly. Give the disabled Finish a `title` naming the save failure so the refusal is explained.

findings.title: The non-Git Files page's scan error replaces the whole page with a bare notice and no retry
findings.impact: The early return drops the search row that carries the page's own "Rescan" button (line 351), so the entire Files view becomes one red box holding the raw backend message with no heading, no context, and no control. The only recovery is the unlabelled circular-arrow glyph in the path bar (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2599), which is not adjacent to the error and is itself not rendered at all when `workspaceStorage` is null. A user whose folder scan fails has to discover an icon in the title bar or switch projects and back.
findings.fix: Render the failure as a state inside the page rather than instead of it: keep the section heading and put a "Rescan" button in the notice's `action` slot wired to `onRescan`, matching the shape ProjectActivityPage already uses for its first-load failure (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1836-1845).

findings.title: Switcher menus stopped rendering `disabledReason`, so an inert verb or tail explains itself only in a hover tooltip
findings.impact: `PathBarMenuItem.disabledReason` is documented at line 44 as "Why the item is inert right now — rendered as its second line", and `renderItem` still honours that. `renderPill` does not: for every item promoted into the footer strip of a switcher menu it drops the reason into `title` only. Concretely, the storage crumb's "Link storage…" tail (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2313) carries `disabledReason: "Everything you've added is already linked"` and the catalog storage crumb's "Unlink" verb carries "This row is not linked to it yet" (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1237); both now render as a greyed pill with no visible reason. The pills are `aria-disabled` and kept in the roving focus order precisely so the reason is reachable by keyboard, but `title` is not surfaced on keyboard focus and is not part of the accessible name, so a keyboard or screen-reader user gets an inert control with no explanation at all.
findings.fix: In `renderPill`, when `inert && item.disabledReason`, put the reason into the accessible name — `aria-label={`${item.label}. ${item.disabledReason}`}` — or render the reason as visible text in the footer strip (the `sync-path-menu-cap` line already exists for exactly this kind of qualifier).

findings.title: A failed setup-draft load leaves the workspace with a red box and no action of any kind
findings.impact: Both writers of this branch — a rejected `getSetupDraft` and the `"This setup draft no longer exists."` case at line 275 — land the user on a panel with no Retry, no Discard, and no Back. In the "no longer exists" case the sidebar still lists the draft row (`setupDrafts` is separate state that was not refreshed), so clicking it just returns here. The only exit is to click some other sidebar entry, and the stale draft row stays in the list until a full app reload.
findings.fix: Give this branch the same two controls the loaded page has: a Retry that re-runs the mount load, and a Discard wired to `onDiscard(draftId)` so a draft the backend says is gone can be cleared from the sidebar without restarting.

findings.title: The new "Dark theme" menu checkbox shows a tick while the user's saved choice is System
findings.evidence:

Rendered as a `menuitemcheckbox`, the row therefore claims "Dark theme, checked" for a user whose stored preference is System on a dark-mode Mac — and toggling it silently drops them out of System with no indication. Because the control only writes explicit values, there is no way back to System from this menu; the user has to find the Settings page's three-way Theme control. The titlebar button beside it (line 2765) does the same write but is honestly labelled as an action ("Switch to light theme"), not as state.
