findings.title: Push review announces N capture-budget conversations but every one of those rows is filtered out of the list
findings.impact: A capture_budget entry is built by hold_over_budget_candidates() as `action: Blocked, selectable: false` (crates/mallard-domain/src/conversation_reconciliation.rs:246-252). sessionSyncPresentation() then maps it to status "unavailable" (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:498 `if (entry.push_decision?.action === "blocked") return blocked("push")`), and both row lists in the Push review drop it: `isPushReviewStatus(status) && isPushReviewDecision(entry.push_decision)` at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 and again for the "older" list at :1599 — isPushReviewStatus only admits "local-outstanding", and isPushReviewDecision requires selectable===true. visibleConversations in this file (line 442) applies the same isPushReviewDecision gate. So the user reads "3 conversations wait for the next round" and cannot find, hover, or inspect a single one of them anywhere in the review. `total={currentGroup.length}` (line 701) also excludes them, so the comment's "0/N readout" rationale is false too — N simply shrinks. The new syncHoldDetail case added for this blocker (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1119) is consequently dead: the only presentation paths that reach it are behind those filters, and the plain Activity page's comparison is built with build_push_actions=false (service.rs:6395) so it never carries the blocker at all.
findings.fix: Either admit these rows into the Push review — give them their own status so isPushReviewStatus/isPushReviewDecision let them through as visible-but-inert rows, which is what the comment promises — or drop the claim from the banner and name the sessions in its text. As written, both the comment at :564-566 and the new syncHoldDetail branch describe UI that cannot render.

findings.title: Comparison-failure banner offers a destructive "Reset local sync state" for any failure, including plain storage-offline
findings.evidence:
title: "Conversations couldn't be compared, so nothing can be selected",
      message: threadComparisonError,
      action: onResetMetadata
        ? (
          <button type="button" className="btn btn-ghost" onClick={onResetMetadata} disabled={busy}>Reset local sync state</button>
        )
        : undefined,
findings.impact: Every other reset-state affordance in the app gates on isIrrecoverableSyncError() — RestorePlanView.tsx:485, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:835 (twelve lines of the same file), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3168, syncOutcome.ts:243 — which matches only six specific corruption strings (src/components/project-sync/syncError.ts:9-14). This new banner skips that gate entirely, and `onResetMetadata` is always supplied (ProjectSync.tsx:3469), so the button always renders. thread_comparison_error is set verbatim from the storage-engine open failure whenever the remote read errors (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:7562-7564 `thread_comparison_error = Some(error.clone())`), i.e. R2 credentials wrong, network down, disk unmounted — and ProjectSync.tsx:1861 deliberately lets that case open the review. So the commonest transient failure now presents a red banner urging the user to run resetProjectSyncMetadata, which the confirm dialog (ProjectSync.tsx:2677) describes as forgetting "reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, Pull results, and saved Push/Pull plans" — irreversible local state destroyed to fix a Wi-Fi outage. Secondary defect on the same line: `message: threadComparisonError` prints the raw backend error string verbatim as user-facing copy.
findings.fix: Gate the action the way every other site does — `action: isIrrecoverableSyncError(threadComparisonError) && onResetMetadata ? … : undefined` — and use the `btn btn-ghost danger` class the other two reset buttons use. Wrap or map threadComparisonError into user copy before printing it, rather than passing the engine's error string through as `message`.

findings.title: "Dark theme" menu checkbox reports the resolved theme, so it shows checked while the stored preference is System and silently discards System when toggled
findings.evidence:
id: "theme",
        label: "Dark theme",
        icon: "moon" as const,
        checked: theme === "dark",
        onSelect: () => onThemeChange(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"),
findings.impact: `theme` is the RESOLVED theme (App.tsx:24 `const theme = choice === "system" ? osTheme : choice`), while `onThemeChange` is setThemeChoice, which only ever writes "light" or "dark". Rendered as role="menuitemcheckbox" with aria-checked (SyncPathBar.tsx:201-203), this item claims persistent state it does not hold: with the default choice of System (preferences.ts:55) on a dark-mode Mac the menu reads "Dark theme ✓" while SettingsPage's Appearance radiogroup reads System (SettingsPage.tsx:397 `aria-checked={themeChoice === choice.value}`). Both render on the same screen — SettingsPage passes appActions as its path-bar overflow at SettingsPage.tsx:376 and draws Appearance at :385 — so the user sees two theme controls disagreeing. Unticking the checkbox pins an explicit Light choice and permanently stops the app following the OS, with nothing said. The existing titlebar control avoids this by being a momentary button labelled "Switch to light/dark theme" (ProjectSync.tsx:2763-2770), never a checkbox. The comment at ProjectSync.tsx:2758-2759 ("theme lives on the Settings page there") is now stale as well.
findings.fix: Either drop `checked` and make the row the same momentary switch the titlebar uses (label it "Switch to light theme" / "Switch to dark theme" off the resolved theme), or read the stored choice via useThemeChoice() and offer all three states, so the menu and the Settings radiogroup can never disagree.

findings.title: Switcher menu's filter field cannot be reached by keyboard at all
findings.impact: Three mechanisms lock a keyboard user out of this input. (1) Opening the menu focuses options[0] — focusMenuOption at SyncPathBar.tsx:422-430 uses menuOptions(), whose selector is only '[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]' (menuKeyboard.ts:11), and the input carries no role, so focus lands past it on the first row. (2) Arrow/Home/End navigation runs through the same menuOptions list, so it can never step back onto the input. (3) Tab closes the menu outright — `if (event.key === "Tab") { onClose(false); return; }` at line 258, and the handler does not test shiftKey, so Shift+Tab closes it too. The field is therefore mouse-only, and the handler's own comment at line 265-266 ("The search field keeps its own Home/End and its characters; the arrows step from it into the list") describes a state no keyboard user can enter. The threshold is only six targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR, line 127), so any user with six projects or storages hits this. Additionally, a bare <input> inside role="menu" is not an allowed owned element, so AT in menu-navigation mode does not expose it either.
findings.fix: Focus the search field first when `searchable` (extend focusMenuOption to prefer '.sync-path-menu-search' when present), let ArrowUp from the first option return to it, and exempt the field from the Tab-closes-the-menu branch at line 258. Wrapping the input in a role="none" container and giving the menu a `aria-owns`-correct structure would also let AT reach it.

findings.title: In switcher menus a disabled item's reason is no longer rendered — it survives only as a title tooltip, contradicting the documented contract
findings.impact: PathBarMenuItem documents `disabled` as "rendered with aria-disabled so the row stays focusable and its reason reachable by keyboard" (line 38-41) and `disabledReason` as "rendered as its second line" (line 45). renderItem still honours that (line 179-181). renderPill does not: every verb and tail in a switcher menu now emits an icon/label-only button whose reason lives in `title` alone — a hover tooltip, which does not open on keyboard focus and is not part of the accessible name or description. Concrete cases now shipping: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2320-2323 "Link storage…" disabled with reason "Everything you've added is already linked" (a tail pill), and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1236-1238 "Unlink from <row>…" disabled with reason "This row is not linked to it yet" (a verb pill, icon-only). Before this change both printed the reason as a visible second line that AT read as part of the button. A keyboard or screen-reader user now arrows onto a dimmed control and is told nothing about why.
findings.fix: In renderPill, when `inert && item.disabledReason`, expose the reason as accessible text — e.g. render it into a visually-hidden span inside the button, or set aria-description/aria-describedby pointing at a rendered node — instead of relying on `title`. Alternatively render inert items through renderItem so they keep their reason line.

findings.title: Destructive "Unlink" verb renders as an unlabelled glyph whose tooltip never contains the word unlink
findings.evidence: {item.icon && } {tail && {item.label}}
findings.impact: The first unlabelled group of a switcher menu becomes `verbs` (line 169) and each verb is drawn by renderPill with `tail === false`, so only the icon paints — the label survives as aria-label and as `title`. But `title` is `verbTitle(item)`, which returns `item.title` when present (line 131-134). Both unlink verbs set an explanatory `title`: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2344 "Stop syncing this pairing; files already in storage are kept" and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1238 "Stop syncing this pairing; content already in storage is kept". So a sighted mouse user opening the storage crumb menu sees a bare link-off glyph, hovers it, and reads a sentence that never names the action or the target — the string "Unlink from HorrorGame…" that the item actually carries as its label is painted nowhere. The neighbouring cog ("Storage settings…") is equally unlabelled, so the footer strip reads as two anonymous glyphs where two named commands used to be.
findings.fix: Give verb pills a visible label (or at minimum make verbTitle prepend the label: `item.title ? `${item.label} — ${item.title}` : …`), so the destructive command is named in the tooltip and not only in aria-label.

findings.title: New `search` icon is never used and breaks the icon set's stroke grammar, rendering as scattered dots at the recommended size
findings.impact: Three confirmed problems. (1) Dead: `grep -rn 'icon="search"|name="search"|icon: "search"' src tests` returns nothing — no component renders it, and the one search field this diff adds (SyncPathBar.tsx:329) is a bare <input> with no icon. (2) Off-grammar stroke: the ring is drawn one viewBox unit thick at odd coordinates (`M3 6h1v1h-1Z`), whereas every established hollow mark uses two-unit stems on the even grid. Rasterizing the shipped `d` strings at the sampling the file's own docstring calls size={12} (one point per coarse cell) gives clean closed outlines for info, message, folder and catalog, and for `search` gives ~14 disconnected dots — it does not read as a magnifier. Its ink measures 14 of 144 cells against the set's measured 15–48 band (`plus` 15, `user` 22, `catalog` 25, `folder` 27, `tool` 48), i.e. lighter than every other named mark. (3) Broken geometry: the handle's first cell is (15,15) while the ring's nearest cell is (13,13); (14,14) is empty, so the handle floats detached from the ring even at size 24.
findings.fix: Either delete the `search` entry from IconName and the render block, or redraw it on the even two-unit grid the rest of the set uses, connect the handle to the ring, and land the ink in the 20–40 band — then actually use it in SyncPathBar's filter field.

findings.title: Capture-budget copy states 512 MB where the budget is 512 MiB
findings.evidence:
case "capture_budget":
        return "Not in this round — the review's 512 MB capture budget filled before this session's turn. Push the selected sessions first, then open Push review again.";
findings.impact: MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES is `512 * 1024 * 1024` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/provider_capture.rs:25) = 536,870,912 bytes = 512 MiB ≈ 537 MB. findings.title: project_files_error is declared and never read, so a failed Git-managed inventory silently removes the Project files step
findings.evidence:
project_files: ProjectContentInventory | null;
  project_files_error: string | null;
findings.impact: `grep -rn project_files_error src/` returns only this declaration — no component reads it. The backend sets it symmetrically with thread_comparison_error (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:7569-7571) and logs a warning for it (commands.rs:1493-1499) with the comment that the reason "must reach the log, not only the context the frontend may or may not render". For a Git project the frontend then computes `lockedProjectContentInventory` as null (ProjectSync.tsx:1875-1878) and `showProjectFiles: !isGitRepository || lockedProjectContentInventory !== null` (line 1918) — false. syncReviewSteps drops the tab entirely, so a failed inventory is indistinguishable from an empty one: the Project files step vanishes from the Push review with no banner, no tab, and no explanation. findings.title: ProjectActivityPage never withdraws its review-list-ready report on unmount, stranding the Pull button permanently disabled
findings.impact: In the Pull review this reports into `setReviewListReady` (RestorePlanView.tsx:598), and RestorePlanView gates its primary action on it: `activityHistoryInUse && !reviewListReady ? "Loading storage changes…"` (RestorePlanView.tsx:377), which disables the footer Pull button (line 692) and becomes its tooltip (line 693). ProjectActivityPage is mounted only while `activeStep === "history"` (RestorePlanView.tsx:575). Clicking the footer step navigator to "Project files" while the session comparison is still in flight unmounts the page with `false` as the last value reported and no cleanup to correct it. `activityHistoryInUse` (`conversationItems.length > 0 && Boolean(project)`) is step-independent, so Pull stays dead on the Project files step, tooltipped "Loading storage changes…", while nothing on screen is loading. The only escape is switching back to History and waiting for a full refetch. This directly breaks the promise in the comment at RestorePlanView.tsx:673 ("Pull stays live on both steps"). Every sibling report-up in the codebase does have the unmount cleanup — ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2333, RestorePlanView.tsx:398, SessionDetailPage.tsx:192, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:777 — this one is the sole outlier.
findings.fix: Add a cleanup to the effect at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2253 so the report is withdrawn on unmount, mirroring line 2333: `useEffect(() => { onReviewListReadyChange?.(reviewListReady); return () => onReviewListReadyChange?.(false); }, [reviewListReady, onReviewListReadyChange]);` — or, better, have RestorePlanView reset `reviewListReady` to false when the activity page is not mounted, so the gate is derived rather than remembered.

findings.title: The new switcher filter field is unreachable from the keyboard and invisible to a screen reader in menu mode
findings.impact: The field renders whenever a switcher has 6+ targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR, line 129) — 7+ registered projects on the Project crumb, 7+ storages on the Storage crumb, both ordinary states. It is a plain `<input>` with no tabIndex, and no path leads to it: (a) the menu focuses `menuOptions(root)[0]` on open (line 424), and `menuOptions` matches only `[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]` (menuKeyboard.ts:11), so the input is never in the roving order; (b) `moveMenuFocus` walks that same list, so ArrowUp from the first row wraps to the last row, never up into the field; (c) Tab and Shift+Tab are swallowed to close the menu — at the menu itself (line 258: `if (event.key === "Tab") { onClose(false); return; }`) and at each crumb opener (lines 516, 551, 618) — so it cannot be tabbed into either. Typing a printable character with focus in the list runs the type-ahead (line 283) instead of reaching the visible text box sitting right above it. Separately, `role="menu"` admits only the menuitem family — the rule this same file cites for its own banner at line 306 — so an `<input>` child is not exposed at all to a screen reader in menu navigation. Keyboard and AT users get a search box they can see but cannot use.
findings.fix: Move the field out of the `role="menu"` element (wrap the popover in a plain div, put the input above the menu and give the menu `aria-controls`/`aria-activedescendant` from it), focus the input instead of `options[0]` when `searchable`, and let ArrowUp from the first option return focus to it. At minimum, stop swallowing Tab when the field exists so it can be reached.

findings.title: A long switcher list runs off the bottom of the window: no max-height on the menu, and nothing in the shell can scroll
findings.impact: There is no `max-height` and no `overflow` on `.sync-path-menu` or on `.sync-path-menu.switcher` (line 3158), while `html, body, #root { overflow: hidden }` (line 7) and `.sync-app { overflow: hidden }` (line 804) mean the overflow is clipped at the window edge with no scrollbar anywhere. The menu opens at ~59px from the top (52px bar + 6px offset). Switcher chrome measures ~192px (header ~56, search 42, foot ~74 plus its 8px top margin, border+padding 12), and each target row is 34px (`.sync-path-menu-item { min-height: 34px }`, line 3100). At the window's configured `minHeight: 560` (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) only ~9 rows fit; at the default 720 height, ~13. With more projects than that — and the search field exists precisely because 6+ is expected — the `.sync-path-menu-foot` strip is clipped below the window edge. That strip is where every verb lives: for the Project crumb, Reveal in Finder, Agent profile…, Rename project…, Reset local sync state… and "Add project…" all become unreachable, with no scrollbar and no cue that they exist.
findings.fix: Cap the popover (`max-height: calc(100vh - 72px)` on `.sync-path-menu`) and make only the target-list region scroll (`overflow-y: auto` on a wrapper around the `lists.map(...)` output in SyncPathBar.tsx:340-349), leaving `.sync-path-menu-current`, `.sync-path-menu-search` and `.sync-path-menu-foot` pinned.

findings.title: Disabled reasons are dropped from the DOM in the switcher footer — only a hover tooltip carries them
findings.impact: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2314 states the contract in a comment — "Stays put at zero candidates and says why, instead of vanishing from the DOM for a reason the user cannot see" — and gives "Link storage…" `disabledReason: "Everything you've added is already linked"` (line 2321). That item lands in `tails`, so `renderPill` draws it with no detail line at all: the reason survives only as a `title` tooltip, which does not appear on keyboard focus in WKWebView and is not bound to the button by `aria-describedby`, so `aria-disabled` is announced with no explanation. The same loss hits the greyed "Unlink from …" verb in StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1235 (`disabledReason: "This row is not linked to it yet"`), which is additionally icon-only. `renderItem` (line 184), used for the list rows of the very same menu, still renders the reason as a second line — so the two halves of one popover now disagree about whether a greyed control explains itself.
findings.fix: In `renderPill`, when `inert && item.disabledReason`, render the reason in the DOM — either as a visible line below the pill row (it already has `flex-wrap: wrap` and a `.sync-path-menu-cap` slot at App.css:3225 that could carry it) or via a visually-hidden span wired with `aria-describedby` — rather than relying on `title` alone.

findings.title: With a single storage the Storage switcher collapses to a header and one unlabelled '+' glyph
findings.impact: Group roles are inferred from position, so a group's meaning changes when a neighbouring group disappears. The storage-settings page's crumb menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1706-1731) is `[ "Switch to"?, { items: [Add storage…] } ]` and the "Switch to" group is omitted whenever `storages.some(c => c.id !== editedStorageConfig.id)` is false — i.e. on any install with exactly one storage, which is where every new user starts. `populated[0]` is then the unlabelled Add group, so `verbs` claims it and `renderPill(item, false)` renders `{tail && {item.label}}` as false: a bare 32px "+" button with no text. `lists` is empty, so the menu body is empty too. Opening the Storage crumb there shows the storage you are already standing on (with a tick) plus an unlabelled "+", and the words "Add storage…" appear nowhere on screen — while the identical item renders as a labelled text pill the moment a second storage exists.
findings.fix: Give `PathBarMenuGroup` an explicit `role: "verbs" | "targets" | "more"` (defaulting to "more" for an unlabelled group) and select `verbs`/`lists`/`tails` from that instead of from `populated[0]`'s position, so a group's rendering does not change when a sibling group is empty.

`aria-label` on a bare `

The switcher branch also drops the visible `.sync-path-menu-label` heading that the headerless branch still renders three lines later (line 358), so the label is gone from both channels: the caller passes "Switch to", and it reaches neither eye nor ear. Any switcher that offers more than one named group (the shape the code explicitly supports — `lists` is a filtered array, not a single group) would render them as one undifferentiated run of rows with nothing separating them. The `

` on the next line is likewise a non-menuitem child of `role="menu"`, so the "No match." state is also unannounced.
findings.fix: Put `role="group"` on the wrapper so `aria-label` takes effect, and render the visible `.sync-path-menu-label` heading whenever `lists.length > 1`. Give the empty-state paragraph `role="presentation"` plus a visually-hidden live announcement, or move it outside the `role="menu"` subtree.

findings.title: The titlebar App actions popup declares role=menu with none of the keyboard contract the codebase requires
findings.evidence:
<div
          id="sync-app-actions-menu"
          className="storage-link-actions-menu"
          role="menu"
          aria-label="App actions"
          hidden={!appMenuOpen}
        >
findings.impact: This popup has no `onKeyDown` at all: no `moveMenuFocus`, no roving tabindex, and the open handler (line 2780, `onClick={() => setAppMenuOpen((current) => !current)}`) never moves focus into it. That is exactly the failure `menuKeyboard.ts:1-9` was written to prevent — "Declaring the role without this is a promise the widget does not keep: a screen reader switches to menu navigation and the arrow keys then do nothing." Every other popup in the app (SyncPathBar, BranchPicker, SessionDebugMenu, ProjectFileDetailsMenu, StorageCatalogPage's row menu) routes through that helper; this one does not. It renders on exactly the screens that have no path bar (project setup draft, Add Catalog resource, Projects index — ProjectSync.tsx:3722-3734), so on those screens it is the only app-level menu.
findings.fix: Route it through `menuOptions`/`moveMenuFocus`/`focusMenuEdge` from sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts like every other menu, or drop `role="menu"`/`aria-haspopup="menu"` and let it be a plain disclosure containing an ordinary button.

findings.title: session-detail-card-prompt and -reply are minted on every transcript card and styled by nothing
findings.evidence:
<div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-prompt">
...
    <div className="session-detail-card session-detail-card-reply">
findings.impact: Neither class appears anywhere in src/App.css (`grep -c 'session-detail-card-prompt' src/App.css` and the `-reply` equivalent both return 0), so the prompt card and the reply card paint identically: same `.session-detail-card` box, fill, border, radius and stamp band (App.css:7247, 10972). The same uncommitted change also removed the previous shape distinction — `.session-detail-response-prose` is gone from both the TSX and App.css — so in a long transcript the only remaining cue for who is speaking is the 12px glyph in the left rail (EventNode, line 263). The two hooks that would let the two speakers differ are present on every card and do nothing.
findings.fix: Either give `.session-detail-card-prompt` / `.session-detail-card-reply` a real distinction in App.css (fill, edge weight or stamp tint), or delete the two class names from SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and :346 so the markup stops implying a difference that does not exist.

findings.title: New `.flat` list frame double-boxes inside every container that already owns a frame — Push/Pull Files review and "Older activity"
findings.impact: The retheme turned every `.flat` thread list into a 2px ink box with a 14px radius and a hard cast shadow, and added carve-outs for only two of its four nesting contexts (`.sync-history-uncommitted` at App.css:9403 and `.sync-history-storage-only` at App.css:10019). The two that were missed both nest the list inside a container that is already a frame with `overflow: hidden`: `ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:573` renders `<div className="sync-history-thread-list flat">` directly inside `.sync-project-file-tile` (App.css:6450), and `ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2061`/`:2076` render it inside `details.sync-history-older-group` (App.css:6519). Measured in the running stylesheet at http://localhost:1420: the tile is 348px with a 2px ink border and the list inside it is 344px with its own 2px ink border — the two edges abut into a 4px double line down both sides, the inner list's 14px corners are clipped square by the parent's `overflow: hidden`, and its 2px 2px cast shadow is cut off at the right and bottom. The "Older activity" fold is worse: group (420px) > flat list (416px) > `details.sync-history-older-inert` > flat list (388px), three concentric ink boxes with three clipped shadows. Every directory tile on the Push and Pull Files review is affected, in both themes.
findings.fix: Add the same carve-out the other two contexts already have — `.sync-project-file-tile > .sync-history-thread-list.flat, .sync-history-older-group > .sync-history-thread-list.flat, .sync-history-older-inert > .sync-history-thread-list.flat { border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; box-shadow: none; }` — or invert the rule so the frame is opt-in (e.g. `.sync-history-thread-list.flat.framed`) and let only the page-level lists ask for it.

findings.title: The switcher menu's new search field cannot be reached by keyboard at all
findings.impact: The input carries no `role`, so `menuOptions()` (menuKeyboard.ts:11, selector `[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]`) never returns it — verified in the browser against the real stylesheet: with the switcher rendered, `menuOptions` yields 7 buttons and `opts.includes(input)` is `false`. Every keyboard route in is closed: opening the menu with ArrowDown/ArrowUp calls `focusMenuOption(...)` which focuses the first/last *menuitem*; `moveMenuFocus` only steps between menuitems; Tab is intercepted at SyncPathBar.tsx:258 (`if (event.key === "Tab") { onClose(false); return; }`) and by the crumb button's own handler, both of which close the menu before focus moves; and printable characters from a focused row go to the typeahead. So a keyboard-only user with 6+ storages or projects sees a filter field, cannot focus it, and must arrow through the entire list. Once focus has arrowed out of the field, there is no way back in either. Separately, an `<input>` is not a permitted child of `role="menu"` (only menuitem/group/separator), so a screen reader in menu-navigation mode will not expose it.
findings.fix: Give the field a place in the roving order and a legal ARIA shape: either restructure the popover as a combobox/listbox (`role="combobox"` on the input with `aria-controls` pointing at a `role="listbox"` of the targets), or keep `role="menu"` and focus the input on open, teach `menuOptions` to include it, and make ArrowUp from the first option return to it. Do not leave a mouse-only control inside a menu.

findings.title: Switcher footer holding every verb for the object scrolls off the window with nothing to scroll
findings.impact: The rewrite moved the object's verbs from the top of the menu (where the old `groups.map` rendered the unlabelled first group before the switch list) to a footer strip after the list. `.sync-path-menu` (App.css:3060) has no `max-height` and no `overflow`, `.sync-app` is `overflow: hidden` (App.css:809) and `html, body, #root` are `overflow: hidden` (App.css:7-11), so nothing scrolls. Measured in the browser at the app's own minimum window size (800x560, from src-tauri/tauri.conf.json), with the menu opening 98px below the top: at 9 switch targets the footer is already cut off (menu bottom 571 vs viewport 560); at 12 targets the menu is 575px tall and overruns by 113px, putting the whole footer — "Storage settings…", "Unlink from …", and "Add storage…" — past the clip with no way to see or click it. Keyboard focus still moves onto those clipped buttons (`moveMenuFocus` focuses them and no ancestor can scroll them into view), so focus lands on an invisible control. A user with 9+ storages or projects loses every command on that crumb.
findings.fix: Give `.sync-path-menu` a `max-height: calc(100vh - <bar+gutter>)` with the *target list* as the only scrolling region, so the header, the search field and the verb footer stay pinned and visible — or move the verbs back above the switch list so a long list truncates the switch targets rather than the commands.

findings.title: Switch targets lose the path that told two same-named projects or storages apart
findings.impact: Every caller supplies the path as the disambiguator: the project switcher passes `detail: compactProjectPath(candidate.project_root), detailIsPath: true` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2434-2436) and the storage switchers pass `detail: storageSubtitle(candidate), detailIsPath: storageSubtitleIsPath(candidate)` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1715-1716), which is `true` for every local storage. With `target && detailIsPath`, that second line is now suppressed and survives only in the `title` tooltip. Two checkouts of the same folder name (`~/a/app` and `~/b/app`, both labelled `app` by `projectLabel`) render as two identical rows; two local storages with no name render as two rows both reading `(unnamed)` with nothing else on them. The only disambiguator is a mouse-hover tooltip — unavailable to keyboard and screen-reader users, and unavailable at all to the search field's filter result, which still matches against the hidden path (line 177) so a user can type a path fragment and get back rows that do not show it. Reproduced in the browser: two rows both reading "app" with no second line.
findings.fix: Keep the path line on switch targets — it is the only thing that makes the row identifiable — and, if the one-line height is the goal, elide it (middle-truncate to the last two segments) rather than removing it, or show it only when two targets share a label.

findings.title: Positional group inference turns "Add storage…" into an unlabelled icon when it is the menu's only group
findings.impact: The storage-settings crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707-1731) builds its menu as `[...(other storages exist ? [{label: "Switch to", …}] : []), { items: [add-storage] }]` — it has no leading verbs group. When exactly one storage is configured (the ordinary first-run state) the "Switch to" group is spread away, `populated[0]` is the unlabelled `add-storage` group, and the heuristic classifies it as *verbs*. `renderPill(item, false)` then renders it with `aria-label={item.label}` and no `{item.label}` (SyncPathBar.tsx:232, 242), so "Add storage…" appears as a bare 32px "+" icon in the footer of an otherwise empty switcher, instead of the labelled text pill it is on every other crumb. Nothing on screen says what the button does.
findings.fix: Stop inferring roles from position. Tag the groups explicitly (e.g. `role: "verbs" | "targets" | "more"` on `PathBarMenuGroup`) and have `PathBarMenu` read the tag; short of that, treat a trailing unlabelled group as tails whenever it is not also the first group, i.e. only take `populated[0]` as verbs when `populated.length > 1`.

findings.title: Settings switch thumb declares `border-radius` twice; the pill shape is immediately overwritten
findings.impact: The retheme rounded the switch *track* to `var(--r-pill)` (App.css:4315) and added `border-radius: 50%` for the thumb, but left the old `border-radius: 2px` on the following line, which wins as the later declaration in the same block. Every toggle on the Settings page (Theme neighbours, 24-hour clock, open-logs-on-sync, refresh-on-focus) renders a square 12px block sliding inside a stadium track — the one control in the app that visibly contradicts the pill grammar the rest of the cutover adopted. This is the only duplicated property in all 10,997 lines of App.css (verified by a full block-level scan), so it is clearly an unfinished edit rather than an intentional fallback.
findings.fix: Delete `border-radius: 2px;` at App.css:4330 so the `50%` on the line above takes effect.

findings.title: Retheme's pill radius on the session SHOW toggles is dead — a later rule squares them back off
findings.impact: App.css:10983-10986 (`.session-detail-filter-toggle, .session-detail-filter-box { border-radius: 0; }`, commented "square corners") has identical 0,1,0 specificity and comes 3,995 lines later, so it wins unconditionally and the new `var(--r-pill)` never paints. The declaration is dead code, and the two edits state opposite intents for the same control — a maintainer changing either one will see no effect and has no way to tell which is authoritative. The rendered result today is the square toggle, so this is a code-hygiene defect rather than a visual one, but it is exactly the kind of silent source-order defeat the CSS gates cannot catch because they assert source text.
findings.fix: Settle the intent: either drop `border-radius: var(--r-pill)` at App.css:6988, or drop `.session-detail-filter-toggle` from the square-corner rule at App.css:10983 and keep the pill.

findings.title: New "Dark theme" item in the ⋯ menu silently discards the System theme preference with no way back from that surface
findings.evidence:
{
        id: "theme",
        label: "Dark theme",
        icon: "moon" as const,
        checked: theme === "dark",
        onSelect: () => onThemeChange(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"),
      },
findings.impact: `theme` here is the *resolved* theme (App.tsx:24: `const theme = choice === "system" ? osTheme : choice;`) while `onThemeChange` is `setThemeChoice`, which writes the *choice*. The app ships defaulting to System (preferences.ts: "Absence means System, so a fresh install follows the OS"), and the Settings page offers System/Light/Dark. Toggling this checkbox once converts a System user to a pinned Light or Dark and the app stops following macOS appearance from then on — with nothing in the menu saying so and no System option there to undo it. Because `checked` mirrors the resolved theme, the item looks identical before and after the conversion, so the user has no signal that anything but the colour changed.
findings.fix: Either drop the item and leave theme to Settings, or make it honest: render the three-way choice (System / Light / Dark) as `menuitemradio` rows keyed on `useThemeChoice()` rather than a two-state checkbox keyed on the resolved theme.

findings.title: DepartureMono font assets are still bundled after the retheme removed every reference to them
findings.impact: This replaced the `@font-face` for "Departure Mono" (HEAD App.css:7649) and the retheme dropped `--font-pixel` along with it; a repo-wide grep for `Departure` now hits only the untracked `codex-retheme-mockup.html`, so no production code references the face. `public/fonts/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2` (22KB) and `DepartureMono-OFL.txt` are still in `public/`, which Vite copies verbatim into `dist/`, so every shipped build carries a 22KB font nothing can load plus a licence file for a face the app no longer uses. (The Baloo 2 replacement itself checks out: the file really is a variable font with a `wght` axis of 400–800 matching the declared range, `public/fonts/` is Vite's static root so `/fonts/Baloo2-Variable.woff2` resolves, and no production string uses a codepoint outside its 230-glyph cmap.)
findings.fix: Delete `public/fonts/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2` and `public/fonts/DepartureMono-OFL.txt` as part of the cutover, per the repo's "delete the old path in the same change" rule.

findings.title: `--button-primary-border` became a dead token and `.btn-primary`'s base `color` a dead declaration in this cutover
findings.impact: The retheme removed all three `border-color: var(--button-primary-border)` consumers (base `.btn-primary`, `.sync-path-sync.active`, and the RetroTheme `.btn.btn-primary`) in favour of the shared `--box-border`, but left the token declared in both palettes (App.css:8019 and App.css:8128). It is now the only token this diff orphaned — a full var()-vs-declaration diff shows the other six unused tokens (`--accent-glow`, `--amber`, `--bg-3`, `--editor-active-line`, `--surface-overlay`, `--surface-subtle-hover`) were already dead at HEAD. In the same rule, `color: var(--text-0)` is now unreachable: every production emitter writes `btn btn-primary` (16 sites, all verified), so the higher-specificity `.btn.btn-primary { color: var(--button-primary-text) }` at App.css:8523 always wins. If that RetroTheme rule were ever scoped or reordered, the fallback would paint `#1e1817` on `#8a6347` — 3.15:1, a contrast failure — so the dead line is a live trap rather than harmless.
findings.fix: Delete `--button-primary-border` from both palette blocks and change App.css:336 to `color: var(--button-primary-text);` so the base rule agrees with the RetroTheme one instead of holding a failing fallback.

findings.title: Prompt/reply cards clip their own project-path tooltip (`overflow: hidden` on a box that contains an absolutely-positioned overlay)
findings.impact: Hovering (or keyboard-focusing) a project-file link inside a prompt or reply now shows a sliced path card instead of the path. Measured in a browser against this exact App.css: a link on the card's first prose line at a 862px card loses 39.5px of a 70px tooltip off the top (a screenshot shows the box cut flush with the card's top edge, its opening path segments gone); a link near the right edge at the page's 1380px cap loses 302px of the 520px card off the right, cutting off the file name at the end of the path — the part that identifies the target. The link's `onClick` opens that file in an external app (`onOpenProjectPath`), so the user commits to an off-app action without being able to read the destination. This is new in the uncommitted change: at HEAD replies were unboxed prose (`.session-detail-response-prose`) and `.session-detail-prompt-card` declared no `overflow`, so the tooltip escaped. Steps are still fine — `.session-detail-intermediate-prose` (App.css:7282) has no `overflow`, which is why only the two new cards are affected.
findings.fix: Drop `overflow: hidden` from `.session-detail-card` (App.css:7248). Nothing inside needs clipping — the card's scrollWidth equals its clientWidth at every width I measured (700/560/420/340px) once the tooltip pseudo is discounted, and the `pre` already scrolls itself. If the rounded head corners were the reason for it, give `.session-detail-card-head` its own `border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0` instead. Alternatively, render the path card through the existing `src/components/sync-review/TopLayer.tsx` portal, which already exists for exactly this escape problem.

findings.title: Prompt and reply prose lost the 45–75 character measure the rule above it still promises: 152 characters per line at the page's max width
findings.impact: Measured in the browser at `.session-detail-page`'s own `max-width: 1380px`: the prompt/reply copy box is 1314px of content, ≈152 characters per line by digit width (more for real prose, whose average glyph is narrower) at 14px/1.62. The step box beside it still holds 65. So the two kinds that carry the longest text — the user's prompt and the agent's reply — are the only ones that lost the cap, while the shortest kind keeps it, and the comment at line 7232 still states the contract. At HEAD both were capped: `.session-detail-prompt-card` carried `max-width: 68ch` and responses rendered as bare `.session-detail-event-copy`. On any maximized window the reply is now a wall of 150+ character lines.
findings.fix: Restore the cap on the new box: add `max-width: 68ch` to `.session-detail-card` (App.css:7247), which keeps the card and its copy in step and lets the `@container session-detail-layout (max-width: 720px)` block at App.css:7861 keep releasing it — that block currently only resets `.session-detail-event-copy`, which for a card is already `none`.

findings.title: Tool-call action labels fail WCAG 1.4.3 on an expanded row in light theme (READ 3.93:1, EDIT 4.20:1 at 9px)
findings.impact: Measured against this App.css in both themes. Light theme, on the open row's `--surface-row-active` (#f0e3d5): `cat-read` (`--session-detail-link` → #2c779c) = 3.93:1 and `cat-file_edit` (`--session-detail-amber` → #8e640f) = 4.20:1, both at `--type-3xs` (9px, uppercase, letter-spacing 1px), so the 4.5:1 small-text bar applies. Expanding a Read or Edit call therefore makes that row's own action label the least legible text on the page, exactly when the user is reading it. Two more rendered sites on the same open row fall short: `.session-detail-tool-status` (App.css:7637, `--danger-text` #be3824) = 4.41:1 — this is the concrete DOM instance of the already-confirmed R2 — and its `.status-incomplete` variant (App.css:7647) inherits the amber at 4.20:1. `.session-detail-truncation` (App.css:7763) measures 4.43:1 on the payload pane. On the closed row every one of these passes (4.72–5.67), which is why the failures only appear after a click. Dark theme passes everywhere (worst 5.74). The page-scoped comment at App.css:6852-6857 asserts the opposite — that mixing body colour into `--yellow` and `--blue` "clears the bar" — and the css-hygiene gate never measures signal inks on a row surface.
findings.fix: Either darken the two page-scoped mixes at App.css:6858-6859 until they clear 4.5:1 on #f0e3d5 (the `--purple` mix at 7618 already does, at 5.23:1), or stop tinting the open row: give `.session-detail-tool-call[open] > summary` (App.css:7587) the same `--surface-row` the closed row uses and mark open state with the chevron alone. Then extend tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx to measure `--session-detail-amber`/`--session-detail-link` against `--surface-row-active`, which is the surface no current assertion covers.

findings.title: Keyboard focus on a tool-call row draws the ring in the same ink as the 2px border it sits inside
findings.impact: `--box-border: 2px solid var(--accent)` (App.css:7955) and `--focus-ring: var(--accent)` (App.css:8078 dark, 8190 light) resolve to the identical computed colour — I read both off the rendered element: light `rgb(42, 33, 29)` border vs `rgb(42, 33, 29)` ring, dark `rgb(239, 231, 212)` vs `rgb(239, 231, 212)`. With `outline-offset: -2px` the ring lands immediately inside that border, so tabbing onto a tool-call row changes nothing but edge thickness (2px → 4px of the same ink) with no colour change and no gap. At HEAD the summary had no border at all (`border-radius: 3px`, no `border`), so the inset ring read clearly against the row fill; the retheme's `--box-border` swallowed it. This does not contradict the verified `--focus-ring` reading of 12.49/12.51 — that measured the ring against opaque *surfaces*; the adjacent colour here is a border of the ring's own colour, which WCAG 2.4.11 requires 3:1 against (measured 1:1).
findings.fix: Change `outline-offset` to a positive value at App.css:7593 so the ring sits outside the box on the page ground (`.session-detail-event:focus-visible` at App.css:7156 already uses `outline-offset: 3px` for this reason), or give the ring its own token that is not `--accent`. Audit the other `outline-offset: -2px` rules for the same collision — `.session-detail-payload-action:focus-visible` (App.css:7698) is safe because its border is `--button-border`, not `--accent`.

findings.title: A prompt card's turn duration is computed from the filtered event set, so the new tool-calls-off default silently drops it
findings.impact: `events` is the filtered page, so the duration a prompt card prints depends on which kinds are toggled on. The uncommitted `toolCalls: false` default (sessionDetailModel.ts:94) makes the under-reporting case the one users open into. Verified by running the real production functions against a Claude-shaped turn (prompt at t, intermediate step at t+30s, tool call at t+600s, no terminal response — the shape you get whenever the last assistant message was followed by a tool call, i.e. every still-running or interrupted turn): default kinds resolve to `prompt,response,checkpoint`, `sessionTurnDurationLabel` returns `null`, and the same turn with Tool calls toggled on returns `10m`. So the card shows no duration at all for a ten-minute turn, and toggling an unrelated view filter makes a fact appear or change on a card whose own content did not change. The head still prints "1 call" from `turn_tool_summary` on that same card, so the card asserts work happened while refusing to say how long it took.
findings.fix: Compute spans from a source that does not move with the filter — carry the turn extent on the prompt event alongside `turn_tool_summary` (the backend already attaches per-turn data at crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/claude/history.rs:696), or request the turn's bounds independently of `included_event_kinds`. Failing that, drop the duration from the head rather than print a number that means "extent of whatever is currently visible".

findings.title: Every markdown link in session prose renders a junk `node="[object Object]"` attribute
findings.impact: react-markdown v10 (package.json:32) calls custom components with `passNode: true` (node_modules/react-markdown/lib/index.js:355 → node_modules/hast-util-to-jsx-runtime/lib/index.js:339-340 `props.node = node`). The destructure keeps `node` in `props`, and the spread puts it on the DOM element. Confirmed by rendering the same component shape through `renderToStaticMarkup` in this repo's own dependency tree: output is `docs`, with no React warning to surface it. Every link in every prompt, reply and step body carries the attribute, and the hast node (which holds source position data) is stringified on each render. Harmless to render, but it pollutes the DOM a maintainer inspects and defeats any future attribute selector on links.
findings.fix: Destructure it out: `a: ({ href, children, node: _node, ...props })` at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:158. The sibling `img` renderer (line 120) already avoids this by not spreading.

findings.title: `session-detail-card-prompt` and `session-detail-card-reply` are emitted but have no CSS rule anywhere, so the two speakers' cards render identically
findings.impact: `grep -n "session-detail-card-prompt\|session-detail-card-reply" src/App.css` returns nothing — the only rules are on the shared `.session-detail-card` (7247), `.session-detail-card > .session-detail-event-copy` (7255) and `.session-detail-card-head` (7263). Both modifiers are inert, so a prompt and a reply are byte-identical boxes and the entire speaker distinction rests on the 24px rail tile's glyph. That is the stated design, but the two dead hooks make the stylesheet look like it distinguishes them when it does not, and tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:339-343 asserts them as source text, so the pair will survive indefinitely without ever being styled.
findings.fix: Either give the two modifiers a job (the reply card is the one place a subtler fill would cost nothing) or drop them from SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and :346 and relax the two test regexes to match `session-detail-card` alone.

findings.title: A lower-bound single tool call prints "1+ call" instead of "1+ calls" in the card stamp
findings.impact: `formatSessionCount` renders a `lower_bound` count as `${value}+` (sessionDetailModel.ts:178-182), but the plural is chosen from the raw `value`, so a lower bound of 1 reads "1+ call" — verified by running both functions: `1+ call`, `2+ calls`. "1+" means at least one and possibly more, which is plural. Reachable: the per-turn summary is minted with the session-wide `tool_quality` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/claude/history.rs:696-703 and codex/history.rs:1062-1069), which drops to `LowerBound` whenever the projection sees an orphan tool result (`mark_tools_lower_bound`, history.rs:551) — so any turn with exactly one indexed call in such a session prints it.
findings.fix: Pluralise on the rendered string rather than the raw value at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:309, e.g. `callCount.value === 1 && callCount.quality === "exact" ? "call" : "calls"`.

findings.title: Push review's "Remove from storage" control is never wired, so no project file can be deleted from storage and the whole Push deletion-safety UI is unreachable
findings.impact: `onToggleRemoval` has no production caller anywhere in `src/` (grep confirms only the four hits inside ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx itself), so the trash button on a Push project-file card never renders and `pushProjectContentRemovals` is permanently empty — every one of the eight assignments in ProjectSync.tsx writes `new Set()`. A user who deletes a file from the project folder has no way to remove it from storage: the next Push leaves the stored copy in place (`publishPendingPush` at ProjectSync.tsx:2191 only strips recipe entries listed in that always-empty set), and the next Pull re-adds the file locally. Everything downstream is dead with it — the "Removes from storage" card badge, the `.removal` card style, the Push impact row's "Delete files / Delete folders" counts (always 0), and the "Approve removal of N files and M folders from storage" acknowledgement in ProjectFileCommitImpact, which can never appear on Push.
findings.fix: In PushResourceWorkspace.tsx, pass `onToggleRemoval` through to `<ProjectFilesReviewPage mode="push">` (a new prop on the workspace, wired in ProjectSync.tsx to a `setPushProjectContentRemovals` toggler alongside the existing `onToggleProjectContentWarning`). If removal from storage is genuinely not a shipped capability, delete `onToggleRemoval`, `removalIds`, the `removal` card branch and `ProjectFileCommitImpact`'s `deletionTarget="storage"` copy instead of leaving a documented affordance that cannot be reached.

findings.title: Path-bar Push commits the review without the project-file deletion acknowledgement that gates the footer Push button
findings.impact: The Push review has two identical "Push" commit controls — the footer primary and the path-bar verb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2678 calls `inlineStorageReview?.onContinue?.()`, which is `publishPendingPush`). The footer one refuses to fire until the user ticks "Approve removal of N files and M folders from storage"; the path-bar one has no such condition and publishes the same removals in one click, with a generic title ("Push the selected resources to this storage") that never mentions deletion. `pushReviewBlockingCount` cannot cover the gap — it explicitly skips removals (`if (projectContentRemovals.has(resourceId)) continue;`, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:187). The Pull side proves the intended contract: RestorePlanView reports `primaryDisabledReason` (including the same deletion gate) up through `onPrimaryChange`, and ProjectSync.tsx:3482 mirrors it into `continueDisabled`. Today the bypass is latent only because the removal UI is unreachable (see the previous finding); restoring that wiring makes it live.
findings.fix: Give PushResourceWorkspace the same `onPrimaryChange` reporting RestorePlanView already has (RestorePlanView.tsx:390-397): surface `pushDisabledReason` to ProjectSync and set `continueDisabled: pushReviewPrimary?.disabledReason !== null` plus `continueTitle` at ProjectSync.tsx:3400, so the path-bar verb and the footer button share one gate.

findings.title: Crumb switcher menus render every verb — including the destructive ones — as an unlabelled icon pill, so "Reset local sync state" is a bare trash glyph
findings.impact: Uncommitted regression in SyncPathBar.tsx. Any crumb with a `menuHeader` is now a "switcher": its first unlabelled group becomes icon-only pills in a footer strip (`const verbs = ... populated[0].items`, line 168). Before this change those were full rows with visible text. The project crumb's strip is now four naked glyphs — folder, terminal, pencil, trash — where the trash is `Reset local sync state…` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2420-2427), which discards reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records and saved plans. The storage crumb's strip is [gear][link-off], where link-off is `Unlink from <project>…` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2283-2296); the Catalog scope crumb's is [refresh][pencil][trash], where trash is `Remove this Catalog row…` (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1307-1315). Worse, when there is only one project (or one Catalog row) `lists` is empty and the menu degenerates to a header row plus a strip of unnamed icons — no readable text at all. The only per-verb name left is a hover `title`, and the one caption that does print (`caption`, line 178) names just the Agent-profile verb, implying the rest are unnamed by design.
findings.fix: In `renderPill`, render the label for verbs as well as tails (drop the `tail &&` guard on the `<span>`), or drop back to `renderItem` rows for any group containing a `danger: true` item. At minimum, extend the footer caption to name every verb rather than only the ones carrying a `detail`.

findings.title: Switcher menus drop the visible disabled reason that the item contract promises, leaving greyed pills unexplained
findings.impact: In the storage crumb switcher, `Link storage…` carries `disabledReason: "Everything you've added is already linked"` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2320-2322) and `Unlink from …` in the Catalog storage crumb carries `disabledReason: "This row is not linked to it yet"` (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239). Both now fall in the tail/verb strip, where the reason exists only as a hover tooltip — invisible to keyboard and touch users, and gone from the screen-reader text since `renderItem`'s second-line `<small>` is what used to carry it. The user sees a greyed control with no stated cause, which is exactly the failure mode the comment at line 38-42 ("the menu never changes shape for a cause the user cannot see") was written to prevent.
findings.fix: Render the disabled reason for inert pills — e.g. append it to the pill's `aria-label` and print it in the `.sync-path-menu-cap` caption line above the strip — or keep any item with a `disabledReason` in the row list instead of demoting it to a pill.

findings.title: "Reset Mallard" and "Delete all logs" carry a `danger` class that no CSS rule matches, so the app's most destructive buttons render as ordinary ghost buttons
findings.impact: `src/App.css` is the only stylesheet (App.tsx:10). Its complete set of `danger` selectors is `.notice .btn.danger` (1382), `.sync-sync-review-recovery-actions .danger` (6303), and a handful of component-specific ones (`.sync-path-menu-item.danger`, `.sync-path-menu-verb.danger`, `.catalog-card-ack.danger`, …) — none of which match a `btn btn-ghost danger` sitting in a `SettingsRow` control. So `Reset Mallard` (permanently deletes all of ~/.mallard including the only local backups of files Pull replaced), `Delete all` retained logs (SettingsPage.tsx:643) and the icon-only `Remove storage` trash (StorageSettings.tsx:274) all paint in `--text-1` — identical to the neutral `Open folder` and `Clean up now` buttons beside them. The retheme makes it worse: `.btn.btn-ghost` (App.css:8518) drops the box shadow and lowers font-weight to `--weight-medium`, so the single most destructive control in the product is the visually lightest button on its page. The token needed for the fix (`--danger-text`) already measures 5.05:1 light / 7.14:1 dark against `--surface-footer` and 5.26 / 6.69 against `--button-bg`, so no contrast work is required.
findings.fix: Add a global `.btn.danger { color: var(--danger-text); }` (with a `border-color`/hover treatment) in App.css beside the other `.btn` variants, rather than keeping the rule scoped to `.notice`; verify by computed style, since the existing CSS gates assert source text and cannot see this.

findings.title: The "Clear storage data" confirmation is an info-kind dialog with a generic OK button, weaker than the confirmation for cleaning up log files
findings.impact: `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` documents `kind` as defaulting to `info` (node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog/dist-js/index.d.ts:199). The only irreversible cloud-data deletion in the product therefore shows the info icon and the platform-default "OK"/"Cancel" pair, where OK is the default button that Return activates. By contrast the far milder log cleanup passes `{ kind: "warning", okLabel: "Delete logs" }` (SettingsPage.tsx:213) and `resetMallard` passes `{ kind: "warning", okLabel: "Reset Mallard" }` (SettingsPage.tsx:258). A user who dismisses the dialog with Return — the same reflex that dismisses "Discard draft", which uses the identical chrome — deletes every synced project repository and Library resource in that storage.
findings.fix: Pass `{ title: "Clear storage data", kind: "warning", okLabel: "Clear storage data", cancelLabel: "Cancel" }` at ProjectSync.tsx:3250, matching the pattern already used for log deletion and Reset Mallard.

findings.title: The "Delete all" logs confirmation omits the file count and size that the milder cleanup confirmation states
findings.evidence:
const approved = await confirm(
      deleteAll

Mallard configuration, backups, local files, and cloud revisions will not be changed."
        : `Remove retained logs older than ${stats.policy.retention_days} days?

${stats.file_count} log file${stats.file_count === 1 ? "" : "s"} (${formatBytes(stats.total_bytes)}) ${stats.file_count === 1 ? "is" : "are"} currently retained. Removed logs cannot be recovered.`,

The user approving the larger deletion is told less about what is being destroyed than the user approving the smaller one, even though `stats.file_count` and `stats.total_bytes` are already in scope on the line below.

findings.title: A folder tile's select-all checkbox acts on the whole subtree while the tile only shows search-filtered, capped rows
findings.impact: `groups` is built from `shownCards` (search-filtered, capped at `PROJECT_FILE_CARD_RENDER_LIMIT = 500`), but `renderTileHead`'s checkbox calls `setSubtree`, which filters the unfiltered `rows`. With a search active, a `src/` tile showing two matching cards and labelled "Include every file in src/" selects every selectable row under `src/` — potentially hundreds the user cannot see without clearing the search. On a Pull review this is a write decision: `rowIsSelectable` does not exclude `delete_file` / `delete_directory` rows in pull mode, so one click can queue local deletions for files the filter has hidden. The footer deletion count and approval checkbox do surface the total afterwards, but nothing at the moment of the click says the action reached beyond the visible cards.
findings.fix: Scope `setSubtree` and `subtreeSelection` to the rows the tile is actually showing while a search or render cap is in effect, or re-label the head control and its `aria-label` to say it covers the whole subtree and print the hidden-row count beside it.

findings.title: Menu type-ahead cannot reach the switcher's tail pills, because they expose neither a `.sync-path-menu-copy` label nor an `aria-label`

Typing "a" in an open project switcher never focuses "Add project…" — the keyboard user gets silence and has to arrow past the whole switch-to list instead. findings.fix: Wrap the tail label in `.sync-path-menu-copy > span` the way `renderItem` does, or give tails an `aria-label` as well as visible text so the existing lookup chain resolves.

findings.title: H02 (still open) — portalled details popovers never take focus, and the first Tab closes them

findings.title: M03 (still open) — three menu patterns still open without moving focus into the menu

findings.title: M13 (still open) — root overflow is clipped and the sidebar has a hard 220px floor, so 400% zoom has no escape
findings.impact: Nothing at the document level can scroll. findings.fix: Allow the shell to scroll instead of clipping at the root, or auto-collapse the sidebar below a viewport threshold rather than relying on the toggle. Replace fixed `height` on text-bearing controls with `min-height` plus padding so they grow with the root font size.

findings.title: M14 (still open) — delayed loading is a named region, never an announced status

            label: "Add Catalog resource…",
findings.impact: Adjacent items in one menu name the same object type two ways, and the tooltip on the first uses "resources" for the *contents* of that object — so "resource" means both the container and the things inside it. The Add flow's h1 is "Add Catalog resource" (AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:208) and the index page repeats it (CatalogIndexPage.tsx:37/49), while the path bar's menuLabel is "Catalog row" (line 1279), which SyncPathBar.tsx:332 interpolates into the switcher search placeholder as "Switch catalog row…" and its aria-label as "Filter catalog row list". A user cannot tell whether Remove deletes their skills or just the listing.
findings.fix: Choose one user-facing name for the (kind × profile) pairing — "Catalog group" reads correctly in all four positions — and apply it at StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1279/1311/1337/1931-1932, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:208, CatalogIndexPage.tsx:37/49 and ProjectSidebar.tsx:939-940. Keep "resource" for the individual skills, pets and plugins only.

findings.title: "this Mac" and "this computer" name the same machine in adjacent branches of one status-label function
findings.impact: `rowStatusLabel` writes the badge sentence for every Catalog row, and two of its branches disagree about what to call the local machine — the same list can show "Only on this Mac" and "Only on this computer" one row apart. The split runs through the whole app (22 "this Mac", 25 "this computer", 12 "this machine"), including inside single files: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:499 vs :641 both describe an unsynced session, and ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:61 vs :209 both describe an absent file. A third noun reads as a third place.
findings.fix: Standardise on "this computer" (the majority form, and the only one that is not macOS-specific) and sweep the three variants across src/components/storage-catalog/model.ts:106/129/154, StorageCatalogPage.tsx (15 sites), ProjectActivityPage.tsx:641/648, ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:209/212, ProjectBindingEditor.tsx and ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx.

findings.title: Reset-local-sync-state confirmation lists five internal data-model nouns, one of which appears nowhere else in the product
findings.evidence: `Reset local sync state for “${projectLabel(summary)}”?\n\nMallard will forget this project's reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, Pull results, and saved Push/Pull plans. Project files, provider sessions, project setup, recipes, storage configuration, and cloud data will not be deleted.`,
findings.impact: This is the confirmation for a destructive, irreversible action, so its job is to let the user weigh what goes against what stays — but "reviewed sync bases", "conversation mappings", "recovery records" and "recipes" are backend type names with no UI presence. "recipes" is `BundleRecipe`, the saved Push selection; a grep of every production component finds the word in no other user-visible string, so the reassurance "recipes … will not be deleted" reassures about something the reader has never seen named. The path-bar tooltip for the same action (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2426) already uses a shorter, equally opaque list.
findings.fix: Rewrite the dialog in the nouns the UI shows: what is forgotten is "which versions you have already reviewed, and any Push or Pull selections you saved"; what is kept is "your files, your sessions, your project setup, your storages, and everything already in storage". Update ProjectSync.tsx:2679 and the matching tooltip at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2426 together.

findings.title: "Clear current selection" is an icon-only trash button inside a review that deletes files
findings.impact: The button only unticks checkboxes, but it wears the trash glyph with no visible text, sitting in the header of a review whose selected rows include "Delete file" and "Delete folder" operations (ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:74-75). The same trash icon is used for genuinely destructive actions elsewhere — "Remove this Catalog row…" (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1312) and "Reset local sync state" (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:840, SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:22) — so a user reasonably reads it as "delete the selected files" and avoids it, or clicks it expecting a confirmation that never comes.
findings.fix: In src/components/sync-review/SyncReviewSelectionBar.tsx:62-69 swap `name="trash"` for a non-destructive glyph ("x", already in the icon set and used by the close button below it) and reserve trash for actions that remove data.

findings.title: Push review's empty state tells the user to Refresh; that screen has no refresh control
findings.evidence: No project resources discovered Refresh after the provider has created tasks, sessions, or project configuration.
findings.impact: This renders inside the Push review (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:768) when the session list comes back empty. The Push review header holds only the title, the recommended/clear/close cluster and the step tabs — a grep for refresh in PushResourceWorkspace.tsx finds no control, only the spinner glyph at line 901 — and the path bar's refresh button belongs to the workspace behind the review. The one instruction the empty state gives cannot be carried out without closing the review, which the copy never says. It also introduces "tasks" as a fourth noun for the objects the same review calls sessions, conversations and resources.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence to name the action that is actually available — "Close this review and use Refresh, then open Push again once the agent has recorded a session." — or pass an onRefresh handler into ResourceInventory and render a real button beside the message. Drop "tasks" from the list.

findings.title: Session-detail readout counts permanently filtered-out events as merely not-yet-loaded
findings.impact: `coverage.total` sums every supported kind regardless of the filter state (sessionDetailModel.ts:149-160), while `loadedCount` is `events.length` — the page fetched with `included_event_kinds` from the active filters. The uncommitted change to default `toolCalls` to false means an agent session with 800 tool calls and 40 prompt/response events now opens reading "40 of 840 events" with no Load-more button (SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:156 renders it only when `nextCursor` is set, and the filtered query exhausts immediately). The readout's stated purpose — how much of the record is on screen — is now wrong on first open of every real session.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailToolbar.tsx:31-34 compute the denominator from the enabled filters only (sum sessionFilterCount over the keys where filters[key] is true) so the readout tracks pagination, and state the hidden kinds separately, e.g. "40 of 40 shown · 800 tool calls hidden".

findings.title: New capture-budget copy calls the same rows "conversations" in the banner and "sessions" in the row detail
findings.impact: Both strings are new in this working tree and both describe the identical blocker on the identical screen: the banner at the top of the Push review says "Push the selected conversations first" and hovering one of the blocked rows says "Push the selected sessions first". A reader has to decide whether "conversations" and "sessions" are the same set. "capture budget" is also implementation vocabulary (MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES in crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/provider_capture.rs:25) that names a limit the user cannot see or change.
findings.fix: Use "session" in both, matching the rest of the review, and phrase the limit in user terms: "This round could only read 512 MB of transcripts, and these were past the limit." Edit PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:574-575 and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1120.

findings.title: Projects index heading never inflects: renders "1 projects · 1 storage · 1 links"
findings.evidence: {projects.length} projects · {storages.length} storage · {links.length} links
findings.impact: Three counts, none pluralised: "projects" and "links" are always plural (wrong at 1) and "storage" is always singular (wrong at 0 and at 2+). Every other count string in this file inflects correctly (e.g. line 1787 `project${storageLinkCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}`, line 2947 `location${…}`), so this line reads as unmaintained. Note the render path is narrow — the block sits after the early return at line 2230 and requires `editingStorage` truthy with `storageDraft` falsy, a pairing every setEditingStorage call site keeps in lockstep — so this header may in fact be unreachable, which is itself worth resolving.
findings.fix: Either inflect all three counts the way line 1787 does, or — if the block is confirmed dead — delete the `profile-links-heading` branch at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2752-2772 along with its `.profile-links-counts` rules in App.css:3674 and 8389.

findings.title: Catalog Pull failure notice drops the singular noun the surrounding code computes
findings.impact: `noun` is computed on the line directly above and used correctly in the two success notices below (1142-1143), but the failure branch reaches past it for `kind.plural` unconditionally. Pulling a single skill that fails produces "Pulled 0 of 1 skills — 1 failed." This is the one slip in a file that otherwise inflects at six other sites (940, 1055, 1061, 1120, 1133, 1538).
findings.fix: In src/components/storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1136 use the `noun` already in scope, keyed off `Object.keys(choices).length` rather than `applied` since that is the number the noun follows.

findings.title: Repo chooser always writes "resources" even when a repo holds one
findings.evidence: rev {match.revision ?? "—"} {match.resource_count ?? 0} resources
findings.impact: The meta column of each choosable repo reads "1 resources" whenever a repo holds a single item, in a radio list the user is being asked to pick from carefully. The same line also abbreviates "rev" while the equivalent chip on the storage settings screen spells it out — ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:455 renders `Revision` for the identical field — so the two places the user compares repos label the same number differently.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:145 add the singular branch (`resource${(match.resource_count ?? 0) === 1 ? "" : "s"}`) and change "rev" on line 143 to "Revision" to match ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:455.

findings.title: Logs drawer is titled "log" in lower case, and a genuinely empty log blames the filters
findings.evidence:
log ... ...
No entries match these filters.
findings.impact: The panel's own visible title is lower-case "log" and its clear button is lower-case "clear", while the region wrapping it is named "Logs" (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:187), the sidebar trigger reads "Logs" (ProjectSidebar.tsx:749) and Settings says "Logs", "Log files" and "activity logs" — four spellings of one feature, and a visible name that does not match its accessible name. Separately, line 358 is the only empty state: on a fresh install with every filter on and no search, the drawer asserts that entries exist and the filters are hiding them, sending the user to adjust controls that will change nothing.

findings.title: Projects landing page names only Codex in a two-provider app
findings.evidence:
Project history

Select a completed project to view its Codex history.
findings.impact: This is the main pane a user lands on with no project open. The app supports Codex and Claude — providerLabel (model.ts:181) derives the name from the key, storage-catalog/model.ts:17 returns "Codex" or "Claude", and the Add-Catalog kind cards say "Codex and Claude" — so a Claude user is told the page shows Codex history. "completed project" is also internal vocabulary for a project whose setup draft is finished; nothing on screen defines it, and the sentence gives no way to complete one.
