findings.title: A file row calls the same entry a "Folder" and a "Directory" one click apart
findings.evidence: {isDirectory ? "Folder" : fileKindLabel(row.relativePath)} ... entryTypeLabel={isDirectory ? "Directory" : row.entryType === "blocked" ? "Blocked entry" : "Regular file"}
findings.impact: The visible Kind chip on the row reads "Folder" and the details popover opened from that same row reports "Type: Directory" (ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:50). The rest of the review consistently uses "folder" — "Delete folder", "Create folder" (lines 75-76), "Approve deletion of N … empty local folders" (ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx:33) — so "Directory" is the outlier and reads as a different classification.
findings.fix: In src/components/project-sync/ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:426 change "Directory" to "Folder" so the chip and the popover agree; the same swap applies to "Regular file" versus the chip's file-kind label if you want the popover to stop introducing a second vocabulary.

r.coverage:
WHAT I READ AND RAN
- Computed the real production import graph from src/main.tsx with a script (57 files) so mockups were excluded by construction, not by filename guessing. Confirmed src/*mockup*.tsx, plugin-icons.tsx, no-commit-icons.tsx and plug-diagonal.tsx are NOT reachable from main.tsx and do not leak.
- Read src/terminology.ts and traced every call: userFacingRepoTerms is used in exactly two places (LogPanel.tsx:125, storageError.ts:13). Nothing else in the tree translates Bundle→Repo, which is why "Repository ID"/"Repo"/"repository" diverge freely in hand-written JSX.
- Swept every user-visible string in the production set: JSX text nodes, and string/template literals in title, aria-label, aria-valuetext, placeholder, label, summary, notify(), confirm() and Notice title/message. Read in full: ProjectSync, ProjectLinksWorkspace, ProjectActivityPage, PushResourceWorkspace, RestorePlanView, pullReviewModel, ProjectFilesReviewPage, ProjectFilesActivityPage, ProjectFileDetailsMenu, ProjectSetupWorkspace, ProjectBindingEditor, BundleConnectionDialog, SettingsPage, StorageSettings, StorageIndexPage, ConversationPathRepairNotice, SyncOutcomeNotice, syncOutcome, syncError, storageError, ResourceInventory, LogPanel, ActivityLogDrawer, StartupLoadingScreen, ProjectSidebar, SyncPathBar, SyncReviewSelectionBar, SyncReviewTabs, reviewSteps, the six session-detail files, and all three storage-catalog files plus model.ts.
- Reviewed the uncommitted diff for each changed frontend file (SyncPathBar +217, SessionDetailEvent +74, PushResourceWorkspace +34, ProjectSidebar +16, sessionDetailModel, Icons, ProjectSync, ProjectActivityPage, types.ts). Three findings (capture-budget nouns, the session-detail readout, the switcher search placeholder folded into the Catalog-naming finding) are new defects introduced by this working tree.
- Checked count-driven copy systematically: grepped every interpolation adjacent to a countable noun and verified the n===1 branch. Most of the app inflects correctly; the three that do not are reported.
- Verified claims against the Rust backend rather than assuming: FailedAction's only construction site (service.rs:11927) hardcodes display_name: None; the BindingChanged reason's own backend message (service.rs:7318) says "an agent profile"; the stale-action error format (service.rs:9359) uses {:?}; generated_named_id (mallard-domain/lib.rs:437) produces action-<24 hex>; MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES is 512 MiB (provider_capture.rs:25).
- Traced reachability before reporting. Two candidates were dropped for being unreachable: pullReviewModel.ts's "task" strings (blockedConversationDetail is filtered out by VISIBLE_PULL_CONVERSATION_ACTIONS, and the conversation ItemList only renders when `project` is undefined, which ProjectSync.tsx:3487 normally supplies), and ConversationPathRepairNotice's degenerate "0 conversations point to 0 different project paths" (unreachable because service.rs sets ready = issues.is_empty() && blockers.is_empty()). "512 MB" was also dropped: format.ts deliberately labels binary units KB/MB/GB, so the copy is internally consistent.
- Confirmed the Pull-review display_title question from memory: pullReviewModel.ts:273 does assign row.display_title to item.threadTitle, and syncOutcome.ts:174 reads it — but item.title stays the kind label "Conversation" by design (documented at pullReviewModel.ts:16-17) and the RestorePlanView list that would print it is only reached when `project` is null, so the old banner-title bug is not live. The related defect that IS live is the failed-row fallback at syncOutcome.ts:204.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK
- Nothing was rendered. All findings are from source; I did not run the app, the frontend suite, or a browser, so I cannot report on how these strings wrap, truncate, or are announced in VoiceOver's actual reading order.
- Backend error strings other than the four I traced: errorMessage passes every Rust message through untouched, so there are likely more raw-text leaks than the one I could quote a format! for.
- Localization, RTL, and OS-level text scaling were out of scope for this lens.
- One reachability judgement is stated with a caveat rather than as fact: the Projects-index heading block at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2752-2772 appears unreachable (every setEditingStorage call site pairs with setStorageDraft), but I established that by reading a 3000-line component rather than by executing it.

findings.title: Ghost buttons render an opaque button fill: `.btn-ghost { background: transparent }` loses to the RetroTheme `.btn` rule on source order
findings.impact: Every `.btn.btn-ghost` in the app computes `background: rgb(253,248,241)` (light) / `rgb(24,21,18)` (dark) instead of transparent — verified by computed style on production markup rendered through `renderToStaticMarkup`. Because `border-color: transparent` and `box-shadow: none` DO win, a ghost paints as a borderless, shadowless opaque slab: a button with its outline deleted. It is plainly visible wherever the ghost sits on anything but plain paper — the "Reset local sync state" / "Retry" / "Open Pull review" actions inside a `.notice.danger` (ground #edd5c6) show a cream pill over the red tint, and the icon-only ghosts in the review selection bar and inline footers (`.sync-sync-review-icon-action`, `.sync-inline-action-close`) each grow a slab. 67 `btn-ghost` call sites in src/components; in the harvested production markup the affected classes include bare `btn btn-ghost` (60), `sync-sync-review-icon-action` (88), `sync-inline-action-close` (44), `conversation-path-repair-button`, `log-manage-btn`, `btn-ghost danger`. Only classes that re-declare `background: transparent` at higher specificity escape.
findings.fix: The comment added in this diff at src/App.css:344 already states the intent ("Ghosts opt back out of the box grammar: no edge, no cast shadow") and the retheme block at src/App.css:8518 already re-declares `box-shadow: none` on `.btn.btn-ghost` to beat the later `.btn`. Move `background: transparent` (and, for symmetry, `border-color: transparent`) into that same `.btn.btn-ghost` block so it carries the same (0,2,0) specificity, or add `background` to the existing 8518 rule.

findings.title: The disabled Push/Pull button fades to 1.26:1, hiding the live transfer readout while a sync runs
findings.impact: `opacity` fades ink and fill together, so `--button-primary-text` over `--button-primary-bg` collapses to 1.26:1 light (#e2d4c8 on #cfbcad) and 1.30:1 dark (#372a20 on #4b3929) — measured on the rendered `.btn.btn-primary.sync-pull-apply-button`. That button is `disabled={busy || …}` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:897, RestorePlanView.tsx:692, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1630 and :1804) and it is also where the transfer progress is printed: while a push runs it renders `{index}/{total} · {MB}…` inside itself. So the app's only in-place progress readout is unreadable for the whole duration of the operation, and the button's label ("Push"/"Pull") is unreadable whenever a review has nothing selected. The plain `.btn:disabled` case is milder but still 2.08:1 light / 2.77:1 dark.
findings.fix: Extend the existing repair at src/App.css:10545 to the review footers — add `.sync-pull-apply-button:disabled` (and ideally a general `.btn-primary:disabled`) to that selector list so the disabled primary keeps `opacity: 1` with an inert fill and a legible label. Better still, drop the `opacity` fade for `.btn:disabled` app-wide and express disabled as a token pair (inert fill + `--text-3` ink), since a fade on a translucent-over-fill button always collapses both sides.

findings.title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard at all
findings.impact: There is no key sequence that puts focus in the filter field. Tab closes the menu — both from the opener (SyncPathBar.tsx:516, :551, :618) and from inside it (:258). ArrowDown/ArrowUp from the opener call `focusMenuOption(…, "first")`, which focuses `menuOptions()[0]`, and `moveMenuFocus` cycles that same list; the `<input>` matches none of those selectors and is never focused programmatically on open. Only a mouse click reaches it. The field is rendered exactly when the switcher has ≥6 targets (SyncPathBar.tsx:174) — i.e. precisely when a keyboard user most needs to filter rather than arrow through a long list. Separately, `role="menu"` does not admit a textbox child, so a screen reader in menu-navigation mode never announces the field either; the `aria-label="Filter … list"` on it is unreachable.
findings.fix: Either focus the search input on open (and let ArrowDown step from it into the list, which the handler at SyncPathBar.tsx:263-272 already supports), or make it part of the roving order. The structural fix is to stop declaring the container `role="menu"` when `searchable` is true and use the combobox/listbox pattern instead (`role="dialog"` wrapper + `role="listbox"` of targets), since a menu that contains a textbox is not a menu.

findings.title: Light-theme notice inks fall below 4.5:1 on every tinted row; the hygiene gate only ever measures them over --surface-card
findings.impact: Because the fill is translucent, the ink's real ground is whatever is behind the notice, but tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx:78-97 composites each `*-soft` over `--surface-card` only — the one ground where light passes (danger 4.63). Measured on production markup rendered through the real components, light theme: on `--surface-row-hover` #f6e2d8 danger 4.45; on `--app-shell` #f2dfd5 danger 4.31; on `--surface-row-active` #edd5c6 danger 3.94, warning 4.16, info 4.18, success 4.21, and the `--text-2` body copy inside them 4.22-4.31. The dark palette clears 4.5 on every one of those grounds (worst 4.12, and only over `--button-bg-active`), so this is a light-only asymmetry the palette comment does not acknowledge. Reachable in production: the gate `NoticeZone` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3224) and `SiblingRepoNotice` live inside `.storage-link-block`, which paints `--surface-row-hover` on hover (src/App.css:3739) and `--surface-row-active` while an inline review is open (src/App.css:3747) — so simply moving the pointer toward the notice's own Retry button drops its error text below the floor.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) In the gate, measure each `*-soft` composite over the full opaque-surface list the third assertion already enumerates (`--bg-0…--surface-footer`), not just `--surface-card`. (2) Darken the four light `--*-text` inks by one step so they hold 4.5 down to `--surface-row-active` (#f0e3d5), which is what the palette comment at src/App.css:8181-8184 already claims — or make the `*-soft` fills opaque so the ground is fixed and testable.

findings.title: Expanding a tool call drops every ink in its summary row below 4.5:1 in the light theme
findings.impact: Opening a tool row swaps its ground from `--surface-row` (#fdf9f3) to `--surface-row-active` (#f0e3d5). Measured there in light theme at 9px: the `failed`/`incomplete` status badge `--danger-text` #be3824 = 4.41:1 (confirmed in the rendered DOM), the EDIT tool name `--session-detail-amber` #8e640f = 4.18:1, the READ tool name `--session-detail-link` #2c779c = 3.94:1. The same three in dark measure 7.08-12.63:1, so the failure is light-only. Expanding a tool call is the primary interaction on the session-detail page, and the badge that fails hardest is the one that says a call failed. The comment at src/App.css:8178-8180 asserts these variants "hold ≥4.5:1 on every paper surface down to --surface-row-active (#f0e3d5)"; they do not.
findings.fix: Either darken `--danger-text`, and the `--session-detail-amber` / `--session-detail-link` mix ratios at src/App.css:6858-6859, until they clear 4.5 on #f0e3d5, or stop using `--surface-row-active` as the open-row fill and use `--surface-row-hover` (where all three pass). Add the open-row ground to the hygiene gate so the next palette edit is measured against it.

findings.title: --control-border is dead for every text field: a blanket .sync-app rule overrides it with the weaker --button-border
findings.impact: src/App.css:7946-7950 declares the invariant — "The boundary of anything the user operates … must clear 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11). Only --border-strong does" — and exposes `--control-border: var(--border-strong)` for it. Three rules reach for that token (src/App.css:1577, :1642, :4553), and all three lose: the blanket rule above has specificity (0,3,1) against their (0,1,1). Verified by computed style — `.sync-folder-field input` resolves to `rgb(157,139,127)` = `--button-border` #9d8b7f, not `--border-strong` #66574f. Measured, `--button-border` gives 2.84:1 against `--app-shell`, 2.97:1 against `--bg-2`/`--surface-footer` and 2.59:1 against `--surface-row-active`, where `--border-strong` would give 5.6:1+ (dark: 2.29-2.94 vs `--border-strong`'s 3.0+). The practical trap is worse than the ratio: a maintainer fixing a control-boundary problem by editing `--border-strong` or `--control-border` will see no change on any text field in the app.
findings.fix: Change `border-color: var(--button-border)` at src/App.css:8582 to `var(--control-border)`, then delete the now-redundant `border: 1px solid var(--control-border)` from src/App.css:1577, :1642 and :4553 so there is one place that decides a field's edge. `--button-border` should stay for button edges only.

findings.title: Session-detail filter toggles have a 1.4:1 boundary in their off state — and this diff makes off the default for two of them
findings.impact: Measured on the rendered toolbar: the off-state toggle's border `--border` reads 1.41:1 (light, #d8cec4 on #faf3eb) and 1.35:1 (dark, #2e2925 on #0f0d0b), and its `--bg-4` fill separates from the toolbar ground by 1.08:1 light / 1.04:1 dark — so an unpressed toggle has essentially no boundary and does not read as a control (WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3:1 for the visual information that identifies a component). Only the on state gets a real edge (`--accent`, src/App.css:7013). Before this diff `toolCalls` defaulted to `sessionCountSupported(counts.tool_calls)`, so the page opened with at least one toggle visibly pressed; it now opens with both Steps and Tool calls hidden and the only way to reveal them is two controls that measure 1.4:1. A user who does not already know the SHOW row is a row of buttons will conclude the transcript has no tool calls.
findings.fix: Give the off state a boundary that clears 3:1 — swap `border: 1px solid var(--border)` for `var(--control-border)` at src/App.css:6987, which is exactly the token the file reserves for operable boundaries. Reserve `--border` for the dividers its own comment (src/App.css:7946) assigns it to.

findings.title: The switcher renders menu verbs as unlabelled icon pills, reducing destructive commands to a bare glyph
findings.impact: For any crumb menu with a header, the first unlabelled group becomes icon-only pills with the label moved to `title`/`aria-label`. In production that turns "Reset local sync state…" into a bare trash glyph (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2420-2427), "Unlink from <project>…" into a bare link-off glyph (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2284-2296 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1233-1241), and "Rename project…" into a pencil. Only verbs that carry a `detail` reach the caption line (SyncPathBar.tsx:180-183) — of the four project verbs, only "Agent profile" does. A trash glyph sitting under a project's name reads as "delete this project", not "forget local sync bases"; the sentence that distinguishes them exists only in a hover tooltip, which is unavailable to touch and slow for everyone else. These were full labelled menu rows before this diff.
findings.fix: Render verbs the way tails are rendered — icon plus label — or at minimum print the label for any item flagged `danger`. If footer width is the constraint, wrap the pills instead of dropping the words; a destructive command must never be identified by a glyph alone.

findings.title: Custom scrollbar thumb is below the 3:1 non-text floor in both themes, and the track is invisible
findings.impact: `::-webkit-scrollbar-track` is `background: transparent` (src/App.css:8419), so the 6px thumb is the only indication that a pane scrolls and where you are in it. Composited over `--bg-0` the thumb measures 2.11:1 in light (#d1c8c0 over #fefbf6) and 2.81:1 in dark; hover lifts it to 3.30 / 4.83. Every scrolling region in the app — the activity list, the review lists, the session timeline, the sidebar panes — is affected, and it is worse in the light theme, which is the OS default for most users.
findings.fix: Raise the resting mix to the value hover already uses (52% clears 3:1 in light at 3.30 and 4.83 in dark), or give the track a faint opaque fill so the thumb has a defined adjacent colour to contrast against rather than the page.

r.coverage:
METHOD. I did not eyeball the CSS: I measured it in a real engine. (1) Token parity — parsed src/App.css and diffed the three palette blocks (bare `:root` L7912, `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` L7990, `:root[data-theme="light"]` L8102). Every colour token declared in one theme is declared in the other; the only single-definition tokens are geometry (`--button-radius`, `--r`, `--r-sm`, `--r-pill`, `--retro-gutter*`, `--retro-panel-radius*`, `--retro-chevron-down`), which are correctly theme-invariant. So there is no missing-override bug — the light/dark asymmetry that exists is in the VALUES, not the coverage. (2) Dangling references — scanned every `var()` against every declaration: only `--sync-sidebar-width`, `--danger-border` and `--review-count-digits` are undeclared, all three with fallbacks, plus `--sync-startup-progress` which is set inline by StartupLoadingScreen.tsx:37. No broken token references from the retheme's deletions of `--font-pixel`, `--r-lg` and the ten `--retro-*` values. Only one hardcoded colour survives outside the palette blocks (`.sync-modal::backdrop`, theme-neutral). (3) Computed-style audit — I bundled the frontend test suite with esbuild, stubbing `node:test`/`node:assert` and wrapping `react-dom/server`, to harvest 199 fragments of REAL production markup (3.6 MB) rendered by the real components with the tests' own fixtures; plus a second probe rendering SyncPathBar (both switcher and overflow menus, open), SessionDetailEvent (prompt/reply/step/tool-call), Notice/NoticeZone and the button family. Served those over HTTP against an unmodified copy of src/App.css and walked the DOM in Chrome, resolving each text node's effective colour and its effective background by compositing every translucent fill and every `opacity` up the ancestor chain, in both `data-theme` states, with animations disabled (an early pass produced ~45 phantom failures from entrance keyframes at t=0 and from `.sync-visually-hidden` — both excluded). Ran the same walk over four grounds (`--bg-0`, `--surface-card`, `--surface-row-hover`, `--surface-row-active`, `--app-shell`) and a second pass for non-text contrast: control borders and icon-only controls at the 3:1 floor. Every ratio in the findings is a measurement, and each one was traced back to the App.css rule that produces it before being reported. (4) Read in full: the SyncPathBar/PathBarMenu diff and menuKeyboard.ts, the SessionDetailEvent/sessionDetailModel diff, the ProjectSidebar/ProjectSync/PushResourceWorkspace/ProjectLinksWorkspace diffs, Notice.tsx, preferences.ts/App.tsx/main.tsx (theme stamping), and docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md.

NOT RE-REPORTED. R1-R4 from this session stand and I built on them rather than restating: R1's inverted surface choice is the mechanism behind finding #4 (the gate measures one ground, and it is the easy one) and R2's `--danger-text` 4.405 on `--surface-row-active` is the value that lands in production in finding #5. The prior audit's H03 (muted text) and M04 (focus rings) are genuinely fixed — I re-measured `--text-2`/`--text-3` at 4.72+ light / 5.74+ dark on all 13 declared opaque surfaces, and `--focus-ring` at 12.49/12.51 worst case.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. Nothing runs under Tauri here, so states that need a live backend were reached only through fixtures: I could not exercise real hover/active/focus-visible pseudo-states in the engine, so findings #1 (ghost hover), #4 (`.storage-link-block:hover`) and #7 rest on measured resting-state values plus specificity/source-order reasoning that I confirmed empirically for the resting case. I did not evaluate layout at small window sizes beyond reading the `@container sync-pathbar` rules (the new `.sync-path-menu.switcher { width: 380px }` fits a 580px workspace at the 800px minimum, but I did not verify it against a long storage name). The `--switch-off` track (2.44 light / 2.31 dark against `--surface-card`) is below 3:1 but the switch carries a `--control-border` boundary and a thumb-position cue, so I did not report it. The ProjectSidebar divider arithmetic (`SECTION_DIVIDER_NET = 8` vs `getBoundingClientRect().height`, which includes the tray's new `padding: 8px 2px 2px 0`) overstates the elastic space by ~10px, but the `fr` rows absorb it and I could not confirm a visible consequence without a running window, so I left it out.
